which is required to commute for any
g\in G
.

Principal
G
-bundles are of great relevance for the study of general
G
-bundles.
In particular, any
G
-bundle
(E,M,\pi_{E},F)
is associated to some (unique) principal
G
-bundle
(P,M,\pi_{P},G,\lhd)
over
M
and any associated
G
-bundle can be constructed from
P
.
In the following sections we will present the frame bundle
F\mkern-1.5muM
and
G
-structures
G\mkern-1.4muM
as specific instances of principal bundles, which will make the claims made here less abstract and uncover some consequences of them.

Sections and fields:

Smooth
F
-valued fields over
M
are formalized as smooth
sections

\sigma
of a bundle
E\!\xrightarrow{\pi}\!M
with fiber
F
.
A smooth section is thereby defined as a smooth map
\sigma:M\to E
that assigns to each point
p
of the base space an element in the fiber
E_{p}
over
p
, that is, it satisfies
\pi\circ\sigma=\mathrm{id}_{M}
, which the following commutative diagram visualizes:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces M}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces E}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces M}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sigma}
\mathrm{id}_{M}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi}

(149)

An important example are tangent vector fields, which are modeled as sections
v:M\to T\mkern-1.5muM
that assign a tangent vector
v(p)\in T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
to each point
p
in
M
.
Note that the projection map is, by its nature, non-invertible, such that
\sigma\circ\pi\neq\mathrm{id}_{E}
.
The following diagram does therefore in general
not
commute:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces E}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces M}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces E}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi}
\mathrm{id}_{E}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\sigma}

\>\!\circlearrowleft\>\!

(150)

In cases below where a diagram does not commute, which is mostly the case for sections, we emphasize this visually by adding the symbol

\>\!\circlearrowleft\>\!

.
Smooth sections do not necessarily exist globally but can always be defined on trivializing neighborhoods
U\subseteq M
.
Via a local trivialization, a local section can be identified with a function
s:U\to F
by setting
s(p)=\psi_{p}(\sigma(p))
for
p\in U
.
We denote the space of global sections by
\Gamma(E)
while the space of local sections is written
\Gamma(U,E)
.

Bundle morphisms:

The morphisms (maps) in the category of fiber bundles are called
bundle morphisms
or bundle maps.
They differ from mere diffeomorphisms between the total spaces in that they are additionally required to respect the bundle structure, i.e. to
map fibers to fibers
.
In general, a smooth bundle map between two smooth fiber bundles
(E,M,\pi,F)
and
(\widetilde{E},\widetilde{M},\widetilde{\pi},\widetilde{F})
is a smooth map
\phi:E\to\widetilde{E}
between the total spaces such that there exists a second smooth map
\widehat{\phi}:M\to\widetilde{M}
between the base spaces which satisfies
\widetilde{\pi}\circ\phi=\widehat{\phi}\circ\pi
, that is, the following diagram is required to commute:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces E}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\widetilde{E}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces M}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\widetilde{M}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi\,}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\,\widetilde{\pi}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\widehat{\phi}}

(151)

The map on the base space ensures that the bundle morphism maps fibers at
p\in M
to fibers at
\widehat{\phi}(p)\in\widetilde{M}
instead of “shearing them apart”.
Obvious generalizations to bundle
isomorphisms
and bundle
automorphism
exist.
For instance, bundle isomorphisms require
\phi
and
\widetilde{\phi}
to be invertible, i.e. diffeomorphisms (and to respect further structure if defined).

The specific kind of bundle map under consideration can be narrowed down further by demanding additional requirements.
A
bundle
M
-morphism
between two bundles
(E,M,\pi,F)
and
(\widetilde{E},\widetilde{M},\widetilde{\pi},\widetilde{F})

over the same base space
M
is required to map fibers
E_{p}
over any
p\in M
to fibers
\widetilde{E}_{p}
over the same point
p
, that is,
\widehat{\phi}=\mathrm{id}_{M}
.
In terms of a commutative diagram this reads:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces E}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\widetilde{E}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces M}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi\,}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\,\widetilde{\pi}}

(152)

From this perspective, we identify the bundle trivialization in Diagram (
131
) as a bundle
U
-morphism
\Psi
between the trivial bundles
\pi^{-1}(U)
and
U\times F
over
U
.

If the fibers carry additional structure, this structure is typically required to be preserved by the bundle map.
For instance,
vector bundle morphisms

\phi
between
(E,M,\pi,\mathbb{R}^{k})
and
(\widetilde{E},M,\widetilde{\pi},\mathbb{R}^{\widetilde{k}})
are demanded to respect the vector space structure on the fibers, and therefore to restrict to
fiber wise linear maps
\phi|_{p}:E_{p}\to\widetilde{E}_{\phi(p)}
.
Similarly,
principal bundle morphisms
are required to respect the property of the fibers to be right
G
-torsors, i.e. to be right
G
-equivariant.
Given two principal bundles
(P,M,\pi,G,\lhd)
and
(\widetilde{P},\widetilde{M},\widetilde{\pi},\widetilde{G},\widetilde{\lhd})
and some group homomorphism
\theta:G\to\widetilde{G}
, a principal bundle morphism is required to make the following diagram commute for any
g\in G
:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces P}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\widetilde{P}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces P}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\widetilde{P}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces M}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\widetilde{M}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi\,}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lhd g\ }
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\,\widetilde{\pi}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\ \widetilde{\lhd}\,\theta(g)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\widehat{\phi}}

(153)

The local trivialization of principal bundles in Diagram (
148
) is thus seen as a principal bundle
U
-morphism
\Psi
between
\pi^{-1}(U)
and
U\times G
where the group homomorphism
\theta:G\to G,\ g\mapsto g
is given by the identity on
G
.

Bundle morphisms are of particular importance in Section
8
, where they describe the transformation of bundles and feature fields under the action of isometries.
Coordinate independent CNNs are proven to be equivariant w.r.t. these actions on bundles and their sections.

For more background on fiber bundles in general we refer to
[
196
,
162
,
101
,
214
,
204
,
148
,
237
]
.

6.2
The tangent bundle
TM
and frame bundle
FM

Any differentiable (and thus any Riemannian) manifold
M
is canonically equipped with its tangent bundle
T\mkern-1.5muM
and the (general) frame bundle
F\mkern-1.5muM
, consisting of all local reference frames of the tangent spaces.
The two bundles are naturally associated to each other, with their structure group a-priori given by
\Aut(\mathbb{R}^{d})=\operatorname{GL}(d)
.
This fact will be emphasized by “reconstructing”
T\mkern-1.5muM
from
F\mkern-1.5muM
via an associated bundle construction which will later allow us to define associated feature vector bundles.
To clearly separate the concepts introduced and assumptions made, we will describe
T\mkern-1.5muM
and
F\mkern-1.5muM
here as
\operatorname{GL}(d)
-bundles.
The following Section
6.3
will additionally assume a
G
-structure imposed on
T\mkern-1.5muM
and
F\mkern-1.5muM
, which will establish them as
G
-bundles.
While bundles are locally trivializable by definition, we will take the specific trivializations for now as granted and postpone their exact definition to Section
6.4
.

Tangent bundle
TM
:

Any smooth manifold
M
comes with a set of tangent spaces
T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM\cong\mathbb{R}^{d}
.
Their disjoint union
48
48

48

The disjoint union
\coprod_{p\in M}T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM=\bigcup_{p\in M}\left\{(p,v)\,|\,v\in T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM\right\}
of tangent spaces can be thought of as “remembering” from which particular tangent space
T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
a certain vector
v\in T\mkern-1.5muM
originates, which is necessary for the definition of the projection map
\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}
.

\displaystyle T\mkern-1.5muM\ :=\,\coprod_{p\in M}T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM\,,

(154)

together with a canonically given smooth structure and projection map, defines a smooth fiber bundle known as the
tangent bundle
.
The projection map
{\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}:T\mkern-1.5muM\to M}
is thereby given by the obvious choice
{\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}(v)=p}
for
v\in T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
.
As derived in Appendix
A
, local trivializations
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}}:\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}^{-1}(U)\to U\times\mathbb{R}^{d}
of the tangent bundle are canonically induced by charts
x:U\to V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d}
of the manifold.
We can therefore take the trivializability of
T\mkern-1.5muM
as granted and postpone their discussion to Section
6.4
.
A smooth structure on
T\mkern-1.5muM
is induced from the smooth structure of
M
via the above mentioned trivializations from charts.
We skip the technicalities on this construction and refer the interested reader to
[
196
,
162
]
.

The thus defined tangent bundle is a
vector bundle
since its typical fiber
\mathbb{R}^{d}
is a vector space.
Tangent vector fields, describing for instance a flow on
M
, are formalized as sections
\sigma:M\to T\mkern-1.5muM
of the tangent bundle.
Smooth global sections of vector bundles always exist; a standard example is the zero section which assigns the zero vector of
T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
to each
p\in M
.
We want to emphasize that the tangent spaces – and therefore the tangent bundle – are defined without reference to coordinate frames, such that sections describe vector fields in a coordinate free way.

After introducing the tangent frame bundle
F\mkern-1.5muM
below, we will come back to the tangent bundle and its explicit construction as associated
\operatorname{GL}(d)
-bundle which emphasizes its coordinate free nature.
In Section
6.3
we will analogously construct
T\mkern-1.5muM
as a associated
G
-bundle to a
G
-structure
G\mkern-1.4muM
.

Figure 31:
A graphical interpretation of the frame bundle
F\mkern-1.5muM
over
M
and its trivializations.
The fiber
F_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-1.0muM
over
p
is defined as the space of all possible reference frames of
T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
.
All frames in
F_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-1.0muM
are by the projection map
\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!F\!M$}}}
being mapped to that point
p
in
M
to which the fiber is attached.
The fibers
F_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-1.0muM
are isomorphic to
\operatorname{GL}(d)
, but come without an origin which would distinguish a preferred choice of reference frame.
Gauges
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}:F_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-1.0muM\to\operatorname{GL}(d)
or
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{B}:F_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-1.0muM\to\operatorname{GL}(d)
, introduced in Section
6.4
below, identify the fibers with
\operatorname{GL}(d)
, thereby specifying a preferred frame.
Different gauges are related by gauge transformations
g_{p}^{BA}\in\operatorname{GL}(d)
.
We need to warn the reader about two potential misconceptions:
Firstly, the frames in different fibers are a-priori not identified with each other in a canonical way, which the redundant colors might suggest.
Secondly, to minimize clutter, the visualization shows only right-handed, orthonormal frames instead of all possible reference frames.
As we will discuss in the following Section
6.3
, the shown orthonormal, right-handed frames would correspond to a
G
-structure
G\mkern-1.4muM
(a principal
G
-subbundle of
F\mkern-1.5muM
) for the structure group
G=\operatorname{SO}(2)
.

Frame bundle
FM
:

The space of local reference frames of all tangent spaces
T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
forms the (tangent)
frame bundle
.
Consider the spaces of reference frames (ordered bases) of the individual tangent spaces
T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
:

\displaystyle F_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-1.0muM\ :=\ \mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\Big\{$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\Big\{$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big\{$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big\{$}}}}}\big[e_{1},\dots,e_{d}\big]\,\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big|$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big|$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big|$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big|$}}}}}\ \{e_{1},\dots,e_{d}\}\ \text{is a basis of }T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM\mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\Big\}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\Big\}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big\}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big\}$}}}}}

(155)

The frame bundle is defined as their disjoint union
F\mkern-1.5muM:=\coprod_{p\in M}F_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-1.0muM
together with the projection map
\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!F\!M$}}}:F\mkern-1.5muM\to M
which sends frames in
F_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-1.0muM
to
p
and a smooth structure induced from
T\mkern-1.5muM
.
The typical fiber of the frame bundle is
the general linear group
\operatorname{GL}(d)\cong F_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-1.0muM
, i.e. the group of invertible
d\!\times\!d
matrices whose linearly independent columns can be thought of as defining a frame of
\mathbb{R}^{d}
.
As the frame bundle is constructed from the tangent bundle, its local trivializations
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!F\!M$}}:\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!F\!M$}}}^{-1}(U)\to U\times\operatorname{GL}(d)
are immediately induced from those of
T\mkern-1.5muM
; see Section
6.4
.
Fig.
31
shows a graphical interpretation of the frame bundle.

Smooth local sections
\sigma:U\to\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!F\!M$}}}^{-1}(U)\subseteq F\mkern-1.5muM
of the frame bundle map points
p\in U
to frames in
F_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-1.0muM
.
They define smooth local frame fields, that is, smoothly varying choices of reference frames for
T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM,\ p\in U
; visualized in Fig.
13
.
As argued in Eq. (
4
), a choice of frame field on
U
is
equivalent
to a choice of gauge or local trivialization on
U
.
This implies that global frame fields exist only if
F\mkern-1.5muM
– and thus
T\mkern-1.5muM
– are trivial.
We will discuss this equivalence in more depth in Section
6.4
.

A transitive and free right action on the individual fibers
F_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-1.0muM\cong\operatorname{GL}(d)
of the frame bundle is naturally given by the change of frames defined in Eq. (
3.1.1
)
[
196
]
.
The corresponding action

\displaystyle\lhd:\ F\mkern-1.5muM\times\operatorname{GL}(d)\to F\mkern-1.5muM,\quad\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d},\ g\big)\ \mapsto\ [e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\!\lhd g\ :=\ \left[\sum\nolimits_{j}e_{j}\,g_{ji}\right]_{i=1}^{d}

(156)

on
F\mkern-1.5muM
as a whole makes the frame bundle to a principal
\operatorname{GL}(d)
-bundle.
The lack of origin or preferred identity element of the fibers
F_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-1.0muM
as
\operatorname{GL}(d)
-torsors reflects the inherent ambiguity of reference frames.

TM
as GL(
d
)-associated vector bundle (
FM
\bm{\times\mathds{R}^{d})/}
GL(
d
) :

In Section
3.1.1
we expressed tangent vectors in
T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
in terms of their coefficients in
\mathbb{R}^{d}
relative to some reference frame.
The particular choice of frames was thereby irrelevant since the transformation of the coefficients in Eq. (
9
) cancels with the transformation of reference frames in Eq. (
3.1.1
) such that
v=\sum_{i}v^{A}_{i}e^{A}_{i}=\sum_{i}v^{B}_{i}e^{B}_{i}
are equivalent coordinate representations of the same coordinate free vector
v\in T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
.
Following this idea, one can construct the tangent bundle from the frame bundle by pairing reference frames with coefficient vectors and taking a quotient to collapse the resulting redundant descriptions of tangent vectors relative to different frames to one unique element.

In order to construct the tangent bundle in this way, consider the product
F\mkern-1.5muM\times\mathbb{R}^{d}
which can be seen as a fiber bundle with base space
M
and a typical fiber
\operatorname{GL}(d)\times\mathbb{R}^{d}
.
This bundle consists of pairs of (mutually unrelated) reference frames and coefficients.
Motivated by the equivalent expression of tangent vectors in different reference frames we define the
equivalence relation
49
49

49

An
equivalence relation
on a set
X
is a binary relation
\sim
which is

reflexive
(
x\!\sim\!x
),

symmetric
(
x\!\sim\!y\Leftrightarrow y\!\sim\!x
) and

transitive
(
x\!\sim\!y\wedge y\!\sim\!z\Rightarrow x\!\sim\!z
).
It defines a partitioning of
X
into
equivalence classes

[x]:=\{y\in X|x\sim y\}
of elements
x\in X
.
The space of equivalence classes
X/\!\!\sim\ :=\{[x]\,|\,x\in X\}
is called the
quotient set
of
X
by
\sim
.

\displaystyle\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d},\,{v}\big)\ \sim_{\operatorname{GL}(d)}\,\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\!\lhd g^{-1},\,g\cdot{v}\big)\qquad\forall\,g\in\operatorname{GL}(d)

(157)

on
F\mkern-1.5muM\times\mathbb{R}^{d}
.
As an equivalence relation, it partitions
F\mkern-1.5muM\times\mathbb{R}^{d}
into
equivalence classes

\big[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d},\,{v}\big]
.
The space of these equivalence classes is the quotient space
(F\mkern-1.5muM\times\mathbb{R}^{d})/\operatorname{GL}(d)
.
The projection map

\displaystyle\pi_{\scalebox{.75}{$\sim_{\operatorname{GL}(d)}$}}:\ (F\mkern-1.5muM\times\mathbb{R}^{d})/\operatorname{GL}(d)\to M,\ \ \big[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d},\,{v}\big]\mapsto\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!F\!M$}}}\!\left([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\right)\,,

(158)

which is induced from the frame bundle, makes
(F\mkern-1.5muM\times\mathbb{R}^{d})/\operatorname{GL}(d)
to a fiber bundle with base space
M
and typical fiber
\mathbb{R}^{d}
.
Note that the projection map in Eq. (
158
) is well defined as it is independent of the representative of the equivalence class, i.e.

\pi_{\scalebox{.75}{$\sim_{\operatorname{GL}(d)}$}}\left(\big[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\lhd g^{-1},\,g\cdot{v}\big]\right):=\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!F\!M$}}}\left([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\!\lhd g^{-1}\right)=\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!F\!M$}}}\left([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\right)
,
where we used that the right action
\lhd
preserves the fibers of
F\mkern-1.5muM
.
The vector space structure of
\mathbb{R}^{d}
makes
(F\mkern-1.5muM\times\mathbb{R}^{d})/\operatorname{GL}(d)
to a vector bundle with linear combinations within the same fiber being defined by

\displaystyle\alpha\big[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d},\,{v}\big]+\beta\big[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d},\,{w}\big]\ :=\ \big[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d},\,\alpha{v}+\beta{w}\big]\,,

(159)

for arbitrary
\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}
and
{v},{w}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}
.
This definition is easily checked to be independent of the choice of representative in both summands.

The thus defined bundle is isomorphic to the tangent bundle,

\displaystyle T\mkern-1.5muM\,\cong\,(F\mkern-1.5muM\times\mathbb{R}^{d})/\operatorname{GL}(d)\,,

(160)

with the vector bundle
M
-isomorphism given by the fiber wise linear map

\displaystyle\chi:(F\mkern-1.5muM\times\mathbb{R}^{d})/\operatorname{GL}(d)\ \to T\mkern-1.5muM,\ \ \ \left[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d},\,{v}\right]\mapsto\sum_{i=1}^{d}{v}_{i}e_{i}

(161)

which takes some representative tuple of frame and coefficient vector from the equivalence class and maps them to the corresponding tangent vector.
By the definition of the equivalence relation
\sim_{\operatorname{GL}(d)}
, this function is independent of the choice of representative, that is,

\forall g\in\operatorname{GL}(d):\ \chi\left(\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\lhd g^{-1},\,g\cdot{v}\big)\right)={\sum_{i}(g\!\cdot\!{v})_{i}\left([e_{j}]_{j=1}^{d}\!\lhd g^{-1}\right)_{i}}=\sum_{i}{v}_{i}e_{i}\,;\,

cf. Eq. (
3.1.1
).
As discussed in
[
196
]
, the inverse is given by taking a tangent vector, projecting it on an arbitrary frame and taking the equivalence class.

The bundle
(F\mkern-1.5muM\times\mathbb{R}^{d})/\operatorname{GL}(d)
is by construction associated to
F\mkern-1.5muM
as
\operatorname{GL}(d)
-bundle, that is, it has the same transition functions in
\operatorname{GL}(d)
as
F\mkern-1.5muM
, as we will derive in Section
6.4
.
The construction of
T\mkern-1.5muM
as quotient
(F\mkern-1.5muM\times\mathbb{R}^{d})/\operatorname{GL}(d)
emphasizes the
coordinate free
nature of the tangent bundle in a very intuitive way:
it considers all possible choices of coordinatizations of the tangent spaces and treats them as being equivalent by taking a quotient.

6.3
G
-structures
GM
and associated feature vector bundles
\bm{\mathcal{A}}

We will now introduce
G
-structures
G\mkern-1.4muM
as distinguished subsets of frames in
F\mkern-1.5muM
, which encode additional geometric structure on
M
that is to be respected by coordinate independent CNNs.
The tangent bundle is via a similar associated bundle construction to that in the last section reintroduced as an associated
G
-bundle.
This approach can be generalized to construct any other associated
G
-bundle, which we use to define the feature vector bundles
\mathcal{A}
.
All such constructed bundles are associated to each other, that is, they differ only in their fiber
F
but share the same base space
M
, structure group
G
and transition functions
g^{BA}
between trivializing neighborhoods.
The local trivializations of the bundles and their mutual gauge transformations are discussed in detail in the next Section
6.4
.

G
-structures
GM
:

As discussed in Section
3.1
and Table
1
, it is often possible to work with a
distinguished subset of reference frames
which are related by the action of a
reduced structure group

G\leq\operatorname{GL}(d)
.
This is best understood by discussing a few examples before coming to a technical definition below.
For instance, a restriction to orthonormal frames

\displaystyle\operatorname{O}_{\mkern-1.1mup}\mkern-3.4muM\ :=\ \mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\Big\{$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\Big\{$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big\{$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big\{$}}}}}\big[e_{1},\dots,e_{d}\big]\,\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big|$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big|$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big|$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big|$}}}}}\ \{e_{1},\dots,e_{d}\}\ \text{is an \emph{orthonormal} basis of }T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM\ \text{w.r.t.}\ \eta\mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\Big\}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\Big\}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big\}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big\}$}}}}}\ \cong\ \operatorname{O}(d)

(162)

gives rise to a principal subbundle
\operatorname{O}\mkern-3.6muM
of
F\mkern-1.5muM
with structure group
\operatorname{O}(d)
.
Note that the orthonormality of reference frames is judged by the metric
\eta
on
M
– different choices of metrics on a manifold therefore correspond to different subsets of preferred reference frames for the same structure group
\operatorname{O}(d)
.
As a second example, consider a choice of orientation on an orientable manifold, which allows to specify a preferred notion of frames
50
50

50

Conversely, non-orientable manifolds do not allow for a reduction of structure group to
\operatorname{GL}^{\!+}\!(d)

\displaystyle\operatorname{GL}^{\!+}_{p}\!M\ :=\ \mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\Big\{$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\Big\{$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big\{$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big\{$}}}}}\big[e_{1},\dots,e_{d}\big]\,\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big|$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big|$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big|$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big|$}}}}}\ \{e_{1},\dots,e_{d}\}\ \text{is a \emph{positively oriented} basis of }T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM\mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\Big\}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\Big\}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big\}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big\}$}}}}}\ \cong\ \operatorname{GL}^{\!+}\!(d)

(163)

and a corresponding principal subbundle
\operatorname{GL}^{\!+}\!(d)M
of

with structure group

Again, the two different choices of orientations correspond to two different choices of subbundles of accordingly oriented frames.
Combining both requirements for the orthonormality and right-handedness of frames results in an

-structure with fibers

\displaystyle\operatorname{SO}_{\mkern-1.1mup}\mkern-3.2muM\ :=\ \mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\Big\{$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\Big\{$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big\{$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big\{$}}}}}\big[e_{1},\dots,e_{d}\big]\,\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big|$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big|$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big|$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big|$}}}}}\ \{e_{1},\dots,e_{d}\}\ \text{is a \emph{positively oriented}, \emph{orthonormal} basis of }T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM\mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\Big\}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\Big\}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big\}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big\}$}}}}}\ \cong\ \operatorname{SO}(d)\,,

Fig.

Different choices of

The exact same pattern repeats for volume forms

\displaystyle\operatorname{SL}_{p}\!M\ :=\ \mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\Big\{$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\Big\{$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big\{$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big\{$}}}}}\big[e_{1},\dots,e_{d}\big]\,\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big|$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big|$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big|$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big|$}}}}}\ \{e_{1},\dots,e_{d}\}\ \text{is a basis of }\,T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM\ \text{with \emph{unit volume} w.r.t.}\ \omega\mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\Big\}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\Big\}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big\}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big\}$}}}}}\ \cong\ \operatorname{SL}(d)

and thus principal subbundles

.
The specific set of frames which are preferred depends here on the specific choice of volume form.
As a last example, consider

-structures, corresponding to a trivial structure group

By definition,

\displaystyle\raisebox{0.2pt}{$\raisebox{0.4pt}{\scalebox{.8}{$\{$}}\mkern-1.5mue\mkern-0.9mu\raisebox{0.4pt}{\scalebox{.8}{$\}$}}$}_{\mkern-1.2mup}\mkern-1.0muM\ :=\ \mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\Big\{$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\Big\{$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big\{$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big\{$}}}}}\big[e_{1},\dots,e_{d}\big]=\sigma(p)\mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\Big\}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\Big\}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big\}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big\}$}}}}}\ \cong\ \{e\}

All of these examples represent specific choices of

In general, a

is a principal

of

for any

[
215
,

,
40
]
.

51

51

As

The smoothness can hereby be formalized by requiring that around each frame

The projection

\displaystyle\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!G\!M$}}}:=\,\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!F\!M$}}}\mkern-2.0mu\big|_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\mkern-1.4muM$}}:\ \ G\mkern-1.4muM\to M

(167)

of

Together with the restriction

\displaystyle\lhd:\ G\mkern-1.4muM\times G\to G\mkern-1.4muM,\quad\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d},\ g\big)\ \mapsto\ [e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\!\lhd g\ :=\ \left[\sum\nolimits_{j}e_{j}\,g_{ji}\right]_{i=1}^{d}

(168)

of the right action of

on

in Eq. (

on

, this makes the

However, it is important to note that there are

As discussed earlier, the topology of a bundle might obstruct the reduction to a structure group

While the above definition of
G
-structures would be sufficient, it is instructive to briefly review some alternative, equivalent definitions.
The claim that
G\mkern-1.4muM
is a principal
G
-
subbundle
of
F\mkern-1.5muM
is made precise by defining it as a tuple
(P,{E})
consisting of a choice of an (also non-unique) principal
G
-bundle
P
over
M
together with a smooth, right
G
-equivariant embedding
{E}:P\to F\mkern-1.5muM
(over
M
).
52
52

52

The embedding is a principal
G
-bundle
M
-morphism as introduced in Section
6.1
with the group homomorphism
\theta:G\to\operatorname{GL}(d)
being the canonical inclusion of the subgroup
G\leq\operatorname{GL}(d)
into
\operatorname{GL}(d)
.

This is visualized by the following diagram, which is required to commute for any
g\in G
:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces P}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F\mkern-1.5muM}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces P}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F\mkern-1.5muM}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces M}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{E}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{E}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lhd_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0muP}}\mkern 2.0mug\>}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi_{P}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\>\lhd\mkern 2.0mug}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!F\!M$}}}}

(169)

Different subsets of preferred frames correspond in this viewpoint to different choices of embeddings
{G\mkern-1.4muM={E}(P)}
of
P
in
F\mkern-1.5muM
.

G
-structures are furthermore equivalent to sections of the form
s:M\mapsto F\mkern-1.5muM/G
with
G\mkern-1.4muM=s(M)
, which emphasizes that
G_{\mkern-1.3mup}\mkern-1.2muM=s(p)\in F_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-1.0muM/G
is indeed a choice of
G
-orbit in
F_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-1.0muM
as stated in footnote
51
.
Yet another definition of
G
-structures is in terms of (equivalence classes of)
G
-atlases
[
237
]
.
As this is the viewpoint which might be taken in an implementation of
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions, we discuss it in more detail in the following Section
6.4
.
For the interested reader we want to mention that
G
-structures are a specific case of the more general concept of a
reduction (or lift) of structure groups

[
215
,
171
,
40
]
.

G
-structures are of pivotal importance for the theory of
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions.
The particular choice of
G
-structure determines the specific set of reference frames over which the
G
-steerable template kernel is shared.
By the gauge equivariance of the kernels,
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions are guaranteed to respect the
G
-structure, i.e. to be
G\mkern-1.4muM
-
coordinate independent
.
As derived in Section
8
, the isometries with respect to which a
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolution is equivariant are exactly those which preserve the
G
-structure (i.e. those which induce automorphisms of
G\mkern-1.4muM
).

TM
as
G
-associated vector bundle (
GM
\bm{\times\mathds{R}^{d})/}
G
:

Given a
G
-structure
G\mkern-1.4muM
, one can adapt the associated
\operatorname{GL}(d)
-bundle construction of
T\mkern-1.5muM
from
F\mkern-1.5muM
in Section
6.2
to a similar associated
G
-bundle construction of
T\mkern-1.5muM
based on
G\mkern-1.4muM
.
Instead of expressing tangent vectors relative to general frames in
F\mkern-1.5muM
, they will thereby be expressed relative to the distinguished frames in
G\mkern-1.4muM
and the quotient is taken w.r.t. the reduced structure group
G
instead of
\operatorname{GL}(d)
.
The resulting bundle is by design associated to
G\mkern-1.4muM
(or to
F\mkern-1.5muM
with a
G
-atlas, which is equivalent as explained in the next section) and therefore has transition functions which take values in
G
.
The restriction of
\chi
in Eq. (
161
) to
(G\mkern-1.4muM\times\mathbb{R}^{d})/G
yields a vector bundle isomorphism

\displaystyle T\mkern-1.5muM\,\cong\,(G\mkern-1.4muM\times\mathbb{R}^{d})/G\,.

(170)

While all three bundles
T\mkern-1.5muM
,
(F\mkern-1.5muM\times\mathbb{R}^{d})/\operatorname{GL}(d)
and
(G\mkern-1.4muM\times\mathbb{R}^{d})/G
are thus isomorphic
as vector bundles
, they are only isomorphic as associated
G
-bundles if
T\mkern-1.5muM
and
(F\mkern-1.5muM\times\mathbb{R}^{d})/\operatorname{GL}(d)
are endowed with a
G
-structure (or
G
-atlas), which is a-priori not the case.
In contrast, the bundle
(G\mkern-1.4muM\times\mathbb{R}^{d})/G
comes with a
G
-structure by design.
For a precise definition of associated
G
-bundle isomorphisms we refer to
[
196
]
.

Associated feature vector bundles
\bm{\mathcal{A}}
:

The associated
G
-bundle construction
(G\mkern-1.4muM\times\mathbb{R}^{d})/G
can be generalized to attach other fibers with other group actions to the
G
-structure
G\mkern-1.4muM
.
Indeed,
any
bundle associated to
G\mkern-1.4muM
can be constructed in this way.
Important examples in differential geometry are the cotangent bundle
T^{\mkern 0.5mu*}\mkern-3.5muM
with its typical fiber being the dual
\mathbb{R}^{d*}
of
\mathbb{R}^{d}
, acted on by the dual action, or the
(r,s)
tensor bundles
T^{r}_{s}\!M
with fibers
\big(\mathbb{R}^{d}\big)^{\otimes r}\!\otimes\!\big(\mathbb{R}^{d*}\big)^{\otimes s}
being acted on by the corresponding tensor product representation of
G
.

In the following we consider
associated feature vector bundles
with feature vector coefficients
\mathbb{R}^{c}
as typical fibers.
Under gauge transformations, these fibers are acted on from the left by a multiplication with a group representation
\rho:G\to\operatorname{GL}(c)
, that is, Eq. (
136
) is instantiated by
\blacktriangleright_{\rho}:\ {G\times\mathbb{R}^{c}\to\mathbb{R}^{c},}\ \ {(g,{f})\mapsto\rho(g){f}}
.
Similar to before, feature vector bundles are then constructed as a quotient

\displaystyle\mathcal{A}\ :=\ (G\mkern-1.4muM\times\mathbb{R}^{c})/\!\sim_{\!\rho}

(171)

with the equivalence relation
\sim_{\!\rho}
here given by

\displaystyle\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d},\,{f}\mkern 1.0mu\big)\ \sim_{\!\rho}\ \big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\!\lhd g^{-1},\ \rho(g){f}\mkern 1.0mu\big)\qquad\forall g\in G.

(172)

The elements of
\mathcal{A}
are the equivalence classes
\big[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d},\ {f}\big]
of feature vector coefficients relative to reference frames and are therefore
coordinate free
.
A (well defined) projection map is again induced from the projection of the
G
-structure:

\displaystyle\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!\!\mathcal{A}$}}}:\mathcal{A}\to M,\ \ \big[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d},\,{f}\big]\mapsto\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!G\!M$}}}\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\big)

(173)

Linear combinations on the fibers are defined in analogy to Eq. (
159
).
Since such defined feature vector bundles are associated to
G\mkern-1.4muM
, their structure group is
G\leq\operatorname{GL}(d)
, as we will explicitly derive in the next Section
6.4
.
53
53

53

Strictly speaking, the transition functions will take values in
\rho(G)\leq\operatorname{GL}(c)
instead of
G\leq\operatorname{GL}(d)
, however, since the resulting transitions are still
G
-compatible
, the term “
G
-valued” is usually adapted to include such cases
[
237
]
.

Note that this definition includes tangent vector fields and scalar fields, which can of course be processed as feature fields, for
\rho(g)=g
and
\rho(g)=1
, respectively.

The construction of
\mathcal{A}
as an associated
G
-bundle models
G\mkern-1.4muM
-coordinate independent feature vectors on
M
:
features
f_{p}\in\mathcal{A}
are equivalently expressed relative to arbitrary frames in
G\mkern-1.4muM
, with feature coefficients in different coordinatizations being related via Eq. (
172
), but do not have a well defined coordinate expression relative to other frames.
From an engineering viewpoint, this is reflected in the
G
-steerability of convolution kernels which ensures that measurements of features are performed
relative
to frames in
G\mkern-1.4muM
but allows to discriminate between patterns whose poses are not related by a
G
-valued gauge transformation in an
absolute
sense.

Associated feature vector field and feature spaces:

Smooth, coordinate free feature fields are defined as smooth global sections
f\in\Gamma(\mathcal{A})
of the feature vector bundles, that is, as smooth maps
f:M\to\mathcal{A}
satisfying
\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!\!\mathcal{A}$}}}\circ f=\mathrm{id}_{M}
.
As discussed before, such feature fields are guaranteed to exist since vector bundles always admit smooth global sections.
In the following Section
6.4
we show how a local bundle trivialization over
U^{A}
allows to represent
f
by a field
f^{A}:U^{A}\to\mathbb{R}^{c}
of feature vector coefficients.
A different trivialization over
U^{B}
will lead to a different coefficient field
f^{B}:U^{B}\to\mathbb{R}^{c}
representing
f
locally.
From the transition maps between bundle trivializations it will follow that both coefficient fields are on the overlap
U^{AB}=U^{A}\cap U^{B}
of their domains related by
f^{B}(p)=\rho\big(g_{p}^{BA}\big)f^{A}(p)
.
The commutative diagram in Fig.
34
visualizes the relations between feature vector fields and their local trivializations.

The feature spaces of coordinate independent CNNs usually consist of multiple independent feature fields over the same base space.
The bundle describing a feature space as a whole is the
Whitney sum

\bigoplus_{i}\mathcal{A}_{i}
of the feature vector bundles
\mathcal{A}_{i}\xrightarrow{\scalebox{.85}{$\pi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A}_{i}$}}$}}M
underlying its individual fields.
As such it has the same base space
M
, a typical fiber
\bigoplus_{i}\mathbb{R}^{c_{i}}\cong\mathbb{R}^{\sum_{i}\!c_{i}}
defined as direct sum of the individual fields’ fibers and is equipped with the obvious projection map.
It is associated to
T\mkern-1.5muM
,
F\mkern-1.5muM
,
G\mkern-1.4muM
and the
\mathcal{A}_{i}
as
G
-bundles and can therefore equivalently be defined as

\displaystyle\scalebox{1.1}{$\bigoplus$}_{i}\,\mathcal{A}_{i}\ \ \cong\,\ \left(G\mkern-1.4muM\times\mathbb{R}^{\sum_{i}\!c_{i}}\right)\!\!\Big/\!\!\sim_{\oplus_{i}\rho_{i}}

(174)

Note that the direct sum
\bigoplus_{i}\rho_{i}
of representations
\rho_{i}
defining
\mathcal{A}_{i}
guarantees that the transition maps of
\bigoplus_{i}\mathcal{A}_{i}
transform each individual field independently.
The feature spaces are then defined as the spaces
\Gamma\!\left(\bigoplus_{i}\mathcal{A}_{i}\right)
of global sections of the Whitney sum bundle.

6.4
Local bundle trivializations of
TM
,
FM
,
GM
and
\bm{\mathcal{A}}

While the global theory of coordinate independent CNNs is elegantly formalized in terms of coordinate free fiber bundles, a numerical implementation requires coordinate free feature vectors
f(p)\in\mathcal{A}_{p}
to be expressed by coefficient vectors
{f^{A}(p):=\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big(f(p)\big)\in\mathbb{R}^{c}}
relative to some choice of reference frame
\big[e_{i}^{A}\big]_{i=1}^{d}\in G_{\mkern-1.3mup}\mkern-1.2muM
as described in Section
3.2
.
In the language of fiber bundles, this corresponds to a choice of local trivializations or gauges
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!G\!M$}}^{A}
,
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}}^{A}
,
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!F\!M$}}^{A}
and
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A}$}}^{A}
, all of which transform simultaneously if
G\mkern-1.4muM
,
T\mkern-1.5muM
,
F\mkern-1.5muM
and
\mathcal{A}
are taken to be
G
-associated to each other.
Recall that a local description and thus implementation via a
G
-atlas, consisting of local trivializations which cover
M
and satisfy the three conditions (
138
), (
139
) and (
140
), is fully equivalent to the global, coordinate free theory.

In this section we work out the associated trivializations of
T\mkern-1.5muM
,
F\mkern-1.5muM
,
G\mkern-1.4muM
and
\mathcal{A}
and their synchronous gauge transformations.
To stay consistent with Section
3.1
, we start out by assuming trivializations of
T\mkern-1.5muM
to be given and discuss how they induce trivializations of
F\mkern-1.5muM
and corresponding local frame fields.
If a
G
-atlas is chosen for
T\mkern-1.5muM
and thus
F\mkern-1.5muM
, it gives rise to a
G
-structure
G\mkern-1.4muM
whose
G
-atlas agrees with that of
F\mkern-1.5muM
.
The local trivializations of any associated
G
-bundle, in particular those of the feature vector bundles
\mathcal{A}
, follow from those of
G\mkern-1.4muM
.
These trivializations recover the transformation law of feature fields from Section
3.2
.

Trivializations of
TM
:

As the tangent bundle has
\mathbb{R}^{d}
as typical fiber, its local trivializations are given by maps of the form

\displaystyle{\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}}:\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}^{-1}\!\left(U\right)\to U\times\mathbb{R}^{d}}.

(175)

These trivializations correspond to the (spatially smoothly varying) pointwise gauges

\displaystyle\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}:T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM\to\mathbb{R}^{d}

(176)

from Eq. (
1
) by identifying
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}}(v)=\left(\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}(v),\,\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}(v)\right)
for
p=\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}(v)
.
In order to respect the vector space structures of the fiber
\mathbb{R}^{d}
and the tangent spaces
T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
, the trivializations
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}}
are defined as
vector bundle isomorphisms
between
\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}^{-1}(U)
and
U\times\mathbb{R}^{d}
, that is, the maps
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}
are required to be linear and invertible (i.e. vector space isomorphisms).
The transition maps between different trivializations of
T\mkern-1.5muM
will in general take values in the general linear group
\operatorname{GL}(d)
, the (linear) automorphism group of
\mathbb{R}^{d}
.

If further structure is specified on the tangent bundle, the trivializations are required to respect this structure.
For instance, if a metric is defined on
M
and thus
T\mkern-1.5muM
, the maps
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}
are required to be isometric, i.e. to map vectors in
T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
in such a way to vectors in
\mathbb{R}^{d}
that norms and angles are preserved.
As the trivializations are then only allowed to differ in their direction and orientation, different trivializations are guaranteed to be related by a reduced structure group
\operatorname{O}(d)
, corresponding to the metric as
\operatorname{O}(d)
-structure.
More generally, a
G
-structure on
T\mkern-1.5muM
requires – or is implied by – a choice of
G
-atlas
\big\{\big(U^{X},\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}}^{X}\big)\big\}_{\!X\in\mathfrak{X}}\,
.
Two different trivializations
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}}^{A}
and
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}}^{B}
of such a
G
-atlas are on
U^{A}\cap U^{B}
related by
{\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}}^{B}\circ\big(\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}}^{A}\big)^{-1}}
as defined in Eq. (
134
) with
G
-valued transition functions

\displaystyle g^{BA}:U^{A}\mkern-1.0mu\cap\mkern-1.0muU^{B}\to G,\ \ \ p\mapsto\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{B}\circ\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big)^{-1}\,,

(177)

which define the left action
\scalebox{.8}{$\blacktriangleright$}:G\times\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}^{d},\ \ (g,{v})\mapsto g\cdot{v}
on the typical fiber.
For a graphical intuition on the pointwise action of the transition functions on individual fibers we refer back to Fig.
12
.
A diagrammatic visualization of local trivializations of
T\mkern-1.5muM
and their transitions is given in Fig.
32(a)
.

Induced trivializations of
FM
and frame fields:

Any atlas

\big\{\big(U^{X},\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}}^{X}\big)\big\}_{\!X\in\mathfrak{X}}\,

of the tangent bundle is in one-to-one correspondence to an atlas

\big\{\big(U^{X},\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!F\!M$}}^{X}\big)\big\}_{\!X\in\mathfrak{X}}\,

of the frame bundle.
Specifically, given a local trivialization
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}}^{A}
of
T\mkern-1.5muM
, a corresponding local trivialization

\displaystyle\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!F\!M$}}^{A}:\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!F\!M$}}}^{-1}\big(U^{A}\big)\to U^{A}\times\operatorname{GL}(d),\quad[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\mapsto\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big($}}}}}p,\ \psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\big)\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}\,,

(178)

of
F\mkern-1.5muM
, where we abbreviated
p=\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!F\!M$}}}\left([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\right)
, is induced by defining

\displaystyle\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}:F_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-1.0muM\to\operatorname{GL}(d),\quad[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\mapsto\,\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\big):=\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}(e_{i})\big)_{i=1}^{d}

(179)

as a map from tangent frames to invertible
d\!\times\!d
matrices whose
i
-
th
column is given by
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}(e_{i})\in\mathbb{R}^{d}
.
As required for associated bundles, the trivializations of
T\mkern-1.5muM
and
F\mkern-1.5muM
share the
same transition functions
,

\displaystyle\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{B}\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\big)\

\displaystyle=\ \big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{B}(e_{i})\big)_{i=1}^{d}

\displaystyle=\ \big(g_{p}^{BA}\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}(e_{i})\big)_{i=1}^{d}

\displaystyle=\ g_{p}^{BA}\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}(e_{i})\big)_{i=1}^{d}

\displaystyle=\ g_{p}^{BA}\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\big)\ ,

(180)

since the action of
g^{BA}
on the individual trivialized frame axes in the second line agrees with its action on the trivialized frame matrix in the third line.
Furthermore, as claimed for principal bundles in Eq. (
147
), the trivializations of the frame bundle are
right
\operatorname{GL}(d)
-equivariant
, that is, for any
h\in\operatorname{GL}(d)
one has:

\displaystyle\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\lhd h\big)\

\displaystyle=\ \psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\left(\left(\sum\nolimits_{j}e_{j}\,h_{ji}\right)_{i=1}^{d}\right)

\displaystyle=\ \left(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\left(\sum\nolimits_{j}e_{j}\,h_{ji}\right)\right)_{i=1}^{d}

\displaystyle=\ \left(\sum\nolimits_{j}\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\left(e_{j}\right)h_{ji}\right)_{i=1}^{d}

\displaystyle=\ \left(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\left(e_{i}\right)\right)_{i=1}^{d}\cdot h

\displaystyle=\ \psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\big)\cdot h

(181)

Here we used the linearity of
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}
in the third step and identified the index expression as a right matrix multiplication in the fourth step.

summarizes the left action on the trivialization via transition functions

as derived in Eq. (
6.4
) and the right equivariance
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!F\!M$}}^{A}\circ(\lhd\,h)=(\mathrm{id}\times\cdot h)\circ\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!F\!M$}}^{A}
of the trivializations as derived in Eq. (
6.4
).

If identity sections

and

.

Figure 33:
Extended diagrams of the frame bundle trivializations which capture the interplay of the transition functions
g^{BA}\cdot
, the right actions
\lhd\,h
and
\,\cdot\,h
and the identity sections
\sigma^{A}
and
\sigma^{B}
.
As before, we abbreviate
U=U^{AB}=U^{A}\cap U^{B}
.
Except for
\sigma^{A}\circ\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!F\!M$}}}\neq\mathrm{id}_{F\mkern-1.5muM}
and
\sigma^{B}\circ\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!F\!M$}}}\neq\mathrm{id}_{F\mkern-1.5muM}
, the diagrams commute.
If the trivializations are part of some
G
-atlas, similar diagrams, with
F\mkern-1.5muM
and
\operatorname{GL}(d)
being replaced by
G\mkern-1.4muM
and
G
, apply to the corresponding
G
-structure.

As indicated in Eq. (
4
) and visualized in Figs.
12
and
13
, a smooth local trivialization
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}}^{A}
on
U^{A}
of the tangent bundle induces a
frame field
on
U^{A}
.
It is formalized as a smooth
local section

\displaystyle\sigma^{A}:U^{A}\to\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!F\!M$}}}^{-1}\!\left(U^{A}\right),\ \ p\mapsto\left[\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big)^{-1}(\epsilon_{i})\right]_{i=1}^{d}

(182)

of the frame bundle, defined by mapping the standard frame vectors
\epsilon_{i}
of
\mathbb{R}^{d}
back to the tangent spaces in
\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}^{-1}\big(U^{A}\big)\subseteq T\mkern-1.5muM
.
Following Eq.
3.1.1
, a gauge transformation from
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}}^{A}
to
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}}^{B}=(\mathrm{id}\times g^{BA}\cdot)\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}}^{A}
corresponds to a transformation

\displaystyle\sigma^{B}(p)\ =\ \sigma^{A}(p)\lhd\left(g^{BA}_{p}\right)^{-1}

(183)

of sections on
U^{AB}
.
Being defined in terms of
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}}^{A},
the trivializations
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!F\!M$}}^{A}
of
F\mkern-1.5muM
have the nice property that they map the corresponding sections
\sigma^{A}
to the identity frame
e\in\operatorname{GL}(d)\subset\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}
of
\mathbb{R}^{d}
, which can be seen by inserting both definitions:

\displaystyle\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\circ\sigma^{A}(p)\ =\ \psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\Big(\Big[\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big)^{-1}(\epsilon_{i})\Big]_{i=1}^{d}\Big)\ =\ \Big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\circ\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big)^{-1}(\epsilon_{i})\Big)_{i=1}^{d}\ =\ (\epsilon_{i})_{i=1}^{d}\ =\ e

(184)

This property is often used to define sections of
F\mkern-1.5muM
given trivializations
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!F\!M$}}^{A}
as

\displaystyle\sigma^{A}\!:U^{A}\to\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!F\!M$}}}^{-1}\big(U^{A}\big),\ \ \ p\mapsto\big(\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!F\!M$}}^{A}\big)^{-1}(p,e)=\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big)^{-1}(e)\,,

(185)

which ultimately coincides with our definition in Eq. (
182
).
Since
\sigma^{A}
and
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!F\!M$}}^{A}
constructed this way imply each other they are sometimes called
identity sections
and
canonical local trivializations
.
Extending the diagram in Fig.
33(a)
with identity sections
\sigma^{A}
and
\sigma^{B}
, related by Eq.
183
, fixes
h=g^{BA}
and thus leads to the commutative diagram in Fig.
33(b)
.
The left and right multiplications with
g^{BA}
on the typical fiber
\operatorname{GL}(d)
coincide hereby only since
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\circ\sigma^{A}=\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{B}\circ\sigma^{B}=e
for which
g^{BA}\cdot e=g^{BA}=e\cdot g^{BA}
.
Compare Fig.
33(b)
to Fig.
31
, which shows the left gauge action
g_{p}^{BA}\cdot
on
\operatorname{GL}(d)
and the right action
\lhd\big(g_{p}^{BA}\big)^{-1}
of the inverse group element which transforms between the corresponding identity section frames.

G
-atlas induced
G
-structure
GM
:

The agreement of the transition functions of the tangent bundle and the frame bundle in Eq. (
6.4
) implies that a
G
-atlas of
T\mkern-1.5muM
induces a
G
-atlas for
F\mkern-1.5muM
.
As we will derive in the following, such
G
-atlases fix a corresponding
G
-structure
G\mkern-1.4muM
, i.e. a principal
G
-subbundle of
F\mkern-1.5muM
, consisting of preferred frames.

To motivate the definition of
G\mkern-1.4muM
in terms of a given
G
-atlas
\big\{\big(U^{X},\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!F\!M$}}^{X}\big)\big\}_{\!X\in\mathfrak{X}}\,
of
F\mkern-1.5muM
, consider two of its local trivializations
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!F\!M$}}^{A}
and
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!F\!M$}}^{B}
with overlapping domains and let
p\in U^{A}\cap U^{B}
.
The trivializations define reference frames
\sigma^{A}(p)
and
\sigma^{B}(p)
in
F_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-1.0muM
, which are according to Eq. (
183
) related by the right action of some element
g_{p}^{BA}
of the reduced structure group
G\leq\operatorname{GL}(d)
.
Any such defined frame is therefore seen to be an element of a
G
-orbit
G_{\mkern-1.3mup}\mkern-1.2muM\cong G
in
F_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-1.0muM\cong\operatorname{GL}(d)
.
Specifically, expressing the identity sections via Eq. (
185
) as
\sigma^{A}(p)=\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big)^{-1}(e)
and

\sigma^{B}(p)=\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{B}\big)^{-1}(e)=\big(g_{p}^{BA}\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big)^{-1}(e)=\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big)^{-1}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big($}}}}}\big(g_{p}^{BA}\big)^{-1}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}

suggests the pointwise definition of the
G
-structure in terms of inverse images of
G
by (arbitrary) gauge maps:

\displaystyle G_{\mkern-1.3mup}\mkern-1.2muM\ :=\ \mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\Big\{$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\Big\{$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big\{$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big\{$}}}}}\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big)^{-1}(g)\;\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big|$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big|$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big|$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big|$}}}}}\;g\in G\,\mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\Big\}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\Big\}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big\}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big\}$}}}}}\ =\ \big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big)^{-1}(G)

(186)

The independence from the chosen gauge of the
G
-atlas is clear as any other choice

\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{B}\big)^{-1}(G)=\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big)^{-1}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big($}}}}}\big(g_{p}^{BA}\big)^{-1}G\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}=\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big)^{-1}(G)

would yield the same result.
As one can easily check,
G_{\mkern-1.3mup}\mkern-1.2muM
is indeed a right
G
-torsor since
G
is a right
G
-torsor and
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}
is by Eq. (
6.4
) a right
\operatorname{GL}(d)
-equivariant – and thus in particular right
G
-equivariant – isomorphism.
The required smoothness of
G\mkern-1.4muM=\coprod_{p\in M}G_{\mkern-1.3mup}\mkern-1.2muM
follows from the smoothness of the trivializations
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!F\!M$}}^{A}
.

A
G
-atlas of local trivializations of
G\mkern-1.4muM
is given by restricting the trivializations in the
G
-atlas of
F\mkern-1.5muM
to frames in
G\mkern-1.4muM
, that is,

\displaystyle\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!G\!M$}}^{A}:=\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!F\!M$}}^{A}\big|_{\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!G\!M$}}}^{-1}(U^{A})}:\ \ \pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!G\!M$}}}^{-1}\big(U^{A}\big)\to U^{A}\times G\,,

(187)

or, locally,

\displaystyle\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}:=\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big|_{G_{\mkern-1.3mup}\mkern-1.2muM}:\ \ G_{\mkern-1.3mup}\mkern-1.2muM\to G\,.

(188)

It follows immediately that the
G
-valued transition functions agree with those of
T\mkern-1.5muM
and
F\mkern-1.5muM
, that is,

\displaystyle\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{B}\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\big)\ =\ g_{p}^{BA}\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\big)\,,

(189)

and that the trivializations are right
G
-equivariant:

\displaystyle\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\lhd h\big)\ =\ \psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\big)\cdot h\qquad\forall h\in G

(190)

The frame fields are also given by an equivalent expression

\displaystyle\sigma^{A}(p)\ =\ \big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big)^{-1}(e)

(191)

to that in Eq. (
185
).
The commutative diagrams in Figs.
33(a)
and
33(b)
hold as well when replacing
F\mkern-1.5muM
with
G\mkern-1.4muM
and
\operatorname{GL}(d)
with
G
.

Induced trivializations of associated bundles
\mathcal{A}
:

A
G
-atlas

\big\{\big(U^{X},\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A}$}}^{X}\big)\big\}_{\!X\in\mathfrak{X}}\,
,
consisting of local trivializations

\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A}$}}^{X}:\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!\!\mathcal{A}$}}}^{-1}\big(U^{X}\big)\to U^{X}\times\mathbb{R}^{c}

of the associated feature vector bundles

\mathcal{A}=(G\mkern-1.4muM\times\mathbb{R}^{c})/\!\sim_{\!\rho}

is induced from the corresponding trivializations
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!G\!M$}}^{X}
of the
G
-structure.
In order to construct these trivializations, recall that
\mathcal{A}
is defined in terms of equivalence classes

\big[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d},\ {f}\,\big]

consisting of pairs of reference frames and feature coefficient vectors which are related by the equivalence relation
\sim_{\!\rho}
defined in Eq. (
172
).
A natural idea is thus to trivialize

\big[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d},\ {f}\,\big]\in\mathcal{A}_{p}

by picking one representative of its equivalent coefficient vectors in
\mathbb{R}^{c}
.
A preferred choice of representative is hereby given by that coefficient vector belonging to the identity section frame
\sigma^{A}(p)
corresponding to
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!G\!M$}}^{A}
.

Let
[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}:=\sigma^{A}(p)\lhd h\ \in G_{\mkern-1.3mup}\mkern-1.2muM
be some frame that is defined by an offset
h\in G
relative to section
\sigma^{A}
.
This offset can be recovered by the trivialization of the
G
-structure:

\displaystyle\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\!\left([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\right)\ =\ \psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\!\left(\sigma^{A}(p)\lhd h\right)\ =\ \psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\!\left(\sigma^{A}(p)\right)\cdot h\ =\ h

(192)

Here we used the right
G
-equivariance of
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}
and that
\sigma^{A}
is defined as identity section; see Eqs. (
190
) and (
184
), the latter adapted to
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}
.
We can therefore rewrite any frame via its offset as:

\displaystyle[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\ =\ \sigma^{A}(p)\lhd\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\!\left([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\right)

(193)

Similarly, we can rewrite any feature vector
\big[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d},\ {f}\,\big]\in\mathcal{A}_{p}
by different representatives of the equivalence class:

\displaystyle\left[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d},\ {f}\,\right]\ =\ \left[\sigma^{A}(p)\lhd\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\big),\,\ {f}\,\right]\ =\ \left[\sigma^{A}(p),\ \rho\left(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\big)\right){f}\,\right]

(194)

Based on these insights we define induced trivializations of
\mathcal{A}
by setting

\displaystyle\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A}$}}^{A}:\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!\!\mathcal{A}$}}}^{-1}\big(U^{A}\big)\to U^{A}\times\mathbb{R}^{c},\quad\big[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d},\ {f}\,\big]\ \mapsto\ \Big(\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!G\!M$}}}\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\big),\ \psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big($}}}}}\big[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d},\ {f}\,\big]\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}\Big)\ ,

(195)

with

\displaystyle\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}:\mathcal{A}_{p}\to\mathbb{R}^{c},\quad\big[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d},\ {f}\,\big]\,=\,\Big[\sigma^{A}(p),\ \rho\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big($}}}}}\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\big)\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}{f}\,\Big]\ \mapsto\ \rho\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big($}}}}}\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\big)\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}\,{f}\,,

(196)

which picks that particular representative coefficient vector

f^{A}=\rho\left(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\left([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\right)\right){f}\in\mathbb{R}^{c}

that is distinguished by the reference frame
\sigma^{A}(p)
corresponding to the chosen gauge.
For later convenience we note that this implies in particular that the inverse of Eq. (
196
) is given by

\displaystyle\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big)^{-1}\!:\mathbb{R}^{c}\to\mathcal{A}_{p}:\ \ {f}\,\mapsto\big[\sigma^{A}(p),\;{f}\,\big]\ .

(197)

The such defined trivialization is independent of the chosen representative since for any
k\in G
we have:

\displaystyle\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big($}}}}}\big[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\!\lhd k^{-1},\,\ \rho(k){f}\,\big]\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}\

\displaystyle=\ \rho\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\!\lhd k^{-1}\big)\big)\rho(k){f}

\displaystyle=\ \rho\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\big)\cdot k^{-1}\big)\rho(k){f}

\displaystyle=\ \rho\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\big)\big){f}

\displaystyle=\ \psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big($}}}}}\big[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d},\,\ {f}\,\big]\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}

(198)

By construction, the transition functions are given by
\rho\big(g_{p}^{BA}\big)
:

\displaystyle\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{B}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big($}}}}}\big[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d},\,\ {f}\,\big]\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}\

\displaystyle=\ \rho\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{B}\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\big)\big){f}

\displaystyle=\ \rho\big(g_{p}^{BA}\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\big)\big){f}

\displaystyle=\ \rho\big(g_{p}^{BA}\big)\rho\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\big)\big){f}

\displaystyle=\ \rho\big(g_{p}^{BA}\big)\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big(\big[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d},\,\ {f}\,\big]\big)

(199)

If the tangent bundle is taken as a
G
-associated vector bundle
T\mkern-1.5muM\cong(G\mkern-1.4muM\times\mathbb{R}^{d})/G
, its trivializations are recovered from Eq. (
195
) for the specific choice
\rho(g)=g
.
