Figure 34:
Coordinate free feature fields are defined as global sections
f\in\Gamma(\mathcal{A})
.
On local neighborhoods
U^{A}
and
U^{B}
they trivialize to fields of feature coefficient vectors
f^{A}:U^{A}\mapsto\mathbb{R}^{c}
and
f^{B}:U^{B}\mapsto\mathbb{R}^{c}
which are on
U=U^{A}\cap U^{B}
related by
f^{B}(p)=\rho\big(g_{p}^{BA}\big)f^{A}(p)
.
Except for
f\circ\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!\!\mathcal{A}$}}}\neq\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal{A}}
, the diagram commutes.

Assume a coordinate free feature field
f\in\Gamma(\mathcal{A})
to be given.
Relative to gauge
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A}$}}^{A}
, it can be locally represented as a coefficient vector field
f^{A}:U^{A}\to\mathbb{R}^{c}
by defining

\displaystyle f^{A}\ :=\ \operatorname{proj}_{2}\circ\mkern 2.0mu\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A}$}}^{A}\circ f

(200)

which is equivalent to the pointwise definition

\displaystyle f^{A}(p)\ =\ \psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\circ f(p)\,.

(201)

As apparent from the commutative diagram in Fig.
34
, the transition functions in Eq. (
6.4
) carry over to the local coefficient fields such that we get

\displaystyle f^{B}(p)\ =\ \rho\left(g_{p}^{BA}\right)f^{A}(p)

(202)

for
p\in U^{A}\cap U^{B}
.
This agrees with and justifies our definition of the gauge transformations of feature coefficient vectors in Eq. (
28
).

Summarizing remarks:

The here defined local trivializations and transition functions formalize and justify the definitions of gauges and gauge transformations from Section
3.2
.
Local trivializations of
T\mkern-1.5muM
and
F\mkern-1.5muM
were shown to induce each other.
If a
G
-atlas is chosen for either of both, it defines a
G
-structure
G\mkern-1.4muM
, whose
G
-atlas essentially coincides with that of
F\mkern-1.5muM
.
It furthermore induces a
G
-atlas for any other associated bundle, including
\mathcal{A}
.
As visualized in Fig.
32
, the transition functions of all
G
-atlases for
T\mkern-1.5muM
,
F\mkern-1.5muM
,
G\mkern-1.4muM
and
\mathcal{A}
agree, making the bundles
G
-associated to each other.
Specifically, when switching from gauge
A
to gauge
B
, the trivializations of
T\mkern-1.5muM
,
F\mkern-1.5muM
and
G\mkern-1.4muM
transform according to a left multiplication with
g^{BA}
while the feature vector bundle trivializations transform according to a left multiplication with
\rho\big(g^{BA}\big)
; see Eqs. (
177
), (
6.4
), (
189
) and (Eq. (
6.4
)).
At the same time, frame fields transform according to the right action
\lhd\big(g^{BA}\big)^{-1}
(Eq. (
183
)).

6.5
Parallel transporters on associated bundles

Section
3.3
gave an intuitive introduction to the parallel transport of tangent vectors and feature vectors along a path
\gamma
from
q\in M
to
p\in M
.
Here we briefly discuss how coordinate free parallel transporters on the fiber bundles induce each other and derive coordinate expressions relative to given trivializations for them.
We start by assuming coordinate free transporters

\displaystyle\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-2.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}\mkern-2.0mu,\gamma}}:

\displaystyle T_{\mkern-1.5muq}\mkern-0.5muM

\displaystyle\to T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM

(203)

on the tangent bundle
T\mkern-1.5muM
to be
given
and explain how they
induce
transporters

\displaystyle\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-2.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!F\!M$}\mkern-2.0mu,\gamma}}:

\displaystyle F_{\mkern-1.5muq}\mkern-1.1muM

\displaystyle\to F_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-1.0muM

(204)

on the frame bundle
F\mkern-1.5muM
.
If these transporters are
G
-
compatible
with the chosen
G
-structure, as discussed below, they further induce transporters

\displaystyle\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-2.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!G\!M$}\mkern-2.0mu,\gamma}}:

\displaystyle G_{\mkern-1.3muq}\mkern-1.3muM

\displaystyle\to G_{\mkern-1.3mup}\mkern-1.2muM

(205)

\displaystyle\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A}$}\mkern 0.0mu,\gamma}}:

\displaystyle\mathcal{A}_{q}

\displaystyle\to\mathcal{A}_{p}

(206)

on the associated
G
-bundles
G\mkern-1.4muM
and
\mathcal{A}
.
In practice, that is, in our literature review in Part
8.3.2
, most convolutional networks assume either transporters that are based on the Levi-Civita connection or some trivial connection.

A more formal definition of bundle transporters might take a different route, starting by introducing a so called principal Ehresmann connection on the principal
G
-bundle
G\mkern-1.4muM
(which would by definition be
G
-compatible).
Such an Ehresmann connection can either be defined by a choice of horizontal subbundle
HGM
of the tangent bundle
TGM
of
G\mkern-1.4muM
or, equivalently, by a Lie algebra-valued connection 1-form
\omega:TGM\to\mathfrak{g}
on
G\mkern-1.4muM
.
The transport on
G\mkern-1.4muM
would subsequently be defined via the horizontal lift
\gamma^{\uparrow}:[0,1]\to G\mkern-1.4muM
of curves
\gamma:[0,1]\to M
on the base space such that the tangent vectors of the lift in
G\mkern-1.4muM
are horizontal, i.e.
\dot{\gamma}^{\uparrow}\in HGM
.
All transporters on
T\mkern-1.5muM
,
F\mkern-1.5muM
and
\mathcal{A}
as associated
G
-bundles would then be induced from the transporters on the
G
-structure.
Instead of following this formal approach, which would be rather technical and can be found in the literature
[
196
,
237
,
101
,
162
,
148
,
204
]
,
we focus on how the different transporters interrelate by inducing each other.

Transport on
TM
:

To this end, we take a shortcut by assuming the coordinate free transporters
\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-2.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}\mkern-2.0mu,\gamma}}
on
T\mkern-1.5muM
to be given.
Recall that, given gauges
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}}^{\widetilde{A}}
on a neighborhood
U^{\widetilde{A}}
of
q
and
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}}^{A}
on a neighborhood
U^{A}
of
p
, the tangent vector transporter is coordinatized according to Eq. (
33
), that is,

\displaystyle g_{\gamma}^{A\widetilde{A}}\ :=\ \psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\circ\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-2.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}\mkern-2.0mu,\gamma}}\circ\Big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$q$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\Big)^{-1}\ \in\,\operatorname{GL}(d)\,,

(207)

and that its coordinatizations transform under gauge transformations at
q
and
p
according to Eq. (
35
):

\displaystyle g_{\gamma}^{B\widetilde{B}}\ =\ g_{p}^{BA}\,g_{\gamma}^{A\widetilde{A}}\Big(g_{q}^{\widetilde{B}\widetilde{A}}\Big)^{-1}

(208)

We refer back to Eq. (
34
) for a visualization of these definitions in terms of a commutative diagram.

Transport on
FM
:

Given the transporter on the tangent bundle, the transporter on the frame bundle follows immediately from the transport of individual frame axes.
In equations, let
[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\in F_{\mkern-1.5muq}\mkern-1.1muM
be a frame at
q
, then the individual axes
e_{i}
for
i=1,\dots,d
are tangent vectors in
T_{\mkern-1.5muq}\mkern-0.5muM
which can be transported via
\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-2.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}\mkern-2.0mu,\gamma}}
.
We thus define the transporter on the frame bundle as:
54
54

54

The transport of a frame along
\gamma
describes a curve
\gamma^{\uparrow}
(horizontal lift) in
F\mkern-1.5muM
.
The space spanned by all tangent vectors
\dot{\gamma}^{\uparrow}
in
TFM
along such curves is the horizontal subbundle
HFM
of
TFM
, mentioned above.

\displaystyle\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-2.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!F\!M$}\mkern-2.0mu,\gamma}}\!:\ F_{\mkern-1.5muq}\mkern-1.1muM\to F_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-1.0muM,\quad[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\mapsto\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-2.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!F\!M$}\mkern-2.0mu,\gamma}}\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\big):=\big[\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-2.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}\mkern-2.0mu,\gamma}}(e_{i})\big]_{i=1}^{d}

(209)

In order to derive the explicit form of its coordinatization

\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\circ\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-2.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!F\!M$}\mkern-2.0mu,\gamma}}\circ\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$q$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}\!\in\operatorname{GL}(d)
,
consider its action on a group element

, representing a trivialized frame of
\mathbb{R}^{d}
which is spanned by the matrix columns

:

\displaystyle\Big[\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\circ\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-2.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!F\!M$}\mkern-2.0mu,\gamma}}\circ\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$q$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}\Big](h)\

\displaystyle=\ \Big[\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\circ\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-2.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!F\!M$}\mkern-2.0mu,\gamma}}\Big]\Big(\!\big[\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$q$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}(h_{:,i})\big]_{i=1}^{d}\Big)\qquad

\displaystyle\big(\text{def. of $\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}$, Eq.~\eqref{eq:trivialization_FM_p}}\big)

\displaystyle=\ \psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\Big(\big[\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-2.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}\mkern-2.0mu,\gamma}}\circ\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$q$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}(h_{:,i})\big]_{i=1}^{d}\Big)\qquad

\displaystyle\big(\text{def. of $\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-2.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!F\!M$}\mkern-2.0mu,\gamma}}$, Eq.~\eqref{eq:transporter_FM_def}}\big)

\displaystyle=\ \Big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\circ\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-2.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}\mkern-2.0mu,\gamma}}\circ\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$q$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}(h_{:,i})\Big)_{i=1}^{d}\qquad

\displaystyle\big(\text{def. of $\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}$, Eq.~\eqref{eq:trivialization_FM_p}}\big)

\displaystyle=\ \Big(g_{\gamma}^{A\widetilde{A}}(h_{:,i})\Big)_{i=1}^{d}\qquad

\displaystyle\big(\text{triv. of $\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-2.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}\mkern-2.0mu,\gamma}}$, Eq.~\eqref{eq:transporter_gauge_copy}}\big)

\displaystyle=\ g_{\gamma}^{A\widetilde{A}}\,h

(210)

The coordinatizations of the frame transporters are therefore equivalent to those of the tangent vector transporters in Eq. (

) but act on trivialized frames in

instead of acting on coefficient vectors in

.

Compatibility of connections and
G
-structures:

Not any choice of connection or definition of transporters on the
\operatorname{GL}(d)
-bundles
T\mkern-1.5muM
and
F\mkern-1.5muM
is compatible with any
G
-structure.
Specifically, a
G
-structure might not be closed under the transport of frames, that is,
while a frame in
G_{\mkern-1.3muq}\mkern-1.3muM\subseteq F_{\mkern-1.5muq}\mkern-1.1muM
will by
\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-2.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!F\!M$}\mkern-2.0mu,\gamma}}
be transported to some frame in
F_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-1.0muM
, this frame is
not
necessarily contained in
G_{\mkern-1.3mup}\mkern-1.2muM
.
55
55

55

In terms of a principal Ehresmann connection on
F\mkern-1.5muM
, this is the case if the horizontal subbundle
HFM\subseteq TFM
is not contained in
TGM\subseteq TFM
.
An immediate definition of parallel transport in terms of a choice of horizontal subbundle
HGM
on the
G
-structure will always (by definition) lead to a well defined transport on
G\mkern-1.4muM
.

Relative to trivializations of
G\mkern-1.4muM
, such an incompatibility would reflect in coordinatized transporters
{g_{\gamma}^{A\widetilde{A}}\notin G}
, whose left multiplication is well defined on the fibers
\mathbb{R}^{d}
and
\operatorname{GL}(d)
of the
\operatorname{GL}(d)
-bundles
T\mkern-1.5muM
and
F\mkern-1.5muM
, but not on the fiber
G
of
G\mkern-1.4muM
.
If the subbundle
G\mkern-1.4muM
is not closed under the parallel transport on
F\mkern-1.5muM
, this means that no well defined corresponding transport on
G\mkern-1.4muM
– and thus on any associated
G
-bundles
\mathcal{A}
– exists.

As an example, consider the Levi-Civita connection on Euclidean spaces, whose transporters keep tangent vectors and frames parallel in the usual sense on
\mathbb{E}_{d}
.
The
\{e\}
-structure (frame field) in Fig.
40(a)
is closed under this transport, and therefore compatible.
The
\{e\}
-structure in Fig.
40(b)
, on the other hand, is not closed under the transport, and thus incompatible with the Levi-Civita connection.
Similarly, the
\operatorname{SO}(2)
-structure on
S^{2}
in Fig.
55(a)
is compatible with the Levi-Civita connection on the sphere, while the
\{e\}
-structure in Fig.
55(b)
is not.

The reader might wonder which general statements about the compatibility of connections (or transporters) and
G
-structures can be made.
In general, the Levi-Civita connection, or any other metric connection, are compatible with the
\operatorname{O}(d)
-structure
\operatorname{O}\mkern-3.6muM
that corresponds to the metric.
56
56

56

This statement holds by definition since metric connections preserve angles and lengths between vectors and thus the orthonormality of frames.
One can furthermore
define
metric connections as principal Ehresmann connections on
\operatorname{O}\mkern-3.6muM
.

If the manifold is orientable, the Levi-Civita connection is furthermore compatible with any
\operatorname{SO}(d)
-structure that corresponds to the metric.
An example is the
\operatorname{SO}(2)
-structure on
S^{2}
in Fig.
55(a)
.
A necessary (but not sufficient) condition for a
G
-structure to be compatible with a given connection is that the holonomy group of the connection is a subgroup of the structure group
G
.

An important special case is that of
\{e\}
-structures, since they imply a
unique trivial connection
.
57
57

57

A connection is
trivial
if its holonomy group, i.e. its parallel transport around any closed loop, is trivial
[
43
]
.

58
58

58

Only one principal Ehresmann connection
H\raisebox{0.2pt}{$\raisebox{0.4pt}{\scalebox{.8}{$\{$}}\mkern-1.5mue\mkern-0.9mu\raisebox{0.4pt}{\scalebox{.8}{$\}$}}$}\mkern-2.0muM=T\raisebox{0.2pt}{$\raisebox{0.4pt}{\scalebox{.8}{$\{$}}\mkern-1.5mue\mkern-0.9mu\raisebox{0.4pt}{\scalebox{.8}{$\}$}}$}\mkern-2.0muM
can be chosen on
\raisebox{0.2pt}{$\raisebox{0.4pt}{\scalebox{.8}{$\{$}}\mkern-1.5mue\mkern-0.9mu\raisebox{0.4pt}{\scalebox{.8}{$\}$}}$}\mkern-2.0muM
since the vertical subbundle
V\raisebox{0.2pt}{$\raisebox{0.4pt}{\scalebox{.8}{$\{$}}\mkern-1.5mue\mkern-0.9mu\raisebox{0.4pt}{\scalebox{.8}{$\}$}}$}\mkern-2.0muM
is the zero-section of
T\raisebox{0.2pt}{$\raisebox{0.4pt}{\scalebox{.8}{$\{$}}\mkern-1.5mue\mkern-0.9mu\raisebox{0.4pt}{\scalebox{.8}{$\}$}}$}\mkern-2.0muM
.

The corresponding transporters move frames in such a way that the stay parallel with the frames of the
\{e\}
-structure.
Trivial connections might not seem to be of particular importance for the theory of
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions, however, they are actually utilized by many convolutional networks.
Specifically, any network that relies on an
\{e\}
-structure is implicitly assuming a trivial connection.
This includes all of the models in Table
with
G=\{e\}
, specifically those which are reviewed in Sections
11.3
and
12.3
.
59
59

59

These models are
implicitly
assuming a trivial connection by not modeling non-trivial transporters of feature vectors:
they accumulate feature vector coefficients without transforming them.

Note that these models assume the trivial connection only for their feature vector transport but compute geodesics for the transporter pullback, Eq. (
4.2.1
), based on the original Levi-Civita connection.

Transport on
GM
:

Assuming that
G\mkern-1.4muM
is compatible with (i.e. closed under) the transport on
F\mkern-1.5muM
, a well defined transporter is given by restricting the frame bundle transporter to the
G
-structure:

\displaystyle\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-2.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!G\!M$}\mkern-2.0mu,\gamma}}:=\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-2.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!F\!M$}\mkern-2.0mu,\gamma}}\big|_{\scalebox{.62}{$G\mkern-1.4muM$}}:\ \ G_{\mkern-1.3muq}\mkern-1.3muM\to G_{\mkern-1.3mup}\mkern-1.2muM

(212)

The transition functions between different coordinatizations of

do then agree with those of

and thus also
\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-2.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}\mkern-2.0mu,\gamma}}
.
We obtain the following commutative diagram, which visualizes the restriction of the diagram in Eq. (

) from

and
\operatorname{GL}(d)
to

,
G_{\mkern-1.3mup}\mkern-1.2muM
and
G
:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G_{\mkern-1.3muq}\mkern-1.3muM}

(213)

We will in the remainder of this work assume that the transport on
G\mkern-1.4muM
is well defined.

Transport on
\bm{\mathcal{A}}
:

If the transporters of a connection are well defined on
G\mkern-1.4muM
, they induce transporters on any associated
G
-bundle, including the feature vector bundles
\mathcal{A}=(G\mkern-1.4muM\times\mathbb{R}^{c})/\!\sim_{\rho}
.
Let
f_{q}:=\big[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d},\,{f}\>\!\big]
be a coordinate free feature vector in
\mathcal{A}_{q}
.
Its parallel transport is given by that equivalence class defined by keeping some representative coefficients
{f}\in\mathbb{R}^{c}
fixed and transporting the corresponding frame
[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}
:

\displaystyle\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A}$}\mkern 0.0mu,\gamma}}:\mathcal{A}_{q}

\displaystyle\to\mathcal{A}_{p},\quad f_{q}\,\mapsto\,\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A}$}\mkern 0.0mu,\gamma}}(f_{q})\,:=\,\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big[$}}}}}\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-2.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!G\!M$}\mkern-2.0mu,\gamma}}\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}),\>{f}\,\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big]$}}}}}

(214)

In Section
3.3
we claimed that the transporter of numerical feature vector coefficients is given by
\rho\big(g_{\gamma}^{A\widetilde{A}}\big)
provided that
g_{\gamma}^{A\widetilde{A}}\in G
, which is the case if the transport on
G\mkern-1.4muM
is well defined.
This coordinate expression of
\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A}$}\mkern 0.0mu,\gamma}}
can be derived by evaluating the action of

\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\circ\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A}$}\mkern 0.0mu,\gamma}}\circ\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$q$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}\in\,\rho(G)\,\leq\,\operatorname{GL}(c)

on a feature coefficient vector
{f}\in\mathbb{R}^{c}
step by step:

\displaystyle\Big[\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\circ\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A}$}\mkern 0.0mu,\gamma}}\circ\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$q$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}\Big]({f})\

\displaystyle=\ \Big[\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\circ\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A}$}\mkern 0.0mu,\gamma}}\Big]\big(\big[\sigma^{\widetilde{A}}(q),\,{f}\,\big]\big)\qquad

\displaystyle\big(\text{def. of $\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}$, Eq.~\eqref{eq:trivialization_A_p_inv}}\big)

(215)

\displaystyle=\ \psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\Big(\big[\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-2.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!G\!M$}\mkern-2.0mu,\gamma}}\big(\sigma^{\widetilde{A}}(q)\big),\,{f}\,\big]\Big)\qquad

\displaystyle\big(\text{def. of $\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A}$}\mkern 0.0mu,\gamma}}$, Eq.~\eqref{eq:transporter_A_def}}\big)

\displaystyle=\ \rho\Big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\circ\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-2.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!G\!M$}\mkern-2.0mu,\gamma}}\circ\sigma^{\widetilde{A}}(q)\Big)\cdot{f}\qquad

\displaystyle\big(\text{def. of $\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}$, Eq.~\eqref{eq:trivialization_A_p}}\big)

\displaystyle=\ \rho\Big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\circ\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-2.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!G\!M$}\mkern-2.0mu,\gamma}}\circ\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$q$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}(e)\Big)\cdot{f}\qquad

\displaystyle\big(\text{def. of identity section $\sigma^{\widetilde{A}}$, Eq.~\eqref{eq:identity_section_def}}\big)

\displaystyle=\ \rho\big(g_{\gamma}^{A\widetilde{A}}\big)\!\cdot\!{f}\qquad

\displaystyle\big(\text{$\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-2.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!G\!M$}\mkern-2.0mu,\gamma}}$ in coordinates Eq.~\eqref{cd:transport_GM_triv}}\big)

The commutative diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{R}^{c}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{R}^{c}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{A}_{q}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{A}_{p}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{R}^{c}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{R}^{c}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\rho\big(g_{q}^{\widetilde{B}\widetilde{A}}\big)\ }
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\rho\big(g_{\gamma}^{A\widetilde{A}}\big)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\ \rho\big(g_{p}^{BA}\big)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$q$}}^{\widetilde{A}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$q$}}^{\widetilde{B}}}

(216)

implies that the gauge transformations of the coordinatized feature vector transporters read:

\displaystyle\rho\big(g_{\gamma}^{B\widetilde{B}}\big)\ =\ \rho\big(g_{p}^{BA}\big)\rho\big(g_{\gamma}^{A\widetilde{A}}\big)\rho\big(g_{q}^{\widetilde{B}\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}

(217)

Note that this transformation law is in agreement with that in Eq. (
208
).

7
Coordinate free kernel field transforms and
GM
-convolutions

The associated
G
-bundles introduced in Section
6
allow to describe feature fields – and therefore convolutional networks – on a global level.
Given a sequence

{\mathcal{A}_{0}\!\xrightarrow{\scalebox{.85}{$\pi_{{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}_{0}$}}}$}}\!M,}\ \dots,\ {\mathcal{A}_{N}\!\xrightarrow{\scalebox{.85}{$\pi_{{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}_{N}$}}}$}}\!M}
,
of
G
-associated feature vector bundles over
M
, we describe coordinate free convolutional networks as sequences

\displaystyle\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{0})\,\xrightarrow{\ \ L_{1}\ \ }\,\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{1})\,\xrightarrow{\ \ L_{2}\ \ }\ \ \dots\ \ \xrightarrow{\ \ L_{N}\ \ }\,\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{N})

(218)

of parameterized layers
L_{1},\dots,L_{N}
which map between the feature spaces
\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{0}),\dots,\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{N})
, i.e. between spaces of feature fields modeled by the corresponding bundles.
While the field types (or transformation laws)
{\rho_{i}:G\to\operatorname{GL}({c_{i}})}
of the intermediate bundles

\mathcal{A}_{i}:=(G\mkern-1.4muM\times\mathbb{R}^{c_{i}})/\!\sim_{\!\rho_{i}}
for
i=1,\dots,N-1

have to be specified by the user as a hyperparameter, the field types
\rho_{0}:G\to\operatorname{GL}({c_{0}})
and
\rho_{N}:G\to\operatorname{GL}({c_{N}})
of the network input and output are typically determined by the learning task.
The modular construction of neural networks allows to restrict attention to individual layers, mapping between feature spaces
\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}})
and
\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})
of dimensionality
{c_{\textup{in}}}
and
{c_{\textup{out}}}
and type
\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}
and
\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}
.

The main goal of this section is to introduce coordinate free
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions, which are the central building blocks of
G\mkern-1.4muM
-coordinate independent networks on Riemannian manifolds.
To get started, and to introduce concepts which are required later on, we will in Section
7.1
first focus on the simpler case of
\mathit{{1\kern-2.75pt\times\kern-3.1pt1}}

G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions
, which apply point-like kernels.
Section
7.2
shifts the focus to
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions and kernel field transforms with spatially extended kernels.
They are parameterized in terms of smooth, global
kernel fields
, which are introduced in Section
7.2.1
.

G\mkern-1.4muM
-
convolutional kernel fields
are required to share weights between different spatial positions.
In order for this weight sharing to be
G\mkern-1.4muM
-coordinate independent, the template kernels that parameterize
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutional kernel fields are required to be
G
-steerable (Eq. (
244
)).
The actual kernel field transforms and
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions are introduced in Section
7.2.2
.
Their global definition is guided by replacing the local coordinate expressions from Section
4.2
with their global, coordinate free counterparts.
As shown in Section
7.2.3
, these coordinate free definitions reduce in local trivializations to the coordinate expressions form Section
4.2
.

7.1
\bm{1\kern-2.7pt\times\kern-2.9pt1}

GM
-convolutions

{1\kern-2.65pt\times\kern-3.0pt1}

G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions
map input feature fields
f_{\textup{\;\!\!in}}\in\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}})
to output feature fields
f_{\textup{\>\!\!out}}\in\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})
by linearly mapping each individual input feature vector
f_{\textup{\;\!\!in}}(p)\in\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in},p}\cong\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{in}}}}
to an output feature vector
f_{\textup{\>\!\!out}}(p)\in\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out},p}\cong\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}}
at the same location
p\in M
.
The convolutional character is implemented by
sharing
the linear map from
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in},p}
to
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out},p}
between different spatial locations.
However, while the feature spaces
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in},p}
and
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in},q}
as well as
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out},p}
and
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out},q}
are for different
p,q\in M
isomorphic to each other, there is no canonical isomorphism between them given if the considered structure group
G
is non-trivial.
It is therefore not obvious how the linear map could be shared between different locations.
As already suggested in the introduction of this section, this issue is resolved by considering
G
-equivariant kernels which are indifferent to the specific choice of isomorphism or gauge.
The arbitrariness of the trivialization which is chosen from the
G
-atlas reflects the
G\mkern-1.4muM
-coordinate independence of
{1\kern-2.65pt\times\kern-3.0pt1}

G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions
.

Mathematically,
{1\kern-2.65pt\times\kern-3.0pt1}

G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions
can be formulated either as specific vector bundle
M
-morphisms or via the corresponding sections of (associated) homomorphism bundles
\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})
.
Since we require both concepts later on, we will introduce both viewpoints in the following Sections
7.1.1
and
7.1.2
.

7.1.1
\bm{1\kern-2.7pt\times\kern-2.9pt1}

GM
-convolutions as vector bundle
M
-morphisms

{1\kern-2.65pt\times\kern-3.0pt1}

G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions
can be formalized in terms of specific smooth
vector bundle
M
-morphisms
which share weights over spatial positions.
Ignoring the requirement for shared weights for now, such a vector bundle
M
-morphism
\mathcal{C}
is a smooth bundle map satisfying the following commutative diagram:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces M}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6 }{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{C}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6 }{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{out}}}}}

(219)

The commutativity
\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6 }{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}}}}=\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6 }{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{out}}}}\!\circ\,\mathcal{C}
ensures that each fiber
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in},p}
is mapped to the fiber
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out},p}
over the same point
p\in M
(which gives rise to the “
M
” in the term
M
-morphism).
As a vector bundle morphism, the restriction
\mathcal{C}\!\!\;|_{p}:\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in},p}\to\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out},p}
to a single fiber is further defined to be linear.
Relative to a local trivialization
\Psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}}}}^{A}
of
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}
and
\Psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{out}}}}^{A}
of
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}}
, the bundle map is therefore at each point
p\in U^{A}
represented by a matrix

\displaystyle\mathcal{C}^{A}\!\!\;|_{p}\ :=\ \psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{out}},p}}^{A}\circ\mathcal{C}\!\;|_{p}\circ\big(\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},p}}^{A}\big)^{-1}\ \in\,\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}\times{c_{\textup{in}}}}\,.

(220)

Its relationship to a second coordinatization
\mathcal{C}^{B}
is at
p\in U^{A}\cap U^{B}
given by

\displaystyle\mathcal{C}^{B}\!\!\;|_{p}\ =\ \rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}\big(g_{p}^{BA}\big)\;\mathcal{C}^{A}\!\!\;|_{p}\;\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{p}^{BA}\big)^{-1}\,,

(221)

which is evident from the commutative diagram below:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{in}}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in},p}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out},p}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{in}}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{p}^{BA}\big)\ }
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{C}^{A}\!\!\;|_{p}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\ \rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}\big(g_{p}^{BA}\big)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{C}\!\!\;|_{p}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},p}}^{A}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},p}}^{B}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{out}},p}}^{A}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{out}},p}}^{B}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{C}^{B}\!\!\;|_{p}}

(222)

The bundle map
\mathcal{C}
acts on input feature fields
f_{\textup{\;\!\!in}}\in\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}})
to produce output feature fields

\displaystyle f_{\textup{\>\!\!out}}=\mathcal{C}\circ f_{\textup{\;\!\!in}}\quad\in\ \ \Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})\,.

(223)

In terms of a commutative diagram, this mapping is visualized as:

(224)

In order for a vector bundle
M
-morphism
\mathcal{C}_{K_{\!1\!\times\!1}}
to represent a
{1\kern-2.65pt\times\kern-3.0pt1}

G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolution
, it needs to be parameterized in terms of a
{1\kern-2.65pt\times\kern-3.0pt1}

G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolution
kernel template
K_{\!1\!\times\!1}\in\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}\times{c_{\textup{in}}}}
which is shared with coordinatizations at all spatial positions.
As argued before, no particular gauge must thereby be preferred in order to ensure
G\mkern-1.4muM
-coordinate independence
.
It is therefore necessary to
share the weights with all trivializations
X\in\mathfrak{X}
of the
G
-atlas
{A}^{G}
simultaneously
, that is, to require:

\displaystyle\mathcal{C}_{K_{\!1\!\times\!1}}^{X}\!\big|_{p}\ =\ K_{\!1\!\times\!1}\qquad\textup{for \emph{any} gauge}\,\ X\in\mathfrak{X}\,\ \textup{with}\,\ p\in U^{X}\,.

(225)

From the transformation behavior between different coordinatizations in Eq. (
221
) it follows that the kernel template has to satisfy the linear constraint

\displaystyle\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}(g)\,K_{\!1\!\times\!1}\,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}(g)^{-1}=\,K_{\!1\!\times\!1}\qquad\forall g\in G,

(226)

that is, it has to be an intertwiner (an equivariant linear map).
The vector space

\displaystyle\Hom_{G}(\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}},\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}})\ :=\ \mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\Big\{$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\Big\{$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big\{$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big\{$}}}}}K_{\!1\!\times\!1}\in\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}\times{c_{\textup{in}}}}\ \mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big|$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big|$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big|$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big|$}}}}}\ K_{\!1\!\times\!1}\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}(g)=\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}(g)K_{\!1\!\times\!1}\ \ \forall g\in G\mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\Big\}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\Big\}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big\}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big\}$}}}}}

(227)

of intertwining maps characterizes the space of
G\mkern-1.4muM
-coordinate independent
{1\kern-2.65pt\times\kern-3.0pt1}
-convolution
kernels fully.
As already mentioned in Section
4.1.1
,
Schur’s Lemma

[
75
]
implies that the requirement on
K_{\!1\!\times\!1}
to be an intertwiner prevents a mapping between fields which transform under non-isomorphic irreducible representations via
{1\kern-2.65pt\times\kern-3.0pt1}

G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions
.
The more general
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions with spatially extended kernels, defined in Section
7.2
, will resolve this issue.

With these preparations we are ready to give a concise definition of
{1\kern-2.65pt\times\kern-3.0pt1}

G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions
:

Definition 7.1
(
{1\kern-2.65pt\times\kern-3.0pt1}

G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolution
).

A
{1\kern-2.65pt\times\kern-3.0pt1}

G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolution
is a map

\displaystyle K_{\!1\!\times\!1}\raisebox{1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.1}{$\mathbin{\hbox{\hskip 9.08887pt\hskip-9.08887pt\hbox{$\hbox{$\scalebox{.6}{$\bigcirc$}$}$}\hskip-9.08887pt\hskip-2.5pt\raisebox{0.1736pt}{\hbox{$\rule{0.0pt}{0.0pt}\rule{0.0pt}{0.0pt}\hbox{$\star$}$}}\hskip-2.5pt\hskip 9.08887pt}}$}}:\ \Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}})\to\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}}),\ \ \ f_{\textup{\;\!\!in}}\,\mapsto\,K_{\!1\!\times\!1}\,\raisebox{1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.1}{$\mathbin{\hbox{\hskip 9.08887pt\hskip-9.08887pt\hbox{$\hbox{$\scalebox{.6}{$\bigcirc$}$}$}\hskip-9.08887pt\hskip-2.5pt\raisebox{0.1736pt}{\hbox{$\rule{0.0pt}{0.0pt}\rule{0.0pt}{0.0pt}\hbox{$\star$}$}}\hskip-2.5pt\hskip 9.08887pt}}$}}\,f_{\textup{\;\!\!in}}\,:=\,\mathcal{C}_{K_{\!1\!\times\!1}}\!\circ f_{\textup{\;\!\!in}}

(228)

which is parameterized by an
intertwining

{1\kern-2.65pt\times\kern-3.0pt1}

G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolution
kernel
K_{\!1\!\times\!1}\in\Hom_{G}(\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}},\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}})
.
Here
\mathcal{C}_{K_{\!1\!\times\!1}}
is the unique smooth vector bundle
M
-morphism between
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}
and
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}}
which is in
arbitrary
gauges
\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},p}}
and
\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{out}},p}}
from the considered
G
-atlas pointwise defined by

\displaystyle\mathcal{C}_{K_{\!1\!\times\!1}}|_{p}\ :=\ \psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{out}},p}}^{-1}\circ K_{\!1\!\times\!1}\circ\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},p}}\,.

(229)

The independence of the chosen gauges (
G\mkern-1.4muM
-coordinate independence) is guaranteed by
K_{\!1\!\times\!1}
being an intertwiner.

To show the independence of the chosen gauge explicitly, consider any
G
-related trivializations
\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}(g)\,\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},p}}
and
\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}(g)\,\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{out}},p}}
for an arbitrary structure group element
g\in G
, which leave the construction of

\displaystyle\mathcal{C}_{K_{\!1\!\times\!1}}\mkern-2.0mu\big|_{p}\ =\ \

\displaystyle\big(\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}(g)\,\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{out}},p}}\big)^{-1}\circ K_{\!1\!\times\!1}\circ\big(\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}(g)\,\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},p}}\big)

\displaystyle=\ \

\displaystyle\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{out}},p}}^{-1}\circ\big(\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}(g)^{-1}K_{\!1\!\times\!1}\,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}(g)\big)\circ\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},p}}

\displaystyle=\ \

\displaystyle\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{out}},p}}^{-1}\circ K_{\!1\!\times\!1}\circ\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},p}}

(230)

invariant.
That such defined
{1\kern-2.65pt\times\kern-3.0pt1}

G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions
are indeed mapping to sections in
\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})
follows from
\mathcal{C}_{K_{\!1\!\times\!1}}
being a bundle map.
An overview of local coordinatizations of
{1\kern-2.65pt\times\kern-3.0pt1}

G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions
is given in Fig.
35
.

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces U\times\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{in}}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces U\times\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces U\times\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{in}}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6 }{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}}}}^{-1}(U)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6 }{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{out}}}}^{-1}(U)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces U\times\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces U}
\mathcal{C}_{K_{\!1\!\times\!1}}^{B}:=(\mathrm{id}\times K_{\!1\!\times\!1})
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{proj}_{1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\big(\mathrm{id}\!\times\!\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g^{BA}\big)\!\cdot\big)}
\mathcal{C}_{K_{\!1\!\times\!1}}^{A}:=(\mathrm{id}\times K_{\!1\!\times\!1})
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6 }{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}}}}\mkern-12.0mu}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}}}}^{A}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}}}}^{B}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{C}_{K_{\!1\!\times\!1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mkern-6.0mu\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6 }{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{out}}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{out}}}}^{A}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{out}}}}^{B}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\big(\mathrm{id}\!\times\!\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}\big(g^{BA}\big)\!\cdot\big)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{proj}_{1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\!f_{\textup{\;\!\!in}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces K_{\!1\!\times\!1}\mkern-1.0mu\raisebox{1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.1}{$\mathbin{\hbox{\hskip 8.8889pt\hskip-8.8889pt\hbox{$\hbox{$\scalebox{.6}{$\bigcirc$}$}$}\hskip-8.8889pt\hskip-2.5pt\raisebox{0.1736pt}{\hbox{$\rule{0.0pt}{0.0pt}\rule{0.0pt}{0.0pt}\hbox{$\star$}$}}\hskip-2.5pt\hskip 8.8889pt}}$}}\mkern-1.0muf_{\textup{\;\!\!in}}\!\!}

\>\!\circlearrowleft\>\!

\>\!\circlearrowleft\>\!

Figure 35:
Coordinatization of an
{1\kern-2.65pt\times\kern-3.0pt1}

G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolution

K_{\!1\!\times\!1}\raisebox{1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.1}{$\mathbin{\hbox{\hskip 8.8889pt\hskip-8.8889pt\hbox{$\hbox{$\scalebox{.6}{$\bigcirc$}$}$}\hskip-8.8889pt\hskip-2.5pt\raisebox{0.1736pt}{\hbox{$\rule{0.0pt}{0.0pt}\rule{0.0pt}{0.0pt}\hbox{$\star$}$}}\hskip-2.5pt\hskip 8.8889pt}}$}}:\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}})\to\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})
and its corresponding vector bundle
M
-morphism
\mathcal{C}_{K_{\!1\!\times\!1}}
.
The convolutional character is encoded into the morphism by sharing a kernel matrix
K_{\!1\!\times\!1}\in\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}\times{c_{\textup{in}}}}
over different spatial positions
p\in M
.
Since no gauge is to be preferred, the kernel is furthermore shared over different trivializations

\mathcal{C}_{K_{\!1\!\times\!1}}^{A}
and
\mathcal{C}_{K_{\!1\!\times\!1}}^{B}
.
The commutativity of the diagram for any choices

\Psi_{\!\!\mathcal{A}_{\text{in}}}^{A}
,

\Psi_{\!\!\mathcal{A}_{\text{out}}}^{A}
and

\Psi_{\!\!\mathcal{A}_{\text{in}}}^{B}
,

\Psi_{\!\!\mathcal{A}_{\text{out}}}^{B}

therefore enforces the constraint

\rho_{\text{out}}(g)K_{\!1\!\times\!1}\rho_{\text{in}}(g)^{-1}=K_{\!1\!\times\!1}\,\ \forall g\!\in G

which restricts the kernel matrix to be an intertwiner (an equivariant linear map), that is,

K_{\!1\!\times\!1}\in\Hom_{G}(\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}},\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}})\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}\times{c_{\textup{in}}}}
.
Except for
f_{\textup{\;\!\!in}}\circ\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6 }{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}}}}\neq\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}}
and
\big[K_{\!1\!\times\!1}\raisebox{1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.1}{$\mathbin{\hbox{\hskip 8.8889pt\hskip-8.8889pt\hbox{$\hbox{$\scalebox{.6}{$\bigcirc$}$}$}\hskip-8.8889pt\hskip-2.5pt\raisebox{0.1736pt}{\hbox{$\rule{0.0pt}{0.0pt}\rule{0.0pt}{0.0pt}\hbox{$\star$}$}}\hskip-2.5pt\hskip 8.8889pt}}$}}f_{\textup{\;\!\!in}}\big]\circ\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6 }{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{out}}}}\neq\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}}}
, the diagram commutes.

7.1.2
\bm{1\kern-2.7pt\times\kern-2.9pt1}

GM
-convolutions as homomorphism bundle sections

While the vector bundle
M
-morphism with gauge independent coordinatizations from Def.
7.1
and Fig.
35
fully specifies a
{1\kern-2.65pt\times\kern-3.0pt1}

G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolution
, we will now adopt an alternative viewpoint which describes
{1\kern-2.65pt\times\kern-3.0pt1}

G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions
in terms of the
homomorphism bundle

\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})\xrightarrow{\,\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ \!Hom}}}\,}M
.
To this end, recall that the vector bundle morphism
\mathcal{C}
in Eq. (
219
) restricts to linear maps
{\mathcal{C}\!\>|_{p}}:\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in},p}\to\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out},p}
over each
p\in M
.
The set of such linear maps (or vector space homomorphisms) between
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in},p}
and
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out},p}
is denoted as
\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in},p},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out},p})
.
Since it is closed under linear combinations, it forms a vector space itself.
It can be shown that the disjoint union

\displaystyle\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})\ :=\ \coprod_{p\in M}\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in},p},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out},p})

(231)

of these homomorphism spaces forms a vector bundle, the homomorphism bundle between
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}
and
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}}
, when being equipped with the projection map
\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ \!Hom}}}:\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})\to M
which sends elements in
\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in},p},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out},p})
to
p
and a smooth structure induced from that of
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}
and
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}}

[
53
]
.
The fibers over
p
satisfy
\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in},p},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out},p})\cong\Hom(\mathbb{R}^{c_{\textup{in}}},\mathbb{R}^{c_{\textup{out}}})\cong\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}\times{c_{\textup{in}}}}
such that we can take the typical fiber to be the vector space of real-valued
{{c_{\textup{out}}}\!\times\!{c_{\textup{in}}}}
matrices.
The trivializations

\displaystyle\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{\!Hom}}:\ \pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ \!Hom}}}^{-1}(U)\to U\!\times\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}\times{c_{\textup{in}}}},\ \ H\mapsto\big(p,\ \psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}(H)\big),

(232)

where we abbreviated
p=\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ \!Hom}}}(H)
, are
induced
from the trivializations of
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}
and
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}}
by defining

\displaystyle\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}\!:\ \Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in},p},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out},p})\to\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}\times{c_{\textup{in}}}},\ \ \ H\mapsto\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{out}},p}}\circ H\circ\big(\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},p}}\big)^{-1}

(233)

in analogy to Eqs. (
220
) and (
18
).
This implies transition maps

\displaystyle H^{B}\

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\ \psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{out}},p}}^{B}\circ\,

\displaystyle H\circ\big(\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},p}}^{B}\big)^{-1}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\ \psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{out}},p}}^{B}\circ\big(\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{out}},p}}^{A}\big)^{-1}\,

\displaystyle H^{A}\ \psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},p}}^{A}\circ\big(\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},p}}^{B}\big)^{-1}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\ \rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}\big(g^{BA}\big)\,

\displaystyle H^{A}\,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g^{BA}\big)^{-1}

\displaystyle=:

\displaystyle\ \rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{{Hom}}}}\big(g^{BA}\big)\,

\displaystyle H^{A}

(234)

between gauges
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{\!Hom}}^{A}
and
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{\!Hom}}^{B}
on
U^{A}\cap U^{B}
, where we introduced the homomorphism group representation
\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{{Hom}}}}:G\to\operatorname{GL}(\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}\times{c_{\textup{in}}}})
as left and right multiplication with
\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}
and
\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}
for notational convenience.
60
60

60

In general, a homomorphism bundle between two
non-associated
vector bundles with structure groups
G_{1}
and
G_{2}
would have a structure group
G_{1}\times G_{2}
.
Since
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}
and
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}}
are associated, they transform synchronously under the same structure group
G_{1}=G_{2}=G
such that their transition maps take values in the diagonal subgroup
G
of
G\times G
.

The homomorphism bundle
\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})
is by construction associated to
T\mkern-1.5muM
,
G\mkern-1.4muM
,
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}
and
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}}
, that is, its trivializations transform synchronously with those of the other bundles.
As a
G
-associated vector bundle, it can be identified with
(G\mkern-1.4muM\times\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}\times{c_{\textup{in}}}})/\!\sim_{\!\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{{Hom}}}}}
.
Fig.
36(a)
gives an overview of the local trivializations of
\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})
.
Note the similarity to the trivializations of the other associated
G
-bundles in Fig.

.

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces U\times\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}\times{c_{\textup{in}}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ \!Hom}}}^{-1}(U)}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{proj}_{1}}

\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})
.

,

The sections
\sigma_{K_{1\!\times\!1}}:M\to\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})
of the homomorphism bundle which correspond to

G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions
are exactly those which trivialize to the

(intertwining) matrix

K_{\!1\!\times\!1}\in\Hom_{G}(\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}},\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}})\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}\times{c_{\textup{in}}}}

in all gauges.
Such sections correspond to bundle maps which trivialize as specified in Fig.

.

Figure 36:
Local trivializations of the homomorphism bundle
\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})
, which is the vector bundle of linear maps between the spaces
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in},p}
and
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out},p}
for any
p\in M
.
As usual we abbreviate

.
Except for

the diagrams commute.

From the viewpoint of homomorphism bundles, unconstrained bundle maps as in Eq. (
219
) correspond to the action of unconstrained smooth homomorphism bundle sections

\displaystyle\sigma_{\Hom}:M\mapsto\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})\quad\textup{such that}\quad\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ \!Hom}}}\circ\sigma_{\Hom}=\mathrm{id}_{M}

(235)

which can be interpreted as
1\!\times\!1

kernel fields
that do not share weights.
Their global existence is guaranteed by
\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})
being a vector bundle.
Sections corresponding to
\mathit{{1\kern-2.75pt\times\kern-3.1pt1}}

G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions
require in addition that the linear transformations
\sigma_{\Hom}(p)\in\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in},p},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out},p})
are determined by a template kernel
K_{\!1\!\times\!1}\in\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}\times{c_{\textup{in}}}}
which is shared over different positions
p\in M
and any choice of gauge.
They can therefore for any
p\in\!M
be defined as

\displaystyle\sigma_{K_{1\!\times\!1}}(p)\ :=\ \psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{-1}\big(K_{\!1\!\times\!1}\big),\qquad K_{\!1\!\times\!1}\in\Hom_{G}(\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}},\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}})\,,

(236)

where the chosen trivialization
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{\!Hom}}
is arbitrary if (and only if)
K_{\!1\!\times\!1}
satisfies the intertwiner constraint

\displaystyle\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{{Hom}}}}(g)K_{\!1\!\times\!1}=K_{\!1\!\times\!1}\qquad\forall g\in G\,,

(237)

which is equivalent to Eq. (
226
).
61
61

61

The required smoothness of the section follows from the smoothness of the local trivializations.

The gauge irrelevance of such sections is visualized in the commutative diagram in Fig.
36(b)
(compare this to the equivalent bundle map trivialization in Fig.
35
).

Summarizing remarks:

A smooth
{1\kern-2.65pt\times\kern-3.0pt1}

G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolution
layer
K_{\!1\!\times\!1}\raisebox{1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.1}{$\mathbin{\hbox{\hskip 8.8889pt\hskip-8.8889pt\hbox{$\hbox{$\scalebox{.6}{$\bigcirc$}$}$}\hskip-8.8889pt\hskip-2.5pt\raisebox{0.1736pt}{\hbox{$\rule{0.0pt}{0.0pt}\rule{0.0pt}{0.0pt}\hbox{$\star$}$}}\hskip-2.5pt\hskip 8.8889pt}}$}}:\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}})\to\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}}),\ f_{\textup{\;\!\!in}}\mapsto f_{\textup{\>\!\!out}}
can equivalently be defined via a smooth bundle map as
f_{\textup{\>\!\!out}}(p):=\mathcal{C}_{K_{\!1\!\times\!1}}\!\circ f_{\textup{\;\!\!in}}(p)
or via a smooth homomorphism bundle section as
f_{\textup{\>\!\!out}}(p):=\sigma_{K_{\!1\!\times\!1}}(p)\circ f_{\textup{\;\!\!in}}(p)
.
By definition, both trivialize in an arbitrarily chosen gauge
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{\!Hom}}^{A}
to
f_{\textup{\>\!\!out}}^{A}(p)=K_{\!1\!\times\!1}f_{\textup{\;\!\!in}}^{A}(p)
.
The
G\mkern-1.4muM
-coordinate independence of this definition is guaranteed by the intertwining property of the kernel in Eq. (
226
) or, equivalently, Eq. (
237
).
This can be seen by considering a different trivialization via
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{\!Hom}}^{B}
:

\displaystyle K_{\!1\!\times\!1}f_{\textup{\;\!\!in}}^{B}(p)\

\displaystyle=\ K_{\!1\!\times\!1}\left(\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g^{BA}_{p}\big)f_{\textup{\;\!\!in}}^{A}(p)\right)

\displaystyle=\ \rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}\big(g^{BA}_{p}\big)K_{\!1\!\times\!1}f_{\textup{\;\!\!in}}^{A}(p)

\displaystyle=\ \rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}\big(g^{BA}_{p}\big)f_{\textup{\>\!\!out}}^{A}(p)

\displaystyle=\ f_{\textup{\>\!\!out}}^{B}(p)

(238)

7.2
Kernel field transforms and
GM
-convolutions

We now turn to kernel field transforms and
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions with spatially extended (convolution) kernels.
Section
7.2.1
introduces general, unconstrained kernel fields and more specific
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutional kernel fields, which are defined in terms of a shared,
G
-steerable template kernel.
General kernel field transforms and
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions are introduced in Section
7.2.2
.
As both are defined
globally
, their formulation is necessarily
coordinate free
.
Section
7.2.3
expresses both operations relative to local trivializations, recovering our local definitions from Section
4.2
.

7.2.1
Coordinate free kernels fields and
G
-steerable kernels

To detect spatial pattens in feature fields, convolutional networks apply spatially extended kernels which linearly accumulate features from a local neighborhood around each point.
In Eq. (
70
) we defined (unconstrained) template kernels for a
d
-dimensional manifold and
{c_{\textup{in}}}
- and
{c_{\textup{out}}}
-dimensional input and output feature fields as maps

K:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}\times{c_{\textup{in}}}}

which assign a
{c_{\textup{out}}}\times{c_{\textup{in}}}
matrix to each point of their domain.
The definition of convolution kernels as maps with domain
\mathbb{R}^{d}\cong T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
and codomain
\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}\times{c_{\textup{in}}}}\cong\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in},p},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out},p})
suggests a coordinate free definition of kernels
as maps between the tangent spaces and the corresponding homomorphism spaces:

Definition 7.2
(Kernel field).

We define (unconstrained)
kernel fields
of type
\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}},\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}
on a manifold
M
as smooth bundle
M
-morphisms between the tangent bundle
T\mkern-1.5muM
and the feature vector homomorphism bundle
\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})
.
By its definition as an
M
-morphism, a kernel field
\mathcal{K}
lets the following diagram commute:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces T\mkern-1.5muM}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mkern-3.0mu\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces M}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{K}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ \!Hom}}}}

(239)

Despite smoothly mapping between two vector bundles,
\mathcal{K}
is
not
assumed to be a
vector
bundle morphism, that is, the restrictions
\mathcal{K}_{p}:T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM\to\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in},p},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out},p})
are not assumed to be linear.
62
62

62

This reflects that convolution kernels are in general not linear as maps
K:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}\times{c_{\textup{in}}}}
.
Note that this does not interfere with the linearity of
K({v})\in\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}\times{c_{\textup{in}}}}
(as map
\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{in}}}}\to\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}}
) for any
{v}\in\mathbb{R}
or, here, the linearity of
\mathcal{K}_{p}(v)\in\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in},p},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out},p})
(as map
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in},p}\to\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out},p}
) for any
v\in T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
.

The name
kernel field
is motivated by the fact that such defined bundle maps
\mathcal{K}
assign a (potentially different) coordinate free kernel
\mathcal{K}_{p}:T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM\to\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in},p},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out},p})
to each point
p
of the manifold.
63
63

63

We expect that it is possible to work out a well defined notion of
kernel bundles
whose sections are in one to one correspondence to our definition of kernel fields as bundle maps (this reformulation would mirror the transition from Eq. (
219
) to Eq. (
235
)).

In practice, kernels
\mathcal{K}_{p}
are often designed to detect local patterns around
p
and are therefore assumed to be compactly supported around the origin of
T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
.

A coordinate free kernel
\mathcal{K}_{p}
at
p
is relative to gauges
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}
and
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}
of the
G
-atlases given by the map

\displaystyle\mathcal{K}_{p}^{A}:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}\times{c_{\textup{in}}}},\qquad\mathcal{K}_{p}^{A}\>:=\>\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\circ\mathcal{K}_{p}\circ\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big)^{-1}\,.

(240)

Fig.
23
visualizes a coordinate free kernel on
T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
and its coordinatizations on
\mathbb{R}^{d}
relative to different gauges.
From the commutative diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{R}^{d}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}\times{c_{\textup{in}}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Hom\!\big(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}|_{p},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}}|_{p}\big)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{R}^{d}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}\times{c_{\textup{in}}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{K}_{p}^{A}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces g_{p}^{BA}\cdot}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{{Hom}}}}\big(g_{p}^{BA}\big)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{K}_{p}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{B}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{B}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{K}_{p}^{B}}

(241)

it follows that different kernel coordinatizations are related by

\displaystyle\mathcal{K}_{p}^{B}\ =\ \rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{{Hom}}}}\big(g_{p}^{BA}\big)\circ\mathcal{K}_{p}^{A}\circ\big(g_{p}^{BA}\big)^{-1}\,.

(242)

Note that this relation only implies
G\mkern-1.4muM
-coordinate independence but does not constrain the coordinate free kernel in any way.
As before, the situation changes when sharing weights over spatial positions.

In order for a kernel field
\mathcal{K}_{\mkern-2.0muK}
to correspond to a convolution, it needs to be fully specified by a single template kernel
K:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}\times{c_{\textup{in}}}}
which is shared over all spatial positions.
We are again forced to share weights with all gauges
X\in\mathfrak{X}
simultaneously in order to preserve their equivalence and thus
G\mkern-1.4muM
-coordinate independence.
As argued in Section
4.2.3
, the appropriate way of sharing
K
with kernel coordinatizations
\mathcal{K}_{\mkern-2.0muK\mkern-2.0mu,p}^{X}
involves a normalization by the reference frame volume
\sqrt{|\eta_{p}^{X}|}
and is defined by

\displaystyle\mathcal{K}_{\mkern-2.0muK\mkern-2.0mu,p}^{X}\ =\ \frac{K}{\sqrt{|\eta_{p}^{X}|}}\qquad\textup{for \emph{any} gauge}\,\ X\in\mathfrak{X}\,\ \textup{with}\,\ p\in U^{X}\,.

(243)

The reason for the frame normalization factor is that convolutions will later be defined in terms of integrals over the tangent spaces.
We are therefore actually required to share the integral operator itself in different coordinatizations,
which is equivalent to identifying the matrix-valued integration measures
\mathcal{K}_{\mkern-2.0muK\mkern-2.0mu,p}^{X}({v})\,\sqrt{|\eta_{p}^{X}|}\;d{v}
for any gauge
X\in\mathfrak{X}
at
p\in M
with a template measure
K({v})\,d{v}
.
The form of the kernel sharing in Eq. (
243
) follows by equating both expressions.

Together with the relation
\sqrt{|\eta_{p}^{A}|}=\big|\!\det(g_{p}^{BA})\big|\mkern 1.5mu\sqrt{|\eta_{p}^{B}|}
between different frame volumes, the kernel transformation law in Eq. (
242
) and the weight sharing in Eq. (
243
) imply the
G
-steerability kernel constraint

\displaystyle\frac{1}{|\mkern-2.0mu\det g\mkern 1.0mu|}\,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{{Hom}}}}(g)\circ K\circ g^{-1}\ =\ K\qquad\forall\>g\in G\,.

(244)

Valid template kernels are thus given by the invariants under the simultaneous gauge action of
|\mkern-2.0mu\det g\mkern 1.0mu|^{-1}
,
\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{{Hom}}}}(g)
and
g^{-1}
.
Writing out the representation
\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{{Hom}}}}
, acting on
\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}\times{c_{\textup{in}}}}
via multiplication with
\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}
and
\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}^{-1}
from the left and right, respectively, the constraint in Eq. (
244
) is seen to be equivalent to that in Eq. (
83
), i.e.

K(g\mkern 1.0mu{v})=|\mkern-2.0mu\det g\mkern 1.0mu|^{-1}\rho_{\text{out}}(g)\,K({v})\,\rho_{\text{in}}(g)^{-1}\ \ \forall\,g\in G,\ {v}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}
.

We cast these insights into definitions:

Definition 7.3
(
G
-steerable kernel).

G
-steerable kernels are characterized by their
invariance under the gauge action
.
The vector space of smooth
G
-steerable kernels that map between field types
\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}
and
\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}
is defined by

\displaystyle{K}^{G}_{\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\mkern-1.0mu,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}}\!:=

\displaystyle\,\Big\{K\!:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}\times{c_{\textup{in}}}}\ \text{smooth}\,\Big|\,\frac{1}{|\mkern-2.0mu\det g\mkern 1.0mu|}\,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{{Hom}}}}(g)\circ K\circ g^{-1}=\,K\ \ \ \forall g\in G\Big\}\,,

(245)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\ \Big\{K\!:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}\times{c_{\textup{in}}}}\ \text{smooth}\,\Big|\,\frac{1}{|\mkern-2.0mu\det g\mkern 1.0mu|}\mkern 1.0mu\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}(g)K(g^{-1}{v})\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}(g)^{-1}\mkern-2.0mu=K({v})\ \ \ \forall\,g\in G,\ {v}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}\Big\},

(246)

where
\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{{Hom}}}}(g)H:=\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}(g)H\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}(g)^{-1}
for any
H\in\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}\times{c_{\textup{in}}}}
and
G\leq\operatorname{GL}(d)
.
The gauge invariance of
G
-steerable kernels allows for
G\mkern-1.4muM
-coordinate independent weight sharing.

G
-steerable kernels were in
[
34
]
introduced to equivariant deep learning, where finite groups were assumed.
The current formulation in Def.
7.3
was proposed in
[
235
]
.
A complete solution for the
G
-steerable kernel spaces for arbitrary representations
\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}
and
\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}
of structure groups
G\leq\operatorname{O}(2)
has been derived in
[
234
]
, an implementation is publicly available at
https://quva-lab.github.io/e2cnn/api/e2cnn.kernels.html
.
Mathematically, steerable kernel are equivalent to
representation operators
like for instance the spherical tensor operators from quantum mechanics.
A generalization of the
Wigner-Eckart theorem
describes
G
-steerable kernels as being composed from harmonic basis functions, Clebsch-Gordan coefficients and endomorphisms of irreducible representations
[
128
]
.

Definition 7.4
(
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutional kernel field).

A
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutional kernel field

\mathcal{K}_{\mkern-2.0muK}
of type
\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}},\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}
is a kernel field which is determined by a shared,
G
-steerable
template kernel
K\in{K}^{G}_{\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\mkern-1.0mu,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}}
.
It is in
arbitrary gauges

\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{X}
and
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{X}\,
from the considered
G
-atlas pointwise defined by:

\displaystyle\mathcal{K}_{\mkern-2.0muK\mkern-2.0mu,p}\,:=\ \big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{X}\big)^{\mkern-2.0mu-1}\circ\frac{K}{\sqrt{|\eta_{p}^{X}|}}\circ\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{X}

(247)

The smoothness of
\mathcal{K}_{\mkern-2.0muK}
follows from the smoothness of the gauges, the metric and the template kernel.

As in the case of
{1\kern-2.65pt\times\kern-3.0pt1}

G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions
, the arbitrariness of the particular choice of gauge in Eq. (
247
) – and therefore the
G\mkern-1.4muM
-coordinate independence of the definition – is guaranteed by the
G
-steerability of
K\in{K}^{G}_{\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\mkern-1.0mu,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}}\!
.
To show this explicitly, one may define the kernel field relative to some gauge
B
and then apply a transformation to any other gauge
A
, which cancels out and therefore leads to an equivalent expression:

\displaystyle\mathcal{K}_{\mkern-2.0muK\mkern-2.0mu,p}\,\ =

\displaystyle\,\ \big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{B}\big)^{-1}\,\circ\,\frac{K}{\sqrt{|\eta^{B}|}}\circ\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{B}

\displaystyle\,\ =

\displaystyle\,\ \big(\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{{Hom}}}}\big(g_{p}^{BA}\big)\,\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big)^{-1}\,\circ\,\frac{K}{\sqrt{|\eta^{A}|}\,/\,|\!\det(g_{p}^{BA})|}\circ\big(g_{p}^{BA}\cdot\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big)

\displaystyle\,\ =

\displaystyle\,\ \big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big)^{-1}\,\circ\frac{\,\big|\!\det(g_{p}^{BA})\big|\,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{{Hom}}}}\big(g_{p}^{BA}\big)^{-1}\circ K\circ g_{p}^{BA}}{\sqrt{|\eta^{A}|}}\circ\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}

\displaystyle\,\ =

\displaystyle\,\ \big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}\big)^{-1}\,\circ\,\frac{K}{\sqrt{|\eta^{A}|}}\circ\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{A}

(248)

Fig.
37
gives an overview of the local trivializations of
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutional kernel fields in terms of a commutative diagram.

.
Convolutional weight sharing requires the coordinate expression of the kernel field
\mathcal{K}_{\mkern-2.0muK}
at any point

and any gauge

to be determined by the shared template kernel
{K:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}\times{c_{\textup{in}}}}}
as

\mathcal{K}_{\mkern-2.0muK\mkern-2.0mu,p}^{X}=K/\sqrt{|\eta_{p}^{X}|}
.
The commutativity of the diagram then implies the
G
-steerability constraint
{|\mkern-2.0mu\det g\mkern 1.0mu|^{-1}\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{{Hom}}}}(g)\circ K\circ g^{-1}=K}\ \ \forall g\in G
on the space
{K}^{G}_{\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\mkern-1.0mu,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}}
of template kernels.
We want to emphasize that, despite looking similar to the diagram in Fig.
35
, the diagram in the current figure should be seen as analog to that in Fig.
36(b)
.
The difference between the current diagram and that in Fig.
36(b)
is that the linear maps in the homomorphism bundle are via
\mathcal{K}_{\mkern-2.0muK}:T\mkern-1.5muM\to\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})
determined by an element of the tangent bundle
T\mkern-1.5muM
instead of the section
\sigma_{K_{1\!\times\!1}}:M\to\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})
.

Note that the
G
-steerability constraint in Eq. (
246
) or (
245
) reduces to the constraint on
{1\kern-2.65pt\times\kern-3.0pt1}

G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolution
kernels in Eq. (
226
) or (
237
) when being evaluated at the origin
{v}=0
of
\mathbb{R}^{d}
, which is invariant under the action of any
g\in G
.
The results on
{1\kern-2.65pt\times\kern-3.0pt1}

G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions
, derived in the previous section, are therefore seen to be a special case for the choice of point-like kernels.
64
64

64

To make this statement precise, one would have to generalize Def.
7.3
to operator-valued distributions and define
{1\kern-2.65pt\times\kern-3.0pt1}

G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolution
kernels as operator-valued Dirac deltas.
We omit this generalization here for brevity.

We further want to mention that the constraint on spatially extended kernels does in general not require their codomain to be restricted to
\Hom_{G}(\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}},\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}})
, i.e. the space of intertwiners.
In contrast to
{1\kern-2.65pt\times\kern-3.0pt1}

G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions
, this allows
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions with spatially extended kernels to map between fields that transform according to non-isomorphic irreducible representations.

7.2.2
Kernel field transforms and
GM
-convolutions

Having defined both feature fields and kernel fields, we are ready to introduce kernel field transforms and
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions.
They are pointwise defined in terms of integral operators which compute output feature vectors
f_{\textup{\>\!\!out}}(p)
at points
p\in M
by matching the kernel
\mathcal{K}_{p}
at
p
with the feature field
f_{\textup{\;\!\!in}}
“as seen from
p
”.

The local representation of an input field “as seen from
p
” is formally given by its
transporter pullback
, which is visualized in Fig.
22
.
It is defined as the usual pullback from
M
to
T\mkern-1.5muM
via the Riemannian exponential map
65
65

65

We define the exponential map on the full tangent bundle as

\exp:T\mkern-1.5muM\!\to M,\ \ v\mapsto\exp_{\scalebox{.85}{$\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$T\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\mkern-1.0mu(v)$}}(v)
.
Recall that we assumed the manifold to be geodesically complete, such that the exponential map is well defined on the whole tangent bundle (and resort to zero-padding if this assumption fails to hold).

with the additional application of a parallel transporter (Eq. (
214
)), which is necessary in order to express the pulled back features in
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in},\exp(v)}
as features in
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in},p}
.
Denoting this parallel transporter along the geodesic path
\gamma_{v}(t):=\exp((1-t)\,v)
between
\gamma(0)=\exp(v)
and
\gamma(1)=\pi(v)=:p
by

\displaystyle\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.75}{$\!\mathcal{A}$},\scalebox{.75}{$\,p\!\leftarrow\!\exp(v)$}}}:\mathcal{A}_{\exp(v)}\to\mathcal{A}_{p}\,,

(249)

we thus define the pulled back feature field representations on the tangent spaces as follows:

Definition 7.5
(Transporter pullback of feature field to
TM
).

Given a feature field
f\in\Gamma(\mathcal{A})
, we define its (redundant) representation on the tangent bundle as

\displaystyle\operatorname{Exp}^{*}\mkern-5.0muf:\ T\mkern-1.5muM\to\mathcal{A},\quad\ v\,\mapsto\,\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.75}{$\!\mathcal{A}$},\scalebox{.7}{$\mkern 1.0mu\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}(v)\!\leftarrow\!\exp(v)$}}}\!\circ f\circ\exp(v)\,.

(250)

The Riemannian exponential map
\exp
corresponds hereby to the Levi-Civita connection, while the transporter
\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.75}{$\!\mathcal{A}$},\scalebox{.7}{$\mkern 1.0mu\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}(v)\!\leftarrow\!\exp(v)$}}}
relies on some
G
-compatible connection; see Sections
3.3
and
6.5
.

From the construction it is clear that
\operatorname{Exp}^{*}\mkern-5.0muf(v)\in\mathcal{A}_{p}\,
for any
v\in T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
, that is,
\operatorname{Exp}^{*}\mkern-5.0muf
is a bundle
M
-morphism, satisfying the following commutative diagram:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces T\mkern-1.5muM}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mkern-3.0mu\mathcal{A}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces M}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{Exp}^{*}\mkern-5.0muf}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!\!\mathcal{A}$}}}}

(251)

Despite smoothly mapping between two vector bundles,
\operatorname{Exp}^{*}\mkern-5.0muf
is
not
assumed to be a
vector
bundle morphism, that is, the restrictions
\operatorname{Exp}^{*}_{p}\mkern-2.0muf:T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM\to\mathcal{A}_{p}
are usually not linear.

The restriction
\operatorname{Exp}^{*}_{p}\mkern-2.0muf:=\operatorname{Exp}^{*}\mkern-5.0muf\big|_{T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM}
of the transporter pullback’s domain to
T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
captures the feature field from the perspective of an observer at
p
as shown in Fig.
22
.
Note that this definition resembles a local representation of the feature field in terms of
geodesic normal coordinates
, with the difference that it is not restricted to the injectivity radius of the exponential map.
66
66

66

Any feature vector
f(q)
might therefore be represented multiple times on the same tangent space
T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
, once for each
v\in T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
with
\exp(v)=q
.
If this is not desired, one may restrict the kernel support to the injectivity radius of the exponential map, such that only the geodesically nearest occurrence will be measured.

We furthermore want to mention that the transporter may be replaced with any other isomorphism between
\mathcal{A}_{\exp(v)}
and
\mathcal{A}_{p}
, as done for instance in
[
211
]
.

As stated before, kernel field transforms and
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions are defined as matching the local feature field representations on the tangent spaces with kernels.
Working towards these definitions, note that the bundle
M
-morphisms of kernels
\mathcal{K}:T\mkern-1.5muM\to\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})
and local field representations
\operatorname{Exp}^{*}\mkern-5.0muf_{\textup{\;\!\!in}}:T\mkern-1.5muM\to\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}
, can be combined to yet another (nonlinear)
M
-morphism from
T\mkern-1.5muM
to
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}}
,

(252)

where
\operatorname{ev}:\big(\mathcal{K}(v),\,\operatorname{Exp}^{*}\mkern-5.0muf_{\textup{\;\!\!in}}(v)\big)\mapsto\mathcal{K}(v)\operatorname{Exp}^{*}\mkern-5.0muf_{\textup{\;\!\!in}}(v)
is the evaluation map on
\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})\!\times\!\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}
.
Kernel field transforms compute output feature vectors at
p
by integrating this product of kernels and input fields over the respective tangent space
T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
:

Definition 7.6
(Kernel field transform).

Let
\mathcal{K}
be any smooth kernel field.
The corresponding
kernel field transform
is a smooth integral transform

\displaystyle{T}_{\overset{}{\mkern 0.0mu\mathcal{K}}}:\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}})\to\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})

(253)

which is pointwise defined by
67
67

67

The integration over
T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
via the Riemannian volume density
dv
is discussed in Appendix
C
.

\displaystyle\big[{T}_{\overset{}{\mkern 0.0mu\mathcal{K}}}(f_{\textup{\;\!\!in}})\big](p)\,\ :=\,\int\limits_{T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM}\!\!\mathcal{K}(v)\,\operatorname{Exp}^{*}\mkern-5.0muf_{\textup{\;\!\!in}}(v)\ dv\,\ =\,\int\limits_{T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM}\!\!\mathcal{K}(v)\ \mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.75}{$\!\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}$},\scalebox{.7}{$p\!\leftarrow\!\exp_{p}\!v$}}}\;f_{\textup{\;\!\!in}}(\exp_{p}\!v)\ dv\,.

(254)

In order to be well defined, the integral needs to exist and the resulting output field
{T}_{\overset{}{\mkern 0.0mu\mathcal{K}}}(f)
needs to be smooth.
This requires
\mathcal{K}
to be chosen suitably, e.g. by assuming it to decay rapidly or to be compactly supported.

Note that general kernel field transforms do not necessarily model convolutions as they do not assume weights (kernels) to be shared between spatial positions.
Such general kernel field transforms will become handy in Section
8
, where we derive a requirement for spatial weight sharing from the requirement for isometry equivariance.

Appendix
G
discusses the existence and smoothness of kernel field transforms.
A sufficient condition for kernel field transforms to be well defined is the restriction of kernel supports to balls of a fixed radius
R>0
:

Theorem 7.7
(Kernel field transform existence for compactly supported kernels).

Let
\mathcal{K}
be a kernel field whose individual kernels
\mathcal{K}_{p}
at any
p\in M
are (at most) supported on a closed ball of radius
R>0
around the origin of
T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
, that is,

\displaystyle\supp\!\big(\mathcal{K}_{p}\big)\ \subseteq\ \big\{v\in T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM\,\big|\,\lVert v\rVert\leq R\big\}\quad\forall p\in M\,.

(255)

The corresponding kernel field transform
{T}_{\overset{}{\mkern 0.0mu\mathcal{K}}}
is then guaranteed to be well defined, i.e. the integral in Eq. (
254
) exists and the output field
{T}_{\overset{}{\mkern 0.0mu\mathcal{K}}}(f)\in\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})
is smooth for any smooth input field
f\in\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}})
.

Proof
:

The requirement to restrict the kernel support to a closed ball of certain radius is common practice in deep learning.
Note, however, that a compactly supported kernel is at odds with scale equivariant convolutions, which, by the corresponding
G
-steerability kernel constraints, require infinitely far extending kernels.
Current implementations of scale equivariant convolutions usually approximate scale equivariant kernel spaces by restricting their support
[

243

77

and are therefore covered by Theorem
7.7
.

Based on general kernel field transforms, we define
coordinate free
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions
by adding the assumption of spatial weight sharing, i.e. by assuming
G\mkern-1.4muM
-

:

(

Let
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}
and

and

-convolution

-

\displaystyle K\,\star\,:\,\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}})\to\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}}),\quad f_{\textup{\;\!\!in}}\mapsto K\star f_{\textup{\;\!\!in}}\,:=\,{T}_{\overset{}{\mkern 0.0mu\mathcal{K}_{\mkern-2.0muK}}}(f_{\textup{\;\!\!in}})\,=\!\int\limits_{T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM}\!\mathcal{K}_{\mkern-2.0muK}(v)\ \operatorname{Exp}^{*}\mkern-5.0muf_{\textup{\;\!\!in}}(v)\ dv

(256)

Theorem 7.10

Proof

by observing that the coordinate free

.
Specifically, the coordinate expression of a

This result assures that a global, coordinate free
