8
Isometry equivariance

A main characteristic of the convolution operation and its various generalizations is their equivariance w.r.t. symmetries of the underlying manifold.
For instance, the conventional convolution on Euclidean spaces is translation equivariant while spherical convolutions are rotation equivariant.
More generally, any locally compact group and their homogeneous spaces admit group convolutions
[
84
,
123
,
31
,
75
]
,
which were recently picked up by the deep learning community to generalize convolutional networks to such spaces
[
33
,
121
,
37
,
7
]
.
However, as these approaches rely fundamentally on the global,
transitive
symmetries of the homogeneous space, they do not immediately apply to general Riemannian manifolds.

G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions on the other hand shift the focus from
global symmetries of the space itself
to
local symmetries in the coordinatization of the space
.
As it turns out, the local gauge equivariance of
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions, together with convolutional weight sharing, induces their equivariance under
the action of global symmetries.

Stated more precisely,
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions are equivariant under the action of
G
-structure preserving isometries
(Def.
8.1
), which form a subgroup
\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}\leq\Isom(\mkern-1.5muM\mkern-0.5mu)
of the full isometry group.
The requirement on the symmetry to be an isometry (i.e. to preserve the metric) comes hereby from the use of exponential maps, which rely on the Levi-Civita connection and thus Riemannian metric.
The additional requirement on these isometries to preserve the
G
-structure is a consequence of the definition of feature vector bundles as associated
G
-bundles, whose elements have a well defined meaning only relative to those reference frames that are contained in
G\mkern-1.4muM
.
Note that the latter is not really a restriction, as one may always choose structure groups
G\geq\operatorname{O}(d)
, for which
any
isometry respects the corresponding
G
-structure.
On the contrary, this design allows for a precise control of the level of isometry equivariance.
For instance, the conventional convolution on Euclidean vector spaces relies on the canonical
\{e\}
-structure of
\mathbb{R}^{d}
, visualized in Fig.
40(a)
, and is therefore solely translation equivariant.
An
\operatorname{SO}(d)
-structure on
\mathbb{R}^{d}
, visualized in Fig.
41(a)
, is additionally preserved by rotations, and thus corresponds to
\operatorname{SE}(d)
-equivariant convolutions.
Equivariance under the full isometry group
\operatorname{E}(d)
of
\mathbb{R}^{d}
is implied when choosing an
\operatorname{O}(d)
-structure on
\mathbb{R}^{d}
.

The goal of this section is to derive theorems which formally characterize the isometry equivariance of
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions and kernel field transforms.
Section
8.1
lays the foundations of this investigation by introducing isometry groups of Riemannian manifolds and discussing a range of well known relation and constructions which they induce.
Specifically, Section
8.1.1
introduces isometries and isometry groups while Section
8.1.2
defines their induced action (“pushforwards”) on the associated bundles in a coordinate free setting.
In Section
8.1.3
we express these actions on bundles relative to local trivializations and discuss their passive interpretation as isometry induced gauge transformations, visualized in Figs.
10
(right) and
21
.
Section
8.1.4
briefly states how the quantities involved in kernel field transforms behave under the action of isometries.

Based on these properties, we study the isometry equivariance of kernel field transforms and
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions in Section
8.2
.
After defining the term “isometry equivariance” formally, Section
8.2.1
proves a central result, which asserts that the demand for
isometry equivariance requires the invariance of the kernel field under isometries
; see Fig.
43
.
Section
8.2.2
considers the more specific
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions and proves that they are by design equivariant under any isometry that preserves the
G
-structure.
This result implies in particular, that
\operatorname{O}\mkern-3.6muM
-convolutions are equivariant w.r.t. any isometry.

The invariance constraint on kernel fields enforces that they share weights over the orbits of the isometry group.
This suggests that invariant kernel fields can equivalently be described by representative kernels on orbit representatives, which we formalize in Section
8.3
.
Section
8.3.1
discussed isometry induced quotient spaces and their representatives.
In Section
8.3.2
we use these mathematical definitions to prove that the space of isometry invariant kernel fields is indeed isomorphic to kernel fields on quotient representatives.
This implies in particular that isometry equivariant kernel field transforms on homogeneous spaces are necessarily convolutions, which closes the loop to prior work.

8.1
Isometries and their action on manifolds, bundles and fields

(a)
Action of different subgroups of the isometry group on fields.

(b)
Orbits of the isometry group.

Figure 38:
Visualizations of the isometry group
\Isom(\mkern-1.5muM\mkern-0.5mu)\cong\operatorname{O}(2)
of an egg
M
, which we will use throughout this section to exemplify different concepts and constructions relating to isometries.
Fig.
38(a)
shows the action of the isometry group on (tangent or feature) vector fields.
It can be thought of as consisting of the subgroups of rotations in
\operatorname{SO}(2)
and reflections in
{R}
.
The action of the isometry group partitions the egg into orbits
\Isom(\mkern-1.5muM\mkern-0.5mu).p=\big\{\phi(p)\,\big|\,\phi\in\Isom(\mkern-1.5muM\mkern-0.5mu)\big\}
of points
p\in M
, shown in Fig.
38(b)
in different colors.
Note that not all orbits are homeomorphic to each other – the orbits at the poles are single points while any other orbit traces out a circle around the egg.
The isometry group of the egg acts non-transitively on it, that is, not every point can be reached from any other point.
A kernel field transform is isometry equivariant if it commutes with the isometry action on feature fields.
We show that isometry equivariance is guaranteed if and only if the kernel field is invariant under the action of isometries.
This implies in particular that isometry equivariance require weight sharing along the isometry orbits; see Fig.
43
.

In this section we introduce most of the mathematical concepts required for our study of the isometry equivariance of kernel field transforms and
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions.
After defining isometries in Section
8.1.1
, we discuss in Section
8.1.2
how they induce natural actions on tangent vectors and reference frames.
For structure groups
G<\operatorname{O}(d)
, not any isometry is compatible with any
G
-structure.
We define the subgroup
\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}\leq\Isom(\mkern-1.5muM\mkern-0.5mu)
of those isometries which do act on (induce automorphisms of) a
G
-structure
G\mkern-1.4muM
and their
G
-associated feature bundles.
While these constructions are kept coordinate free, Section
8.1.3
expresses the action of isometries on fiber bundles relative to local bundle trivializations.
In preparation for our investigation of isometry equivariant kernel field transforms later on, Section
8.1.4
discusses how isometries commute with the exponential map and with parallel transporters, which allows to derive how isometries act on the transporter pullback
\operatorname{Exp}^{*}_{p}\mkern-2.0muf
of feature fields
f
.
While staying mostly mathematical, we try to draw connections to the application wherever possible.

8.1.1
Isometry groups

A (global)
isometry

\phi:M\to\hat{M}
is a diffeomorphism between Riemannian manifolds
(M,\eta)
and
(\hat{M},\hat{\eta})
, which
preserves the metric
.
In terms of the pushforward (differential)
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}:T\mkern-1.5muM\to T\mkern-1.5mu\hat{M}
of tangent vectors, which we introduce in Appendix
A.2
and in Section
8.1.2
below, this statement is made precise by requiring that isometries satisfy

\displaystyle\eta_{p}(v,\,w)\ =\ \hat{\eta}_{\phi(p)}(\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}v,\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}w)\qquad\forall\ \ p\in M,\,\ v,w\in T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM\,,

(264)

i.e. that they preserve distances and angles between tangent vectors.
Intuitively, an isometry is thought of as a distance preserving map between manifolds.
Note that the inverse of an isometry is necessarily an isometry as well.
Since isometries (and their inverses) respect the metric, they constitute the
isomorphisms in the category of Riemannian manifolds
.

The set of all isometries
\phi:M\to M
from a Riemannian manifold to itself, equipped with the usual function composition
\circ:(\phi_{1},\phi_{2})\mapsto\phi_{1}\circ\phi_{2}
, defines a group, known as
isometry group

\Isom(\mkern-1.5muM\mkern-0.5mu)
of
M
.
This group is the automorphism group of a Riemannian manifold, which contains all of its (metric) “symmetries”.
It is a subgroup of the diffeomorphism group
\Diff(M)
of
M
.
The full isometry group might have non-trivial subgroups, which we will in the following denote by
\mathcal{I}\leq\Isom(\mkern-1.5muM\mkern-0.5mu)
.
An example is given in Fig.
38(a)
, which visualizes the isometry group
\Isom(\mkern-1.5muM\mkern-0.5mu)\cong\operatorname{O}(2)
of an egg.
The full isometry group splits (for instance) into the subgroups of rotations in
\mathcal{I}_{1}\cong\operatorname{SO}(2)
and reflections in
\mathcal{I}_{2}\cong{R}
.

In general, the isometry group of a manifold is non-transitive, that is, not every point of
M
can be reached from any other point by its action.
The manifold is then partitioned into disjoint
orbits
, visualized for the example of
M
being an (Easter) egg in Fig.
38(b)
.
The isometry group of a manifold
M
might be trivial, given that
M
is sufficiently asymmetric.
In this case there might still exist non-trivial isometries between open subsets
U^{\widetilde{A}}
and
U^{A}
of
M
, restricted to which Eq. (
264
) holds.
Fig.
39
shows an example of a manifold which is globally asymmetric but has non-trivial isometries between local subsets of itself.
We will in the following only consider global isometries of
M
, however, all concepts of the current Section
8.1
generalize in an obvious way to isometries between local subsets.
Without proof, we claim that the same holds for the isometry equivariance of any neural network operation which acts pointwise, for instance
{1\kern-2.65pt\times\kern-3.0pt1}
-convolutions
, nonlinearities or bias summation.
The equivariance of kernel field transforms with spatially extended kernels holds up to boundary effects.

Figure 39:
An asymmetric manifold, whose
global
isometry group is trivial.
Since the asymmetry is limited to the ears and the mouth of
“
Suzanne
”,
the monkey, there are non-trivial localized symmetries left.
For instance, the smooth map
{\phi:U^{\widetilde{A}}\to U^{A}}
between the red and green highlighted subsets preserves the metric locally.
All concepts developed in Section
8.1
as well as the isometry equivariance of point-wise operations like
{1\kern-2.65pt\times\kern-3.0pt1}
-convolutions
generalize immediately to such isometries between local subsets.
The isometry equivariance of kernel field transforms with spatially extended kernels generalizes up to boundary effects.

8.1.2
Isometry action on fiber bundles

Isometries act naturally on tangent vectors in
T\mkern-1.5muM
and reference frames in
F\mkern-1.5muM
by “carrying them along” with the group action as visualized in Fig.
38(a)
.
If an isometry is in addition compatible with the
G
-structure, that is, if it gives rise to an automorphism of
G\mkern-1.4muM
, it furthermore acts on any associated
G
-bundle, in particular the feature vector bundles
\mathcal{A}
.
We discuss these actions of isometries on the associated bundles and on feature fields in the following.

Isometry action on the tangent bundle
TM
:

Any isometry
\phi\in\Isom(\mkern-1.5muM\mkern-0.5mu)
gives rise to a
pushforward

\displaystyle\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}:T\mkern-1.5muM\to T\mkern-1.5muM\,,\qquad\phi\in\Isom(\mkern-1.5muM\mkern-0.5mu)

(265)

on the tangent bundle, which is just the differential of
\phi
as introduced in Appendix
A.2
.
It can at each point
p\in M
be thought of as a
linear
approximation of
\phi
, which maps vectors
v\in T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
to
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}(v)\in T_{\mkern-1.0mu\phi(p)}\mkern-2.0muM
, that is, it satisfies

\displaystyle\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}\circ\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}\,=\,\phi\circ\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}.

(266)

As argued in Appendix
A.2
, the pushforward is invertible with
(\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}})^{-1}=(\phi^{-1})_{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}
, for which we will unambiguously write
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}
.
69
69

69

The invertibility does not hold for pushforwards in general but only for those of diffeomorphisms and thus isometries.

The pushforward of an element
\phi
of the isometry group is therefore seen to be an (isometric) vector bundle automorphism of
T\mkern-1.5muM
over
\phi
, satisfying the following commutative diagram:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces T\mkern-1.5muM}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}}

By the

(268)

More details about pushforwards between tangent bundles are easily found in the literature, for instance in

Isometry action on the frame bundle
FM

The pushforward on
T\mkern-1.5muM
immediately induces a corresponding principal bundle automorphism
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}
on
F\mkern-1.5muM
by pushing forward the individual frame vectors:

\displaystyle\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\!:F\mkern-1.5muM\to F\mkern-1.5muM,\ \ \ [e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\mapsto\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\big):=\big[\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}(e_{i})\big]_{i=1}^{d}\,,\qquad\phi\in\Isom(\mkern-1.5muM\mkern-0.5mu)

(269)

It maps frames in
F_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-1.0muM
for arbitrary
p\in M
to frames at
F_{\mkern-1.0mu\phi(p)}\mkern-2.0muM

\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!F\!M$}}}\circ\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}=\phi\circ\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!F\!M$}}}
.
To see this, let

\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!F\!M$}}}\circ\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\big)=\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!F\!M$}}}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big($}}}}}\big[\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}(e_{i})\big]_{i=1}^{d}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}=\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}\circ\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}(e_{j})=\phi\circ\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}(e_{j})=\phi(p)

for any
j=1,\dots,d
.
It can further be checked to be invertible with

(\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}})^{-1}=(\phi^{-1})_{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-3.0muM$}}

again abbreviated by
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}^{-1}
.
The
left action
of the

Isometry action on

As

Two specific choices of

.
The full isometry group of

.
In contrast, rotations or reflections map frames in

to frames in
F_{\mkern-1.6mu\phi(p)}\mkern-1.3muM
but fail to send them to
\raisebox{0.2pt}{$\raisebox{0.4pt}{\scalebox{.8}{$\{$}}\mkern-1.5mue\mkern-0.9mu\raisebox{0.4pt}{\scalebox{.8}{$\}$}}$}_{\mkern-1.2mu\phi(p)}\mkern-1.2muM
.
They do therefore not induce automorphisms of the
\{e\}
-structure and are not part of
\Isom_{\scalebox{.85}{$\raisebox{0.2pt}{$\raisebox{0.5pt}{\scalebox{.75}{$\{$}}\mkern-1.3mue\mkern-1.1mu\raisebox{0.5pt}{\scalebox{.75}{$\}$}}$}\mkern-2.0muM$}}
.
Group actions of such isometries on
\raisebox{0.2pt}{$\raisebox{0.4pt}{\scalebox{.8}{$\{$}}\mkern-1.5mue\mkern-0.9mu\raisebox{0.4pt}{\scalebox{.8}{$\}$}}$}\mkern-2.0muM
or any of its
\{e\}
-associated bundles
are not defined
.
Fig.
40(b)
shows an alternative choice of
\{e\}
-structure on

(or
M=\mathbb{E}_{2}
), which is only invariant under translations in the “up-down” direction, i.e.
\Isom_{\scalebox{.85}{$\raisebox{0.2pt}{$\raisebox{0.5pt}{\scalebox{.75}{$\{$}}\mkern-1.3mue\mkern-1.1mu\raisebox{0.5pt}{\scalebox{.75}{$\}$}}$}\mkern-2.0muM$}}\cong\mathcal{T}_{1}=(\mathbb{R},+)
.
The examples in Figs.

and

exemplify that the

-structure automorphisms do not only depend on the structure group
G
but on the particular choice of
G
-structure
G\mkern-1.4muM
.
The general case for
G
being non-trivial is harder to visualize since
G_{\mkern-1.3mup}\mkern-1.2muM
will then not be a single frame but a set of frames.

Since
G
-structures are in general not closed under the action of isometries on
F\mkern-1.5muM
, it might be
impossible
to define a group action of the full isometry group on
G\mkern-1.4muM
or any other associated
G
-bundle.
To remedy this shortcoming, we will in the following consider the subgroup of those isometries that respect the
G
-structure, i.e. which map preferred frames in
G\mkern-1.4muM
to frames in
G\mkern-1.4muM
.

Definition 8.1
(
G
-structure preserving isometries).

Given a
G
-structure
G\mkern-1.4muM
, we define the corresponding subgroup of
G
-structure preserving isometries
\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
as:

\displaystyle\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}\ :=\ \big\{\phi\in\Isom(\mkern-1.5muM\mkern-0.5mu)\,\big|\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}(G_{\mkern-1.3mup}\mkern-1.2muM)=G_{\mkern-1.5mu\phi(p)}\mkern-1.5muM\ \ \ \forall p\in M\big\}\ \leq\ \Isom(\mkern-1.5muM\mkern-0.5mu)

(273)

For such isometries, we define the induced action on
G\mkern-1.4muM
as

\displaystyle\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\,:=\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\mkern-2.0mu\big|_{\scalebox{.58}{$G\mkern-1.4muM$}}\,:\ G\mkern-1.4muM\to G\mkern-1.4muM\,,\qquad\phi\in\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}\,.

(274)

Such defined actions for
\phi\in\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
are
G
-structure automorphisms
, that is, they make the following diagram commute for any
g\in G
(which follows by restricting Eq (

to

and

An

For specific choices of structure groups
G
it is possible to make more general statements about which isometries are contained in the subgroup
\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
.
Most importantly, for orthonormal structure groups
G=\operatorname{O}(d)
(which are compatible with
\eta
)
any
isometry will induce an automorphism of
\operatorname{O}\mkern-3.6muM
, that is, one always has
\Isom_{\operatorname{O}\mkern-3.6muM}=\Isom(\mkern-1.5muM\mkern-0.5mu)\,.

To prove this claim, let
[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\in\operatorname{O}_{\mkern-1.1mup}\mkern-3.4muM\subset F_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-1.0muM
be an orthonormal frame, which is by an arbitrary isometry
\phi\in\Isom(\mkern-1.5muM\mkern-0.5mu)
being sent to
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\big|_{\scalebox{.58}{$\operatorname{O}\mkern-3.6muM$}}[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}=\big[\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}e_{i}\big]_{i=1}^{d}
; see Eq. (
269
).
Applying Eq. (
268
) to the individual axes of the pushforward frame yields

\displaystyle\eta\big(\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}e_{i},\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}e_{j}\big)\,=\,\eta(e_{i},e_{j})\,=\,\delta_{ij}\ \quad\ \forall\ \ i,j\in 1,\dots,d\,,

(276)

which implies the orthonormality of of the pushforward frame
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\big|_{\scalebox{.58}{$\operatorname{O}\mkern-3.6muM$}}[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\in\operatorname{O}_{\mkern-1.1mu\phi(p)}\mkern-3.4muM
and therefore allows to define
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\operatorname{O}\mkern-3.0muM$}}}:=\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\big|_{\scalebox{.58}{$\operatorname{O}\mkern-3.6muM$}}
for any
\phi\in\Isom(\mkern-1.5muM\mkern-0.5mu)
.
More generally, this result implies:

\displaystyle\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}=\Isom(\mkern-1.5muM\mkern-0.5mu)\quad\ \forall\ G\geq\operatorname{O}(d)

(277)

It is similarly possible to show

\displaystyle\Isom_{\mkern 1.0mu\operatorname{SO}\mkern-3.6muM}=\Isom_{+}\mkern-2.0mu(M)\,,

(278)

that is, that any orientation preserving isometry in
\Isom_{+}\mkern-2.0mu(M)
induces an automorphism of an
\operatorname{SO}(d)
-structure
\operatorname{SO}\mkern-3.6muM

-structure.
This is ultimately a result of only considering isometries, which are adapted to

-structures by definition, instead of considering more general diffeomorphisms.
As mentioned before, the subgroup
\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}

does
in general depend on the specific choice of

-structure
G\mkern-1.4muM
, not only the structure group

This action is well defined since the construction is by the right

As an associated bundle, the pushforward
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,${Hom} }}}
on the homomorphism bundle

) as well.
However, we will later on require an expression of

in terms of the pushforwards
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}$ }}}
and

of

and

For that purpose, let

(281)

where we defined the pushforward on the homomorphism bundle as:

\displaystyle\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,${Hom} }}}\!:\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})\to\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}}),\quad H\mapsto\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}}$ }}}H\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}$ }}}^{-1}\,,\qquad\ \phi\in\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}

(282)

Note that the composition of an element

\displaystyle\rhd\!:\ \Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}\mkern-2.0mu\times\mkern 2.0mu\Gamma(\mathcal{A})\to\Gamma(\mathcal{A}),\quad(\phi,f)\mapsto\phi\rhd\!f\,:=\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}$ }}}\!\circ f\circ\phi^{-1}\mkern-1.0mu\,.

(283)

In terms of a commutative diagram, this definition is visualized as:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{A}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{A}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces M}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces M}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}$ }}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f\ }
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\ \phi\rhd\!f\ :=\>\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}$ }}}\!\circ\mkern-2.0muf\circ\phi^{-1}\mkern-1.0mu}

(284)

Intuitively, this definition states that the pushforward section
\phi\rhd\!f
, evaluated at
p\in M
, returns the feature vector of

from
\phi^{-1}(p)
, pushed forward to

via
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}$ }}}
.
Note that such pushforwards do indeed yield well defined sections, which satisfy

\displaystyle\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!\!\mathcal{A}$}}}\circ(\phi\rhd\!f)\

\displaystyle=\ \pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!\!\mathcal{A}$}}}\circ\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}$ }}}\!\circ f\circ\phi^{-1}\mkern-1.0mu

\displaystyle=\ \phi\circ\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!\!\mathcal{A}$}}}\circ f\circ\phi^{-1}\mkern-1.0mu

\displaystyle=\ \phi\circ\mathrm{id}_{M}\circ\phi^{-1}\mkern-1.0mu

\displaystyle=\ \mathrm{id}_{M}

(285)

as required by Eq. (

).

visualizes the action of isometries on fields.
The action of isometries on the transporter pullback

of a fields

8.1.3
Isometry action in local coordinates

Most of the derivations on the isometry equivariance of kernel field transforms in Sections
8.2
and
8.3
will be kept in a coordinate free setting.
However, since
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions are defined relative to a choice of
G
-atlases of the associated bundles, the investigation of their isometry equivariance will require us to study coordinate expressions of the isometry pushforwards
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}
,
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}
,
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}
and
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}$ }}}
relative to local bundle trivializations.
Coordinate expressions of the isometry action are furthermore useful in numerical implementations, which are necessarily encoding feature fields relative to fields of reference frames.

In the following, we assume gauges
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}}^{\widetilde{A}}
and
\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}}^{A}
on neighborhoods
U^{\widetilde{A}}
of
p
and
U^{A}
of
\phi(p)
to be given.
For convenience, let
U^{A}=\phi\big(U^{\widetilde{A}}\big)
coincide with the image of
U^{\widetilde{A}}
under the isometry, which is always possible without losing generality.

Pushforward on
TM
in coordinates:

Recall that the pushforward on the tangent bundle is a linear map from vectors
v\in T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
to vectors
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}v\in T_{\mkern-1.5mu\phi(p)}\mkern-1.0muM
.
Relative to the given gauges, the pushforward is therefore coordinatized by a field of matrices
72
72

72

Given charts

x^{\widetilde{A}}:U^{\widetilde{A}}\to x^{\widetilde{A}}\big(U^{\widetilde{A}}\big)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d}

and

x^{A}:U^{A}\to x^{A}\big(U^{A}\big)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d}

of
M
, an isometry
\phi
can be locally represented by a map

x^{A}\circ\phi\circ\big(x^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{\mkern-1.0mu-1}\!:x^{\widetilde{A}}\big(U^{\widetilde{A}}\big)\to x^{A}\big(U^{A}\big)

between coordinates.
For the special case that the gauges at
p
and
\phi(p)
correspond to the coordinate bases of those charts,
g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}
is simply given by the
Jacobian
of
x^{A}\circ\phi\circ\big(x^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{\mkern-1.0mu-1}
.

\displaystyle g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}\!:U^{\widetilde{A}}\to\operatorname{GL}(d),\ \ \ p\mapsto g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}(p):=\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}\mkern-2.0mu\circ\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}\mkern-2.0mu\circ\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1},\quad\ \ \phi\in\Isom(\mkern-1.5muM\mkern-0.5mu)\,,

(286)

which transforms between the corresponding numerical coefficients
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}(v)
of
v
at
p
and
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}(\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}v)=g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}(p)\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}(v)
of
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}v
at
\phi(p)
.
More precisely,
g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}
takes values in the subgroup
\langle\,G\cup\operatorname{O}(d)\,\rangle
of
\operatorname{GL}(d)
, which is generated by the elements of
\operatorname{O}(d)
(due to
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}
preserving the metric) and
G
(since the transition functions might form a supergroup of
\operatorname{O}(d)
).
The definition of the pushforward in local coordinates is visualized by the following commutative diagram:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{R}^{d}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces T_{\mkern-1.5mu\phi(p)}\mkern-1.0muM}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbb{R}^{d}}
g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}(p)\mkern 2.0mu\cdot
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}}

(287)

Fig.
21
gives a graphical interpretation of the pushforward in coordinates.

Pushforward on
FM
in coordinates:

The coordinatization of the pushforward on the frame bundle is defined in analogy to Eq. (
286
).
It turns out to be given by the left action of the same group element
g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}
on trivialized frames as shown in the commutative diagram below:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{GL}(d)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-1.0muM}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F_{\mkern-1.6mu\phi(p)}\mkern-1.3muM}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{GL}(d)}
g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}(p)\mkern 2.0mu\cdot
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}}

(288)

To prove this claim, we compute the action on a trivialized frame, given by a matrix
h\in\operatorname{GL}(d)
whose

-th column

represents the
i
-th frame vector:

\displaystyle\Big[\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}\circ\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\circ\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}\Big](h)

\displaystyle=\

\displaystyle\Big[\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}\circ\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\Big]\!\Big(\!\Big(\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}(h_{:,i})\Big)_{i=1}^{d}\Big)\qquad\quad

\displaystyle\big(\text{def. of $\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}$, Eq.~\eqref{eq:trivialization_FM_p} }\big)

\displaystyle=\

\displaystyle\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}\!\Big(\!\Big(\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}\circ\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}(h_{:,i})\Big)_{i=1}^{d}\Big)\qquad\quad

\displaystyle\big(\text{def. of $\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}$, Eq.~\eqref{eq:pushforward_FM_def} }\big)

\displaystyle=\

\displaystyle\Big(\!\Big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}\circ\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}\circ\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}(h_{:,i})\Big)_{i=1}^{d}\Big)\qquad\quad

\displaystyle=\

\displaystyle\Big(g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}(p)\cdot h_{:,i}\Big)_{i=1}^{d}\qquad\quad

\displaystyle\big(\text{def. of $g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}$, Eq.~\eqref{eq:pushforward_TM_coord} }\big)

\displaystyle=\

\displaystyle g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}(p)\cdot h

(289)

The action of the pushforward on local trivializations can be thought of as
inducing a gauge transformation
.
A graphical intuition for this statement was given in Fig.
21
where the initial gauges at
p
and
\phi(p)
are visualized by choices of reference frames.
A pushforward of the frame at
p
to
\phi(p)
(red) does in general not agree with the original frame at
\phi(p)
(green).
The transition between these two frames is the induced gauge transformation by at
\phi(p)
.
We will in the following construct this transformation; first in terms of local trivializations, then in terms of the corresponding frame fields.

From the commutative diagram in Eq. (
288
) it is clear that the gauge
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}:F_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-1.0muM\to\operatorname{GL}(d)
at
p
can via
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}^{-1}
be pulled back to a gauge at
\phi(p)
, which is given by

\displaystyle\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\circ\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}^{-1}\ =\ \big(g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}(p)\big)^{-1}\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}\,:\,\ F_{\mkern-1.6mu\phi(p)}\mkern-1.3muM\to\operatorname{GL}(d)\,.

(290)

The corresponding extension of the commutative diagram in Eq. (
288
) visualizes the equivalence of both expressions and makes an algebraic proof superfluous:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{GL}(d)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-1.0muM}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F_{\mkern-1.6mu\phi(p)}\mkern-1.3muM}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\operatorname{GL}(d)}
g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}(p)\mkern 2.0mu\cdot
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}}
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}^{-1}\ =\ \big(g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}(p)\big)^{-1}\mkern-2.0mu\cdot\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}

(291)

The transition map (gauge transformation) between the isometry induced gauge
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}^{-1}
and the original gauge
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}
at
\phi(p)
is read off to be given by the inverse
73
73

73

The inverse is a matter of convention.
It arises here since we defined
g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}
as coordinate expression of the covariant pushforward of frames while gauges transform contravariantly.

group element

\displaystyle\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}^{-1}\big)\circ\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}\big)^{-1}\ =\ \big(g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}(p)\big)^{-1}\ \ \ \in\,\ \langle\,G\cup\operatorname{O}(d)\,\rangle\ \leq\ \operatorname{GL}(d)\,.

(292)

Note that this group element does for
G\leq\operatorname{O}(d)
not necessarily lie in the structure group, that is, the isometry induced gauge might not be
G
-compatible (it can not be added to an existing
G
-atlas of

).
In the next paragraph on
G
-structures we will show that this happens exactly when

, i.e. for isometries which do not respect the
G
-structure.

To derive the isometry action on frame fields, consider the identity sections
\sigma^{\widetilde{A}}:U^{\widetilde{A}}\to\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!F\!M$}}}^{-1}\big(U^{\widetilde{A}}\big)
over
U^{\widetilde{A}}
and
\sigma^{A}:U^{A}\to\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!F\!M$}}}^{-1}\big(U^{A}\big)
over
U^{A}
.
These sections model the original frame fields from Fig.
21
.
The new frame field is then given by the pushforward section

\displaystyle\phi\mkern 2.0mu\rhd\sigma^{\widetilde{A}}\,:=\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\circ\sigma^{\widetilde{A}}\circ\phi^{-1}\mkern-1.0mu\ :\ U^{A}\to\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!F\!M$}}}^{-1}\big(U^{A}\big)\,,

(293)

which is equivalently defined to that in Eq.
283
.
An alternative expression for the pushforward frame field in terms of the right action of

is found by applying

:

\displaystyle\ \ \psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big($}}}}}\big[\phi\rhd\sigma^{\widetilde{A}}\,\big](\phi(p))\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\ \ \psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\,\sigma^{\widetilde{A}}(p)\qquad\quad

\displaystyle\ \ g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}(p)\qquad\quad

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\ \ \psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big($}}}}}\sigma^{A}\big(\phi(p)\big)\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}\,g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}(p)\qquad\quad

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\ \ \psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big($}}}}}\sigma^{A}\big(\phi(p)\big)\lhd g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}(p)\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}\qquad\quad

(294)

Since
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}
is an isomorphism, it follows that

\displaystyle\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\Big($}}}}\phi\rhd\sigma^{\widetilde{A}}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}\big(\phi(p)\big)\ =\ \phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\sigma^{\widetilde{A}}(p)\ =\ \sigma^{A}\big(\phi(p)\big)\lhd g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}(p)\,,

(295)

that is,

does as expected describe the transformation between identity sections.
This isometry induced transformation between reference frames is in Fig.

visualized by the blue arrow between the (translucent) red and green frame.

The isometry transformed gauge
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}^{-1}
and the pushforward section
\phi\rhd\sigma^{\widetilde{A}}
correspond to each other in so far that the latter is the identity section of the former:

\displaystyle\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}^{-1}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big[$}}}}}\phi\rhd\sigma^{\widetilde{A}}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big]$}}}}}\big(\phi(p)\big)\ =\ \psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}^{-1}\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\sigma^{\widetilde{A}}(p)\ =\ \psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\sigma^{\widetilde{A}}(p)\ =\ e

(296)

Pushforward on
GM
in coordinates:

As argued in the previous Section
8.1.2
, the pushforward on
G\mkern-1.4muM
is only well defined for isometries
\phi
in a subgroup
\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
.
Not surprisingly, the corresponding isometry induced gauge transformations take values in the structure group
G
:

Theorem 8.3
(
\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
in local trivializations).

Let
\phi\in\Isom(\mkern-1.5muM\mkern-0.5mu)
be any isometry of
M
.
Then the following three statements are equivalent:

1.

\phi
is
G
-structure preserving, that is,
\phi\in\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
.

2.

The isometry pullback
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}^{-1}
of any gauge
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}
of the
G
-atlas of
F\mkern-1.5muM
that defines
G\mkern-1.4muM
is
G
-compatible with that
G
-atlas.

3.

The coordinate expression of
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}
relative to any gauges
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}
and
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}
from the
G
-atlas of
F\mkern-1.5muM
takes values in the structure group, that is,
g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}(p)\in G\ \ \ \forall\ p\in M
.

Proof
:

The defining property of a
G
-structure preserving isometry
\phi\in\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
is that it satisfies
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}(G_{\mkern-1.3mup}\mkern-1.2muM)=G_{\mkern-1.5mu\phi(p)}\mkern-1.5muM
for any
p\in M
; see Eq. (
273
).
In terms of a given
G
-atlas of
F\mkern-1.5muM
, Eq. (
186
) defined the
G
-structure at
p\in M
as
G_{\mkern-1.3mup}\mkern-1.2muM:=\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}(G)
where
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}
is an
arbitrary
gauge of the
G
-atlas.
With this expression we expand the left-hand side of the defining property of
\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
:

\displaystyle\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}(G_{\mkern-1.3mup}\mkern-1.2muM)\

\displaystyle=\ \phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\,\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}(G)

\displaystyle=\ \Big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}^{-1}\Big)^{-1}(G)

(297)

Relative to any gauge
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}
of the
G
-atlas at
\phi(p)
, this can be further manipulated to

\displaystyle\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}(G_{\mkern-1.3mup}\mkern-1.2muM)\

\displaystyle=\ \Big(\big(g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}(p)\big)^{-1}\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}\Big)^{-1}(G)

\displaystyle=\ \big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}\big)^{-1}\big(g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}(p)\,G\big)\,.

(298)

The right-hand side of the defining property of
\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
is in terms of
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}
given by

\displaystyle G_{\mkern-1.5mu\phi(p)}\mkern-1.5muM=\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}\big)^{-1}(G).

(299)

Setting both sides equal and using that
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}
is an isomorphism implies
g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}(p)\,G=G
which leads to the claimed equivalence

\displaystyle\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}(G_{\mkern-1.3mup}\mkern-1.2muM)=G_{\mkern-1.5mu\phi(p)}\mkern-1.5muM\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}(p)\in G

(300)

of statements 1. and 3.
To prove the equivalence to statement 2., recall that
g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}(p)
is by Eq. (
292
) equal to the gauge transformation from
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muF\mkern-2.0muM$}}}^{-1}
to
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$F\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}
.
As
G
-atlases have by definition transition functions in the structure group
G
, the implications (2.
\leftrightarrow
3.) follow, such that all three statements are seen to be equivalent.

\Box

These results are of central importance for our later study of the isometry equivariance of
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions.
We will be able to show that such convolutions are equivariant under the action of
\phi\in\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
on feature fields, which relies on the fact that the
G
-steerability of the convolution kernels accounts for the isometry induced gauge transformations
g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}(p)\in G
.

For

8.1.4
Commutativity of isometry actions with the exponential map and transporters

In the following section we will need an expression for the action of isometries on transporter pullbacks
\operatorname{Exp}^{*}_{p}\mkern-2.0muf
of feature fields
f
, which we derive here.
For this purpose, we discuss the behavior of the exponential map and parallel transporters under the action of isometries.

Isometries and the exponential map:

As proven in
[
73
]
, isometries map geodesics to geodesics and do therefore in particular commute with the exponential map.
74
74

74

The proof relies on the fact that the Levi-Civita connection
\nabla:\Gamma(T\mkern-1.5muM)\times\Gamma(T\mkern-1.5muM)\to\Gamma(T\mkern-1.5muM),\ (X,Y)\mapsto\nabla_{\!X}Y
, on which the Riemannian exponential map is based, commutes with isometries:

\phi\rhd\!\big(\nabla_{\!X}Y\big)\ =\ \nabla_{\mkern-2.0mu\phi\rhd\!X}\big(\phi\rhd\!Y\big)
;
see

]

More specifically, the identity

\displaystyle\exp_{\phi(p)}\circ\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}(v)\,=\,\phi\circ\exp_{p}(v)\quad\ \forall\ v\in T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM,\ \ \phi\in\Isom(\mkern-1.5muM\mkern-0.5mu)\,,

(305)

holds for any isometry and any tangent vector at

(still assuming a geodesically complete manifold).
It states that the result of the exponential map at

The isometry-invariance of exponential maps and transporters allows

-convolutions to be equivariant under the action of isometries.

Isometries and parallel transporters:

The pushforward on the tangent bundle was in

]
further argued to commute with the corresponding Levi-Civita transporters, as visualized in Fig.

If an alternative,

that it commutes with the action of isometries as well.
Since the transporters and the pushforwards on

Specifically for the associated feature vector bundles this means that for arbitrary isometries

to hold, such that the following diagram commutes:

Isometries and transporter pullbacks of feature fields:

Knowing the transformation laws of exponential maps and transporters under the action of isometries, we have everything at hand that is required to derive the transformation law of transporter pullbacks
\operatorname{Exp}^{*}_{p}\mkern-2.0muf
of feature fields
f
:

Theorem 8.4
(Isometry action on transporter pullbacks of feature fields).

Let
f\in\Gamma(\mathcal{A})
be any feature field and let
\phi\in\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
be any
G
-structure preserving isometry.
Assume the feature vector transporters to commute with the action of
\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
, that is, that Eq. (
307
) holds
(which is automatically guaranteed for the Levi-Civita connection).
The transporter pullback (Def.
7.5
) of the pushforward field
\phi\rhd\!f
(Def.
8.2
) is then given by:

\displaystyle\operatorname{Exp}^{*}_{p}(\phi\rhd f)\ =\ \phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}}$ }}}\!\circ\big[\mkern-2.0mu\operatorname{Exp}^{*}_{\phi^{-1}(p)}\mkern-2.0muf\mkern 1.0mu\big]\circ\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}

(309)

Proof
:

We start by letting the right-hand side act on an arbitrary vector
v\in T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
and work progressively to the left-hand side by using the properties derived in this section:

\displaystyle\,\ \phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}}$ }}}\big[\mkern-2.0mu\operatorname{Exp}^{*}_{\phi^{-1}(p)}\mkern-2.0muf\mkern 1.0mu\big]\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}(v)

(310)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\,\ \phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}}$ }}}\,\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-5.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.8}{$\!\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}$},\scalebox{.85}{$\mkern 2.0mu\phi^{-1}\mkern-1.0mu(p)\mkern-3.0mu\leftarrow\mkern-1.0mu\exp_{\phi^{-1}\mkern-1.0mu(p)}\!\circ\mkern 2.0mu\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}(v)$}}}\circ f\circ\exp_{\phi^{-1}\mkern-1.0mu(p)}\mkern-2.0mu\circ\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}(v)\quad

\displaystyle\big(\text{transporter pullback, Def.~\ref{dfn:Expf_pullback_field} }\big)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\,\ \phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}}$ }}}\,\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-5.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.8}{$\!\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}$},\scalebox{.85}{$\mkern 2.0mu\phi^{-1}\mkern-1.0mu(p)\mkern-3.0mu\leftarrow\mkern-1.0mu\phi^{-1}\mkern-1.0mu\mkern-2.0mu\circ\exp_{p}(v)$}}}\circ f\circ\phi^{-1}\mkern-1.0mu\circ\exp_{p}(v)\quad

\displaystyle\big(\text{isometry action on $\exp$, Eq.~\eqref{eq:exp_isom_commutation}}\big)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\,\ \mathcal{P}_{\mkern-5.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.8}{$\!\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}$},\scalebox{.85}{$\mkern 2.0mup\mkern-3.0mu\leftarrow\mkern-1.0mu\exp_{p}(v)$}}}\circ\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}$ }}}\circ f\circ\phi^{-1}\mkern-1.0mu\circ\exp_{p}(v)\quad

\displaystyle\big(\text{isometry action on $\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-5.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.75}{$\!\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}$}}}$, Eq.~\eqref{eq:transport_isom_commutation}}\big)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\,\ \mathcal{P}_{\mkern-5.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.8}{$\!\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}$},\scalebox{.85}{$\mkern 2.0mup\mkern-3.0mu\leftarrow\mkern-1.0mu\exp_{p}(v)$}}}\circ(\phi\rhd f)\circ\exp_{p}(v)\quad

\displaystyle\big(\text{pushforward of fields, Eq.~\eqref{eq:pushforward_section_A}}\big)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\,\ \big[\mkern-2.0mu\operatorname{Exp}^{*}_{p}(\phi\rhd f)\mkern 1.0mu\big](v)\quad

\displaystyle\big(\text{transporter pullback, Def.~\ref{dfn:Expf_pullback_field} }\big)

\Box

Intuitively, this result just states that the transporter pullback of a pushforward field equals the pushforward of the original field’s transporter pullback.
Relative to local trivializations, this pushforward can be interpreted as an isometry induced gauge transformation, which was stated in Eq. (
93
).
We will in the following assume that the
G
-compatible connection which is chosen to transport feature vectors will always be
\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
-invariant, and thus that Eq. (
309
) holds.

That the transporter pullback and the isometry pushforward commute is a consequence of the commutativity of the exponential map and parallel transporter, in terms of which the transporter pullback is defined.
Note that general diffeomorphisms do not preserve the metric and thus the exponential map and the transporter pullback of feature fields.
Being based on these constructions, kernel field transforms and
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions can only be isometry equivariant but not fully diffeomorphism equivariant.

8.2
Isometry equivariance of kernel field transforms and
GM
-convolutions

We now turn to investigate under which conditions kernel field transforms and
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions are equivariant w.r.t. the action of isometries on feature fields.
As the action on the
G
-associated feature vector bundles is only defined for
G
-structure preserving isometries, we will formulate all statements for the subgroup
\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}\leq\Isom(\mkern-1.5muM\mkern-0.5mu)
or subgroups
\mathcal{I}\leq\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
thereof.
One can of course always consider structure groups
G\geq\operatorname{O}(d)
, for which
\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}=\Isom(\mkern-1.5muM\mkern-0.5mu)
.

The equivariance of a kernel field transform, and thus
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions, is defined as follows:

Definition 8.5
(Isometry equivariant kernel field transform).

Let
{{T}_{\overset{}{\mkern 0.0mu\mathcal{K}}}:\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}})\to\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})}
be a kernel field transform.
Then
{T}_{\overset{}{\mkern 0.0mu\mathcal{K}}}
is said to be
equivariant w.r.t the action of isometries
in a subgroup
\mathcal{I}\leq\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
if it commutes with this action, that is, if the following property holds:

\displaystyle{T}_{\overset{}{\mkern 0.0mu\mathcal{K}}}\big(\phi\rhd\!f\big)\ =\ \phi\rhd\!\big({T}_{\overset{}{\mkern 0.0mu\mathcal{K}}}(f)\big)\qquad\forall\ \ f\in\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}),\ \ \phi\in\mathcal{I}

(311)

In terms of a diagram,
{T}_{\overset{}{\mkern 0.0mu\mathcal{K}}}
is equivariant w.r.t isometries in
\mathcal{I}
if

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{T}_{\overset{}{\mkern 0.0mu\mathcal{K}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi\,\rhd}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi\,\rhd}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{T}_{\overset{}{\mkern 0.0mu\mathcal{K}}}}

(312)

commutes for all
\phi\in\mathcal{I}
.

A visualization of this definition is given in Fig.
25
.
In the following Section
8.2.1
we will derive a constraint on kernel fields in order for the corresponding kernel field transform to be isometry equivariant.
The geometrically intuitive result which we obtain is that the kernel field itself is required to be invariant under the action of isometries, which implies a form of weight sharing over the isometry orbits; see Fig.
43
.
Section
8.2.2
applies these insights to the more specific case of
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions and
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutional kernel fields.
It turns out that
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions are by the
G
-steerability of their template kernel automatically equivariant with respect to
any
isometry in
\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
.

8.2.1
Isometry equivariance of general kernel field transforms

The main result of this section, Theorem
8.8
, states that
a kernel field transform
{T}_{\overset{}{\mkern 0.0mu\mathcal{K}}}
is isometry equivariant if and only if its underlying kernel field
\mathcal{K}
is invariant under isometries
.
To make sense of this statement we start by defining the transformation behavior of kernel fields when being acted on by isometries.

Definition 8.6
(Isometry action on kernel fields).

Let
\mathcal{K}:T\mkern-1.5muM\to\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})
be a kernel field.
An isometry
\phi\in\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
acts on
\mathcal{K}
via the kernel field pushforward

\displaystyle\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu{K}\mkern 2.0mu$}}}\mathcal{K}\ :=\ \phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,${Hom} }}}\!\circ\mathcal{K}\circ\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}\,.

(313)

Intuitively, this pushforward of kernel fields can be thought of as moving the individual kernels
\mathcal{K}_{p}
at points
p\in M
along the orbits of the isometry group to
\phi(p)
.

Since kernel fields are defined to be bundle
M
-morphisms, that is, to satisfy
\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ \!Hom}}}\mathcal{K}=\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}
, their pushforward is only well defined if it preserves this property.
This is guaranteed since the pushforward on the tangent bundle and homomorphism bundle are bundle maps, satisfying
\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}\circ\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}=\phi\circ\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}
(Eq. (
267
)) and
{\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ \!Hom}}}\circ\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,${Hom} }}}=\phi\circ\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ \!Hom}}}}
(Eq. (
280
)), respectively:

\displaystyle\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ \!Hom}}}\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu{K}\mkern 2.0mu$}}}\mathcal{K}\

\displaystyle=\ \pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ \!Hom}}}\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,${Hom} }}}\mathcal{K}\;\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}

\displaystyle=\ \phi\,\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ \!Hom}}}\,\mathcal{K}\;\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}

\displaystyle=\ \phi\,\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}

\displaystyle=\ \phi\,\phi^{-1}\mkern-1.0mu\,\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}

\displaystyle=\ \pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}

(314)

Definition 8.7
(Isometry invariant kernel fields).

A kernel field
\mathcal{K}
is said to be
invariant

75

75

Instead of saying that
\mathcal{K}
is

, one could call it

since it satisfies

\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,${Hom} }}}\!\circ\mathcal{K}\,=\ \mathcal{K}\circ\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}\ \forall\phi\in\mathcal{I}
.
In general, any function which is equivariant w.r.t. certain group actions on its domain and codomain is

invariant under pre- and postcomposition with the actions on its domain and codomain as in Eq. (

under isometries
in

for all

.
We denote the space of isometry invariant kernel fields by

\displaystyle{K}_{\textup{invar}}^{\mathcal{I}}:=\mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\Big\{$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\Big\{$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big\{$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big\{$}}}}}\mkern 2.0mu\mathcal{K}\mkern-2.0mu:T\mkern-1.5muM\to\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})\ \ \textup{smooth}\ \,\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big|$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big|$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big|$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big|$}}}}}\;\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ \!Hom}}}\!\circ\mathcal{K}=\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}\,,\ \ \ \phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu{K}\mkern 2.0mu$}}}\mathcal{K}=\mathcal{K}\quad\forall\phi\in\mathcal{I}\,\mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\Big\}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\Big\}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big\}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{360448}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big\}$}}}}}\,.

(316)

By writing out
