\displaystyle\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,${Hom} }}}\!\circ\mathcal{K}\circ\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}\,=\ \mathcal{K}\qquad\forall\phi\in\mathcal{I}\,,

(317)

which, after further expanding
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,${Hom} }}}
as defined in Eq. (
282
), becomes:

\displaystyle\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}}$ }}}\mathcal{K}\big(\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}v\big)\ \phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}$ }}}^{-1}=\,\mathcal{K}(v)\qquad\forall\ v\in T\mkern-1.5muM,\ \ \forall\phi\in\mathcal{I}

(318)

Note the similarity of these kernel field constraints in
Eqs. (
317
) and (
318
) with the
G
-steerability constraint on template kernels in Eqs. (
245
) and (
246
), respectively.
Indeed, both constraints are closely related and imply each other to a certain extent as we will show in the following Section
8.2.2
on isometry equivariant
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions.

Figure 43:
Visualization of an invariant kernel field
\mathcal{K}
for the case of an isometry (sub)group
\mathcal{I}=\operatorname{SO}(2)
.
The invariance constraint requires
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu{K}\mkern 2.0mu$}}}\mathcal{K}:=\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,${Hom} }}}\mathcal{K}\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}=\mathcal{K}
for any
\phi
in
\mathcal{I}
.
It enforces kernels to be shared over the orbits
\mathcal{I}.p:=\{\phi(p)\,|\,\phi\in\mathcal{I}\}
of the action but allows for different kernels on different orbits.
Theorem
8.8
proves that invariant kernel fields and equivariant kernel field transforms imply each other.
This is intuitively clear since a specific pattern in the feature field at
p\in M
will evoke the same response when being transported to
\phi(p)
if and only if the kernels at both points coincide.
For the choice of
\mathcal{I}=\operatorname{O}(2)
as isometry group, the kernels would additionally have to satisfy a reflectional constraint; see Fig.
45
.

The following theorem proves that kernel fields which are invariant under isometries do indeed correspond to isometry equivariant kernel field transforms:

Theorem 8.8
(Equivariant kernel field transform
\Leftrightarrow
invariant kernel field).

A kernel field transform
{T}_{\overset{}{\mkern 0.0mu\mathcal{K}}}:\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}})\to\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})
is equivariant w.r.t. isometries in
\mathcal{I}\leq\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
according to Def.
8.5
if and only if
the underlying kernel field
\mathcal{K}
is invariant under isometries according to Def.
8.7
, that is,

\displaystyle{T}_{\overset{}{\mkern 0.0mu\mathcal{K}}}(\phi\rhd f)\,=\,\phi\rhd{T}_{\overset{}{\mkern 0.0mu\mathcal{K}}}(f)\quad\forall\;\phi\in\mathcal{I}\,,\ f\in\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}})\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu{K}\mkern 2.0mu$}}}\mathcal{K}=\mathcal{K}\quad\forall\,\phi\in\mathcal{I}

(319)

Proof
:

To prove this theorem, we write out the kernel field transforms and feature field pushforwards on both sides of the isometry equivariance condition in Eq. (
311
).
The statement follows from a comparison of both sides after a few algebraic manipulations.

We start with the right-hand side of Eq. (
311
):

\displaystyle\big[\phi\rhd{T}_{\overset{}{\mkern 0.0mu\mathcal{K}}}(f)\big](p)\

\displaystyle\overset{(1)}{=}\ \ \phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}}$ }}}\big[{T}_{\overset{}{\mkern 0.0mu\mathcal{K}}}(f)\big]\big(\phi^{-1}(p)\big)

\displaystyle\overset{(2)}{=}\ \ \phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}}$ }}}\mkern-8.0mu\int\limits_{T_{\!\phi^{-1}\mkern-1.0mu\mkern-1.0mu(p)}\mkern-2.0muM}\!\!\mkern-6.0mu\mathcal{K}(v)\ \big[\mkern-2.0mu\operatorname{Exp}^{*}_{\phi^{-1}(p)}\mkern-2.0muf\mkern 1.0mu\big](v)\,\ dv

\displaystyle\overset{(3)}{=}\ \ \phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}}$ }}}\mkern-8.0mu\int\limits_{T_{\!\phi^{-1}\mkern-1.0mu\mkern-1.0mu(p)}\mkern-2.0muM}\!\!\mkern-6.0mu\mathcal{K}(v)\ \phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}$ }}}^{-1}\big[\mkern-2.0mu\operatorname{Exp}^{*}_{p}\!\big(\phi\rhd f\big)\mkern 1.0mu\big]\big(\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}(v)\big)\,\ dv

\displaystyle\overset{(4)}{=}\ \ \int\limits_{T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM}\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}}$ }}}\mathcal{K}\big(\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}\tilde{v}\big)\ \phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}$ }}}^{-1}\big[\mkern-2.0mu\operatorname{Exp}^{*}_{p}\!\big(\phi\rhd f\big)\mkern 1.0mu\big](\tilde{v})\,\ d\tilde{v}

\displaystyle\overset{(5)}{=}\ \ \int\limits_{T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM}\big[\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,${Hom} }}}\mathcal{K}\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}\big](\tilde{v})\ \big[\mkern-2.0mu\operatorname{Exp}^{*}_{p}\!\big(\phi\rhd f\big)\mkern 1.0mu\big](\tilde{v})\,\ d\tilde{v}

\displaystyle\overset{(6)}{=}\ \ \int\limits_{T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM}\big[\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu{K}\mkern 2.0mu$}}}\mathcal{K}\big](\tilde{v})\ \big[\mkern-2.0mu\operatorname{Exp}^{*}_{p}\!\big(\phi\rhd f\big)\mkern 1.0mu\big](\tilde{v})\,\ d\tilde{v}

(320)

Steps
(1)
and
(2)
expand the isometry action
\rhd
on feature fields (Def.
8.2
) and the kernel field transform (Def.
7.6
).
The transformation law of the field’s transporter pullback in Theorem
8.4
, which relies on the
\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
-invariance of the
G
-compatible connection, justifies step
(3)
.
Step
(4)
substitutes
v
with
\tilde{v}=\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}v
.
Since
\phi
is an isometry, the change of volume equates to
1
.
Steps
(5)
and
(6)
identify the action of the kernel pushforward
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu{K}\mkern 2.0mu$}}}
, Def.
8.6
.
The resulting statement is quite intuitive:
A transformation of the kernel field transform’s output corresponds to a simultaneous transformation of its input
and
kernel field.

Writing out the left-hand side yields

\displaystyle\big[{T}_{\overset{}{\mkern 0.0mu\mathcal{K}}}\big(\phi\rhd f\big)\big](p)\ =\ \int\limits_{T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM}\mathcal{K}(v)\ \big[\mkern-2.0mu\operatorname{Exp}^{*}_{p}\!\big(\phi\rhd f\big)\mkern 1.0mu\big](v)\,\ dv\,,

(321)

which is equivalent to the right-hand side
up to
the transformation of the kernel field.

Isometry equivariance requires both expressions to agree for arbitrary fields
f\in\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}})
, points
p\in M
and isometries
\phi\in\mathcal{I}
.
This is the case if and only if
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu{K}\mkern 2.0mu$}}}\mathcal{K}=\mathcal{K}
holds for any
\phi\in\mathcal{I}
, i.e. if the kernel field is invariant under the action of isometries.

\Box

Note that this proof would have been very cumbersome to work out in (a
G
-atlas of) local trivializations.
The global, coordinate free description of kernel field transforms allows for a simple proof without having to worry that the isometries move features between different local trivializations.

At this point we could proceed with a further investigation of isometry invariant kernel fields:
since the invariance constraint implies kernels to be shared over orbits of the isometry group, a description of the entire kernel field on the full manifold is redundant.
It is therefore possible to reduce the description of such kernel fields to kernel fields on quotient spaces.
As this analysis is not required to prove the isometry equivariance of
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions and requires some technical definitions, we postpone it to Section
8.3

8.2.2
Isometry equivariance of
GM
-convolutions

Recall that
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions (Def.
7.8
) were defined as specific kernel field transforms with
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutional kernel fields (Def.
7.4
).
The results on the isometry equivariance of kernel field transforms therefore immediately apply to
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions as well.
However, in addition to the isometry invariance constraint in Eq. (
317
),
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutional kernel fields need to satisfy the
G
-steerability constraint on the template kernel from Eq. (
245
) and share weights over the
G
-structure according to Eq. (
247
).
In order for the
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolution to be isometry equivariant, all of these constraints have to be satisfied simultaneously.
Intuitively, this implies that the convolutional weight sharing needs to agree with the isometry induced weight sharing over orbits.
Luckily it turns out that this is automatically the case for the isometries under consideration:

G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions share weights over the
G
-structure and the isometries in
\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
preserve the
G
-structure such that
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutional kernel fields are guaranteed to be
\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
invariant
.
In coordinates, this reflects in the
\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
-induced gauge transformations
g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}(p)
taking values in the structure group
G
, such that they are explained away by the
G
-steerability of the template kernels.

To make these arguments more rigorous, consider a
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolution
K\star:\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}})\to\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})
with some
G
-steerable kernel
K\in{K}^{G}_{\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\mkern-1.0mu,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}}
, which is by Def.
7.8
just the kernel field transform
{T}_{\overset{}{\mkern 0.0mu\mathcal{K}_{\mkern-2.0muK}}}
with the
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutional kernel field
\mathcal{K}_{\mkern-2.0muK}
.
By Theorem
8.8
, the
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolution is therefore exactly then
\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
-equivariant if
\mathcal{K}_{\mkern-2.0muK}
is
\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
-invariant, i.e. when it satisfies
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu{K}\mkern 2.0mu$}}}\mathcal{K}_{\mkern-2.0muK}=\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,${Hom} }}}\circ\mathcal{K}_{\mkern-2.0muK}\circ\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}=\mathcal{K}_{\mkern-2.0muK}
for any
\phi\in\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
.
This constraint on the full kernel field is equivalently expressed by a set of constraints on the individual convolution kernels that make up the field:

\displaystyle\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,${Hom} }}}\circ\mathcal{K}_{\mkern-2.0muK\mkern-2.0mu,p}\circ\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}\

\displaystyle=\ \mathcal{K}_{\mkern-2.0muK\mkern-2.0mu,\phi(p)}\qquad\forall\ p\in M,\ \ \phi\in\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}

(322)

Considering a specific point
p\in M
, we choose arbitrary gauges
\widetilde{A}
at
p
and
A
at
\phi(p)
from the
G
-atlas.
The
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutional kernel field is by Def.
7.4
at
p
and
\phi(p)
given by

\displaystyle\mathcal{K}_{\mkern-2.0muK\mkern-2.0mu,p}:=\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}\circ\frac{K}{\sqrt{|\eta_{p}^{\widetilde{A}}|}}\circ\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\qquad\textup{and}\qquad\mathcal{K}_{\mkern-2.0muK\mkern-2.0mu,\phi(p)}:=\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}\big)^{-1}\circ\frac{K}{\sqrt{|\eta_{\phi(p)}^{A}|}}\circ\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}\,.

(323)

Plugging these expressions into the constraint in Eq. (
322
) for the fixed
p
and identifying
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,${Hom} }}}\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}
with
\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,${Hom} }}}^{-1}\big)^{-1}
yields:

\displaystyle\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,${Hom} }}}^{-1}\big)^{-1}\circ\frac{K}{\sqrt{|\eta_{p}^{\widetilde{A}}|}}\circ\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}\,\

\displaystyle=\,\ \big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}\big)^{-1}\circ\frac{K}{\sqrt{|\eta_{\phi(p)}^{A}|}}\circ\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}\qquad\forall\ \phi\in\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}

(324)

The isometry equivariance will therefore hold if the weight sharing via the isometry induced gauges
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$(\cdot)$,}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu(\cdot)$}}}
agrees with the weight sharing via the original gauges
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$(\cdot)$,}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}
from
\phi(p)
.
Recall that the isometry induced gauges are by Theorem
8.3
for isometries in
\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
guaranteed to be compatible with the
G
-atlases (of the corresponding bundle).
As shown in Eq. (
7.2.1
), the particular choice of gauge, relative to which the
G
-steerable template kernel is oriented, is irrelevant, as long as the gauges are
G
-compatible.
Since all derivations were independent from the chosen point
p
and the particular choice of gauges, this implies that
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions are by design guaranteed to be
\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
-equivariant.

To gain a better intuition for this result it is worth to make the induced,
G
-valued gauge transformations
g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}(p)
explicit.
To this end, note that the commutativity of the diagrams in Eqs. (
304
) and (
287
) implies

\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,${Hom} }}}^{-1}=\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{{Hom}}}}\big(g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}(p)\big)^{-1}\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}
and

\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}=\big(g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}(p)\big)^{-1}\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}
.
Inserting these coordinate expressions into the constraint in Eq. (
324
) leads to the requirement that

\displaystyle\Big(\mkern-1.5mu\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{{Hom}}}}\big(g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}(p)\big)^{-1}\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}\mkern-1.5mu\Big)^{-1}\!\circ\frac{K}{\sqrt{|\eta_{p}^{\widetilde{A}}|}}\circ\big(g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}(p)\big)^{-1}\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}\

\displaystyle=\ \big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}\big)^{-1}\!\circ\frac{K}{\sqrt{|\eta_{\phi(p)}^{A}|}}\circ\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi(p)$}}^{A}

(325)

needs to hold for any isometry
\phi
in
\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
.
By expanding the inverse on the left-hand side, using that

{\sqrt{|\eta_{p}^{\widetilde{A}}|}\,=\sqrt{|\eta_{\phi(p)}^{A}|}\cdot\big|\mkern-2.0mu\det g^{A\widetilde{A}}_{\phi}(p)\big|}

and dropping the gauges, which is possible since they are isomorphisms, we end up with the constraint

\displaystyle\frac{1}{\big|\mkern-2.0mu\det g^{A\widetilde{A}}_{\phi}(p)\big|}\,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{{Hom}}}}\Big(g^{A\widetilde{A}}_{\phi}(p)\Big)\circ K\circ\Big(g^{A\widetilde{A}}_{\phi}(p)\Big)^{-1}\ =\ K\qquad\forall\ \phi\in\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}\,,

(326)

which looks
exactly
like the
G
-steerability kernel constraint on
K
from Def.
7.3
.
Recall that the isometry induced gauge transformations
g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}(p)
are by Theorem
8.3
guaranteed to be
G
-valued if
\phi
is an element of
\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
.
The constraint in Eq. (
326
) is therefore always satisfied by the
G
-steerability of
K
.

The derived results on the
\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
-invariance of
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutional kernel fields
\mathcal{K}_{\mkern-2.0muK}
are concisely summarized by the statement that the following diagram is guaranteed to be commutative if
K
is
G
-steerable and if
\phi\in\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
is
G
-structure preserving:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces U^{A}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces U^{A}\mkern-2.0mu\times\mkern-1.0mu\mathbb{R}^{d}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\,\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}^{-1}\big(U^{A}\big)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ \!Hom}}}^{-1}\big(U^{A}\big)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces U^{A}\mkern-2.0mu\times\mkern-1.0mu\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}\times{c_{\textup{in}}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces U^{\widetilde{A}}\mkern-2.0mu\times\mkern-1.0mu\mathbb{R}^{d}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}^{-1}\big(U^{\widetilde{A}}\big)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ \!Hom}}}^{-1}\big(U^{\widetilde{A}}\big)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces U^{\widetilde{A}}\mkern-2.0mu\times\mkern-1.0mu\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}\times{c_{\textup{in}}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces U^{\widetilde{A}}}
\mathrm{id}\times\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big($}}}}}\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{{Hom}}}}\big(g^{\prime A\widetilde{A}}_{\phi}\big)\circ K\big/\mkern-2.0mu\sqrt{|\eta^{A}|}\circ\big(g^{\prime A\widetilde{A}}_{\phi}\big)^{-1}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu{K}\mkern 2.0mu$}}}\mathcal{K}_{\mkern-2.0muK}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}}^{A}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ \!Hom}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{\!Hom}}^{A}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi\times g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}\cdot}
\mathrm{id}\times K\big/\mkern-2.0mu\sqrt{|\eta^{\widetilde{A}}|}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{K}_{\mkern-2.0muK}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!T\!M$}}^{\widetilde{A}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ \!Hom}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,${Hom} }}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Psi_{\scalebox{.6}{\!Hom}}^{\widetilde{A}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi\times\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{{Hom}}}}\big(g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}\big)}

(327)

Here we defined the pullback
g_{\phi}^{\prime A\widetilde{A}}:=g_{\phi}^{A\widetilde{A}}\circ\phi^{-1}:U^{A}\to G
of the isometry pushforward coordinatization from
U^{\widetilde{A}}
to
U^{A}
for notational convenience.

Together with Theorem
8.8
, the
\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
-invariance of
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutional kernel fields implies the
\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
-equivariance of
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions:

Theorem 8.9
(Isometry equivariance of
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions).

A
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolution
K\star:\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}})\to\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})
with a
G
-steerable kernel
K\in{K}^{G}_{\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\mkern-1.0mu,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}}
is equivariant with respect to all
G
-structure preserving isometries
\phi\in\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
, that is,

\displaystyle K\star\big(\phi\rhd f\big)\ =\ \phi\rhd\big(K\star f\big)\qquad\forall\ \ f\in\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}),\ \ \phi\in\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}\,.

(328)

The following diagram commutes therefore for every
\phi\in\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces K\star}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi\,\rhd\,}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\,\phi\,\rhd}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces K\star}

(329)

Proof
:

The proof was given in the discussion prior to the theorem.

\Box

Having this general result on
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions derived, we will now discuss some special cases for specific choices of structure groups
G
.
Firstly, for orthogonal structure groups
G=\operatorname{O}(d)
(or supergroups of it), the convolution will commute with
any
isometry:

Theorem 8.10
(Full isometry equivariance of
\operatorname{O}\mkern-3.6muM
-convolutions).

\operatorname{O}\mkern-3.6muM
-convolutions are equivariant w.r.t. the action of
any
isometry
\phi\in\Isom(\mkern-1.5muM\mkern-0.5mu)
on feature fields.
More generally, any
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolution for
G
-structures with structure groups
G\geq\operatorname{O}(d)
is fully isometry equivariant.

Proof
:

The statement follows from Theorem (
8.9
) by observing that
\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}=\Isom(\mkern-1.5muM\mkern-0.5mu)
is guaranteed for structure groups
G\geq\operatorname{O}(d)
.
The latter was discussed in Eq. (
277
).

\Box

This result relies essentially on the fact that isometries are defined as that subgroup of diffeomorphisms on
M
which induce
\operatorname{O}(d)
-structure automorphisms.
Less abstractly stated,
\Isom(\mkern-1.5muM\mkern-0.5mu)
is by definition that subgroup of diffeomorphisms which respect the Riemannian metric
\eta
of
M
and the corresponding
\operatorname{O}(d)
-structure
\operatorname{O}\mkern-3.6muM
is equivalent information to the metric.

On orientable Riemannian manifolds one can furthermore pick an orientation (frame handedness), which together with the metric defines an
\operatorname{SO}(d)
-structure
\operatorname{SO}\mkern-3.6muM
.
The corresponding isometries which lift to
\operatorname{SO}(d)
structure automorphisms are the orientation preserving isometries in
\Isom_{+}\mkern-2.0mu(M)
.

Theorem 8.11
(
\Isom_{+}\mkern-2.0mu(M)
equivariance of
\operatorname{SO}\mkern-3.6muM
-convolutions).

\operatorname{SO}\mkern-3.6muM
-convolutions are equivariant w.r.t. the action of orientation preserving isometries
\phi\in\Isom_{+}\mkern-2.0mu(M)
on feature fields.

Proof
:

This result follows from Theorem (
8.9
) by observing that
\Isom_{\mkern 1.0mu\operatorname{SO}\mkern-3.6muM}=\Isom_{+}\mkern-2.0mu(M)
.

\Box

For instance, an
\operatorname{SO}\mkern-3.6muM
-convolution for
M=\mathbb{R}^{2}
, corresponding to Fig
41(a)
, is equivariant w.r.t. the action of the special Euclidean group
\Isom_{+}(\mathbb{R}^{2})=\operatorname{SE}(2)
.
Similarly, an
\operatorname{SO}\mkern-3.6muM
-convolution for
M=S^{2}
, corresponding to Fig
41(b)
, is rotation equivariant with
\Isom_{+}(S^{2})=\operatorname{SO}(3)
.

Note that the results of Theorems
8.10
and
8.11
depend only on the structure group
G
but not on the particular choice of
G
-structure.
For subgroups
G
of
\operatorname{O}(d)
(or
\operatorname{SO}(d)
) things become more complicated.
In these cases the subgroups
\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
of
\Isom(\mkern-1.5muM\mkern-0.5mu)
depend on the specific embedding of the
G
-structure
G\mkern-1.4muM
into
F\mkern-1.5muM
.
This was for
G=\{e\}
visualized in Fig.
40
.
Specifically, Fig.
40(a)
shows the canonical
\{e\}
-structure of
\mathbb{R}^{2}
, which is fully translation equivariant, that is,
\Isom_{\scalebox{.85}{$\raisebox{0.2pt}{$\raisebox{0.5pt}{\scalebox{.75}{$\{$}}\mkern-1.3mue\mkern-1.1mu\raisebox{0.5pt}{\scalebox{.75}{$\}$}}$}\mkern-2.0muM$}}=\mathcal{T}_{2}:=(\mathbb{R}^{2},+)
.
In contrast, Fig.
40(b)
shows an
\{e\}
-structure of
\mathbb{R}^{2}
which is only translation equivariant along one axis such that
\Isom_{\scalebox{.85}{$\raisebox{0.2pt}{$\raisebox{0.5pt}{\scalebox{.75}{$\{$}}\mkern-1.3mue\mkern-1.1mu\raisebox{0.5pt}{\scalebox{.75}{$\}$}}$}\mkern-2.0muM$}}\cong\mathcal{T}_{1}:=(\mathbb{R},+)
.
From the viewpoint of convolutional networks this result is very intuitive:
The
\{e\}
-steerable kernels in these examples are unconstrained, i.e. conventional convolution kernels.
They do therefore in general not carry any information about their responses when being applied relative to gauge transformed reference frames.
Since the frames, and therefore kernels, in Fig.
40(b)
are differently rotated along the “left-right” direction, the kernel responses change unpredictably when translating a signal in that direction.
If the template kernels would, however be
\operatorname{SO}(2)
-steerable, they could account for the rotation of frames.
This case corresponds to the situation in Fig
41(a)
, i.e. an
\operatorname{SO}\mkern-3.6muM
-convolution.

8.3
Quotient kernel fields

Theorem
8.8
showed that the isometry equivariance of a kernel field transform requires the invariance of the corresponding kernel field.
Since the invariance constraint implies kernels to be shared over orbits as visualized in Fig.
43
, the mathematical description of such invariant kernel fields is redundant:
a single kernel at one orbit representative is sufficient to reconstruct the kernel field on the whole orbit.
In Section
8.3.2
we derive equivalent, reduced descriptions of invariant kernel fields in terms of kernels on orbit representatives.
These representative kernels are themselves constrained by the action of the stabilizer subgroup of the orbit representative.
We propose a (unique) lifting from representative kernels to invariant kernel fields, which establishes an isomorphism between both descriptions.
This lifting isomorphism suggest a way of parameterizing and constructing isometry equivariant kernel field transforms in an implementation.
Before deriving these results in Section
8.3.2
, the following Section
8.3.1
sets up the mathematical framework.

The derivations and results of this section are close in spirit to the theory of
steerable CNNs on homogeneous spaces

[
36
,
37
]
,
however, we generalize their results from homogeneous spaces to general manifolds.
When sticking to homogeneous spaces
M
, we prove that isometry equivariant kernel field transforms are equivalent to
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions.

8.3.1
Isometry induced quotient spaces

The action of a symmetry group on a space partitions it into orbits, defined as the sets of all points which are connected by the group action.
The space of such orbits is the
quotient space
w.r.t. this group action.
In the following we will discuss the quotient spaces arising from the actions of some isometry group
\mathcal{I}\leq\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
both on the manifold and on the fiber bundles.
These definitions will later allow us to share weights over orbits by acting with isometries on kernels.

Manifold quotients:

Any point
p\in M
traces out an
orbit

\displaystyle\mathcal{I}.p\,:=\,\big\{\phi(p)\;\big|\;\phi\in\mathcal{I}\,\big\}\ \subseteq\,M\,,

(330)

which is defined as the set of all points reached by acting on
p
with any isometry in
\mathcal{I}\leq\Isom(\mkern-1.5muM\mkern-0.5mu)
.
One can easily check that the relation “
p
and
q
are elements of the same orbit” is an equivalence relation (see footnote
49
) and thus
partitions
the manifold as visualized in Fig.
44(a)
.
The quotient space

\displaystyle\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM\,:=\,\big\{\mathcal{I}.p\,\big|\,p\in M\big\}

(331)

with respect to this equivalence relation is the space of all orbits, that is, each element of
\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM
corresponds to a full orbit in
M
.
76
76

76

We write
\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM
as a left quotient since
\mathcal{I}
acts on
M
from the left.

The corresponding
quotient map

\displaystyle Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.5muM$}}}:M\to\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM,\ \ p\mapsto\mathcal{I}.p

(332)

identifies a point
p\in M
with its orbit
\mathcal{I}.p\in\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM
.
For each orbit one can select an arbitrary
orbit representative
, formally determined by a
section

\displaystyle r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.0muM$}}}:\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM\to M\quad\textup{such that}\quad Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.5muM$}}}\circ r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.0muM$}}}=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM}\,,

(333)

where the last condition ensures that the representative
r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.0muM$}}}(\mathcal{I}.p)
is indeed an element of the orbit
\mathcal{I}.p
.
One is often interested in continuous (or smooth) sections, however, these do in general not exist.
We will therefore in the following
not
demand the orbit representatives to be chosen continuously and make up for this shortcoming post-hoc if necessary.
As usual for sections, they are in general only right inverses of the quotient map but not left inverses, that is,
r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.0muM$}}}\circ Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.5muM$}}}\neq\mathrm{id}_{M}
.
This is visualized by a commutative diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces M}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.0muM$}}}}
\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.5muM$}}}}

(334)

similar to that in Eq. (
149
) and a non-commutative diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces M}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces M}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.5muM$}}}}
\mathrm{id}_{M}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.0muM$}}}}

\>\!\circlearrowleft\>\!

(335)

similar to that in Eq. (
150
).
The individual fibers
\operatorname{preim}_{Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.5muM$}}}}\mkern-4.0mu(\mathcal{I}.p)=\mathcal{I}.p\subseteq M
of the quotient map
Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.5muM$}}}
are given by the orbits themselves.
Note that
M\xrightarrow{Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.5muM$}}}}\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM
is in general
not
a fiber bundle since the orbits are not necessarily homeomorphic to each other and can therefore not be locally trivialized with a shared typical fiber
F
, as required by the commutative diagram in Eq. (
131
).
Each orbit therefore has an own
type
which is in close relation to the stabilizer subgroups of the points on that particular orbit.
The
stabilizer subgroup

\displaystyle\operatorname{Stab}_{p}\,:=\,\big\{\xi\in\mathcal{I}\,\big|\,\xi(p)=p\big\}\ \leq\ \mathcal{I}

(336)

of a point
p\in M
is thereby defined as that subgroup of the isometry group which leaves
p
fixed.
In terms of the stabilizer subgroup, it holds that the orbit of a point is identified with

\displaystyle\mathcal{I}.p\ \cong\ \mathcal{I}/\operatorname{Stab}_{p}\,.

(337)

To see this claim, let
f_{p}:\mathcal{I}\to\mathcal{I}.p,\ \phi\mapsto\phi(p)
for some
p\in M
and observe that
f_{p}(\phi\circ\xi)=\phi\circ\xi(p)=\phi(p)=f_{p}(\phi)
for any
\xi\in\operatorname{Stab}_{p}
.
It can easily be shown that indeed
\operatorname{preim}_{f_{p}}\!\!\big(\phi(p)\big)=\phi.\operatorname{Stab}_{p}
is a coset of the stabilizer subgroup of
p
and thus that
f_{p}
establishes the claimed isomorphism
\mathcal{I}.p\,\cong\,\mathcal{I}/\operatorname{Stab}_{p}
.

(a)
Quotient map and orbit representatives for
M
.

(b)
Quotient map and orbit representatives for
T\mkern-1.5muM
.

Figure 44:
Quotient maps
Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.5muM$}}}
and
Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}
and orbit representatives (sections)
r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.0muM$}}}
and
r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}
for the actions of the isometry group
\mathcal{I}=\operatorname{O}(2)
on the manifold
M
in Fig.
44(a)
and on the tangent bundle
T\mkern-1.5muM
in Fig.
44(b)
.
A detailed description of both visualizations is given in the main text.

To make these constructions more intuitive, consider the example in Fig.
44(a)
with
\mathcal{I}\cong\operatorname{O}(2)
.
The orbits
\mathcal{I}.n=\{n\}
and
\mathcal{I}.s=\{s\}
of the north and south pole are just points, which are fixed by
\mathcal{I}
.
This agrees with, for instance,
\mathcal{I}.n\cong\mathcal{I}/\operatorname{Stab}_{n}=\mathcal{I}/\mathcal{I}\cong\{n\}
since
\operatorname{Stab}_{n}=\mathcal{I}
coincides with the full isometry group.
For any other point
p\in M
, the orbits
\mathcal{I}.p
are circles.
We have reflections
\operatorname{Stab}_{p}\cong{R}
(flipping over
p
) as stabilizer subgroup and thus indeed get the circle
\mathcal{I}/\operatorname{Stab}_{p}\cong\operatorname{O}(2)/{R}\cong S^{1}
as orbit type.
The quotient map
Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.5muM$}}}:M\to\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM
sends points
q\in M
to their orbits
Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.5muM$}}}(q)=\mathcal{I}.q
in the quotient space
\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM
, shown on the right.
Since the orbits can be traversed from the north to the south pole, the quotient space
\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM
has the topology of a line segment.
The section
r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.0muM$}}}:\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM\to M
picks one representative point
r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.0muM$}}}(o)\in M
for any orbit
o\in\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM
.
In general, this orbit representative does not recover a projected point.
For instance, we have that
r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.0muM$}}}Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.5muM$}}}(p)\neq p
.
One can interpret the section as embedding the quotient space
\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM
into the manifold, shown as the black line
r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.0muM$}}}(\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM)
from the north to the south pole.

Bundle quotients:

Since the isometry group acts not only on the manifold itself but via pushforwards also on the associated bundles, these bundles are in a similar manner partitioned into orbits.
To keep the discussion general, we are in the following considering a generic associated bundle
E\xrightarrow{\pi_{E}}M
, which could stand for
T\mkern-1.5muM
,
F\mkern-1.5muM
,
G\mkern-1.4muM
,
\mathcal{A}
or
\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})
.
We denote elements of the total space as
e\in E
and let
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muE\mkern-4.0mu$ }}}
be the pushforward of
\phi
on
E
as introduced in Section
8.1.2
.
The orbit of an element of the bundle is then in analogy to Eq. (
330
) given by

\displaystyle\mathcal{I}.e\>=\ \big\{\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muE\mkern-4.0mu$ }}}(e)\,\big|\,\phi\in\mathcal{I}\big\}

(338)

while the quotient space, consisting of bundle orbits, is analogously to Eq. (
331
) defined as

\displaystyle\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muE\>=\ \big\{\mathcal{I}.e\,\big|\,e\in E\big\}\,.

(339)

Similar to before, the (canonical) quotient map sends bundle elements to their orbit:

\displaystyle Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0muE$}}}:E\mapsto\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muE,\ \ e\mapsto\mathcal{I}.e

(340)

We define a (uniquely determined) projection map

\displaystyle\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muE$}}}\!:\,\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muE\to\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM,\quad Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0muE$}}}(e)\mapsto Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.5muM$}}}\circ\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\mkern-8.0muE\!\!$ }}}(e)

(341)

between the bundle quotients and manifold quotient as visualized in the following commutative diagram:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muE}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces E}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces M}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muE$}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0muE$}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\mkern-8.0muE\!\!$ }}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.5muM$}}}}

(342)

Note that the definition in Eq. (
341
) does not depend on the particular choice of orbit representative since for any other
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muE\mkern-4.0mu$ }}}(e)\in Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0muE$}}}(e)
we obtain the same result:

Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.5muM$}}}\circ\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\mkern-8.0muE\!\!$ }}}\circ\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muE\mkern-4.0mu$ }}}(e)\,=\,Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.5muM$}}}\circ\phi\circ\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\mkern-8.0muE\!\!$ }}}(e)\,=\,Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.5muM$}}}\circ\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\mkern-8.0muE\!\!$ }}}(e).

Orbit representatives are formally determined by a choice of section

\displaystyle r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.5muE$}}}:\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muE\to E\quad\textup{such that}\quad Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0muE$}}}\circ r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.5muE$}}}=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muE}\,,

(343)

which we again do not demand to be continuous.
However, for convenience we demand the representatives of bundle orbits to lie above the representatives
r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.0muM$}}}(\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM)
in the base space, that is, to satisfy

\displaystyle\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\mkern-8.0muE\!\!$ }}}\circ r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.5muE$}}}\ =\ r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.0muM$}}}\circ\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muE$}}}

(344)

as shown in the commutative diagram below:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muE}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces E}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces M}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muE$}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.5muE$}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\mkern-8.0muE\!\!$ }}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.0muM$}}}}

(345)

The stabilizer subgroup of a bundle element
e\in E
is defined as

\displaystyle\operatorname{Stab}_{e}\,:=\,\big\{\xi\in\mathcal{I}\;\big|\;\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\!E$ }}}e=e\big\}\ \leq\ \operatorname{Stab}_{\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\mkern-8.0muE\!\!$ }}}(e)}\ \leq\ \mathcal{I}\,.

(346)

It is necessarily a subgroup of the stabilizer subgroup
\operatorname{Stab}_{\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\mkern-8.0muE\!\!$ }}}(e)}
of the point
\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\mkern-8.0muE\!\!$ }}}(e)
in the base space, which is easily seen by

\ \xi\in\operatorname{Stab}_{e}\ \Leftrightarrow\ \xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\!E$ }}}e=e\ \Rightarrow\ \pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\mkern-8.0muE\!\!$ }}}(\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\!E$ }}}e)=\xi\,\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\mkern-8.0muE\!\!$ }}}(e)=\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\mkern-8.0muE\!\!$ }}}(e)\ \Leftrightarrow\ \xi\in\operatorname{Stab}_{\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\mkern-8.0muE\!\!$ }}}(e)}.

As before, the relation
\mathcal{I}.e\cong\mathcal{I}/\operatorname{Stab}_{e}
holds.

We extend our example from Fig.
44(a)
by considering the action of
\mathcal{I}\cong\operatorname{O}(2)
on the tangent bundle
T\mkern-1.5muM
of the egg
M
in Fig.
44(b)
.
The orbit (violet) of a non-zero vector
0\neq w\in T_{n}M
(red) at the north pole
n
describes a circle in
T_{n}M
.
This is consistent with
\mathcal{I}.w\cong\mathcal{I}/\operatorname{Stab}_{w}\cong\operatorname{O}(2)/{R}\cong S^{1}
since such a vector is stabilized by reflections
\operatorname{Stab}_{w}\cong{R}
along its axis.
The orbit of
0\in T_{n}M
is a single point in
T\mkern-1.5muM
, which is stabilized by any isometry.
Any other vector
v\in T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
(red), living in a tangent space at a point
p\in M
different from the poles, is by the action of the isometry group rotated and reflected to other tangent spaces
T_{\mkern-1.5mu\phi(p)}\mkern-1.0muM
on the orbit
\mathcal{I}.p
of
p
.
The orbit
\mathcal{I}.v
(orange) of any such vector, if not pointing exactly to the north or south, is given by an eastward and a westward pointing copy of the vector in each of the tangent spaces over
\mathcal{I}.p
.
We have
\operatorname{Stab}_{v}=\{e\}
for such vectors and indeed the orbit
\mathcal{I}.v\cong\mathcal{I}/\operatorname{Stab}_{v}\cong\operatorname{O}(2)/\{e\}
is homeomorphic to
\operatorname{O}(2)
(or two circles).
Vectors
v^{\prime}\in T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
which do point exactly north- or southwards are stabilized by reflections over the axis which they define, that is,
\operatorname{Stab}_{v^{\prime}}\cong{R}
.
Their orbit is homeomorphic to a circle
\mathcal{I}.v^{\prime}\cong\mathcal{I}/\operatorname{Stab}_{v^{\prime}}\cong\operatorname{O}(2)/{R}\cong S^{1}
.

The quotient map
Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}:T\mkern-1.5muM\to\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muT\mkern-1.5muM
projects the tangent bundle to the bundle quotient
\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muT\mkern-1.5muM
, shown in the right half of Fig.
44(b)
.
To understand its structure, we consider all qualitatively different cases:
Firstly, note that the orbits of vectors at the poles correspond to circles of a certain radius, such that the set of such orbits forms a line
\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muE$}}}^{-1}(\mathcal{I}.n)\cong\mathbb{R}^{+}
(pink ray under the black arrow).
Similarly, the orbits of vectors at any other point
p\in M
intersect all tangent spaces
T_{\mkern-1.5mu\phi(p)}\mkern-1.0muM
over
\mathcal{I}.p
in two reflections and therefore form a half plane
\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muE$}}}^{-1}(\mathcal{I}.p)\cong\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^{+}
(orange).
The section
r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}:\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muT\mkern-1.5muM\to T\mkern-1.5muM
sends each bundle quotient element to some representative in
T\mkern-1.5muM
.
By the requirement in Eq. (
344
), these representatives are required to lie in the same fiber over the representatives
r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.0muM$}}}(\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM)
of the manifold quotient
\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM
, shown as the black line.
For instance,
v\in T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
(red) is by the quotient map sent to
Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}(v)\in\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muT\mkern-1.5muM
(black).
The section represents
Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}(v)
by
r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}(v)
(also black), which is an element of
T_{r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.0muM$}}}Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.5muM$}}}(p)}M
and does in general differ from
v
.

8.3.2
Quotient representative kernel fields and stabilizer constraints

To motivate the construction of quotient representative kernel fields and stabilizer constraints, consider the more explicit formulation

\displaystyle\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,${Hom} }}}\!\circ\mathcal{K}_{p}\circ\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}\,=\ \mathcal{K}_{\phi(p)}\qquad\forall\,p\in M,\ \ \phi\in\mathcal{I}\,.

(347)

of the isometry invariance constraint from Def.
8.7
, which follows by writing out Eq. (
317
) for any point
{p\in M}
individually.
This formulation emphasizes that the constraint leads to
shared weights along the manifold orbits

\mathcal{I}.p\in\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM
as visualized in Figs.
43
and
45
.
It implies that the kernel
\mathcal{K}_{r}
at an
arbitrary representative point

r=r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.0muM$}}}(o)
of any orbit
o=\mathcal{I}.r
fully specifies the kernel field on the rest of the orbit, i.e. at all points
\phi(r)
where
\phi\in\mathcal{I}
.
The kernel
\mathcal{K}_{r}
at the representative point
r
is itself constrained by the stabilizer subgroup of
r
:

\displaystyle\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,$Hom }}}\!\circ\mathcal{K}_{r}\circ\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}\,=\ \mathcal{K}_{r}\qquad\forall\,\xi\in\operatorname{Stab}_{r}\,.

(348)

This implies that any isometry invariant kernel field can be parameterized in terms of a field of kernels on manifold orbit representatives
r\in r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.0muM$}}}(\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM)
which satisfy Eq. (
348
).

In case that the stabilizer subgroup at
r
happens to be non-trivial, the stabilizer constraint in Eq. (
348
) implies further symmetries of the kernel
\mathcal{K}_{r}
at
r
itself.
For instance, in the example in Fig.
45
one has the stabilizer subgroup
{\operatorname{Stab}_{r}\cong{R}}
on the highlighted orbit, enforcing a reflectional symmetry of the kernels.
Such stabilizer symmetries allows to compress the description of isometry invariant kernel fields further:
it turns out to be sufficient to know the values
\mathcal{K}(w)
of the kernel field on the tangent bundle quotient representatives
w\in r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}(\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muT\mkern-1.5muM)\subseteq T\mkern-1.5muM
only.
In Fig.
45
this corresponds to knowing the kernel values on the orange highlighted half space, from which the full field on the orbit can be reconstructed by the reflectional and rotational symmetries in
\mathcal{I}\cong\operatorname{O}(2)
.

Theorem
8.12
below makes the latter claim precise by proving that the space
{K}_{\textup{invar}}^{\mathcal{I}}
of isometry invariant kernel fields is isomorphic to a space
{K}_{\textup{quot}}^{\mathcal{I}}
of kernel fields on tangent bundle orbit representatives
r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}(\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muT\mkern-1.5muM)
.

{K}_{\textup{quot}}^{\mathcal{I}}
is characterized by maximally reduced constraints and thus encodes the kernel fields in
{K}_{\textup{invar}}^{\mathcal{I}}
in a non-redundant way.
It can therefore be viewed as the distilled degrees of freedom contained in
{K}_{\textup{invar}}^{\mathcal{I}}
.
In Theorem
8.13
we formulate a third isomorphic space
\mathbin{\hbox{\hskip 12.71877pt\hskip-12.71877pt\hbox{$\hbox{${K}_{\textup{quot}}^{\mathcal{I}}$}$}\hskip-12.71877pt\hskip-2.77779pt\raisebox{3.36446pt}{\hbox{$\rule{-5.5pt}{0.0pt}\rule{-5.5pt}{0.0pt}\hbox{$\widehat{\rule{10.0pt}{0.0pt}}$}$}}\hskip-2.77779pt\hskip 12.71877pt}}
, which equivalently describes isometry invariant kernel fields in terms of the stabilizer subgroup constrained kernels
\mathcal{K}_{r}
from Eq. (
348
).
While the formulation of isometry invariant kernel fields in terms of
\mathbin{\hbox{\hskip 12.71877pt\hskip-12.71877pt\hbox{$\hbox{${K}_{\textup{quot}}^{\mathcal{I}}$}$}\hskip-12.71877pt\hskip-2.77779pt\raisebox{3.36446pt}{\hbox{$\rule{-5.5pt}{0.0pt}\rule{-5.5pt}{0.0pt}\hbox{$\widehat{\rule{10.0pt}{0.0pt}}$}$}}\hskip-2.77779pt\hskip 12.71877pt}}
involves stronger constraints than that in terms of
{K}_{\textup{quot}}^{\mathcal{I}}
, it might be more convenient for implementations, since it describes kernels on full tangent spaces instead of kernels on quotients of tangent spaces.

Figure 45:
Visualization of an isometry invariant kernel field, Def.
8.7
, and its full reconstruction from kernels on quotient representatives only.
In contrast to Fig
43
, we assume here an isometry group
\mathcal{I}=\operatorname{O}(2)
instead of
\operatorname{SO}(2)
.
The visualized kernels therefore have a reflectional symmetry, which is enforced by the stabilizer subgroups
\operatorname{Stab}_{p}\!\cong\!{R}
of points on the orbit
\mathcal{I}.\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}(v)
.
Due to its symmetry, the full kernel field
\mathcal{K}:T\mkern-1.5muM\to\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})
can be reconstructed from its restriction to the bundle quotient representative
r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}(\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muT\mkern-1.5muM)\subseteq T\mkern-1.5muM
; see Theorem
8.12
.
For instance, the shown kernels are fully determined by the partial kernel on the orange half space.
The reconstruction at
v\in T\mkern-1.5muM
is done by evaluating the quotient representative kernel at
r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}(v)\in r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}(\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muT\mkern-1.5muM)

349
), back to
v
.
We want to mention that the visualized
anti
symmetric kernels would result when mapping between feature fields of even and odd parity, while kernels between feature fields of the same parity would be symmetric.

\operatorname{Stab}_{r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}(v)}
.
This is easily seen by observing that for any
w\in T\mkern-1.5muM
, any
\xi\in\operatorname{Stab}_{w}
and any
\mathcal{K}\in{K}_{\textup{invar}}^{\mathcal{I}}
one has
\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,$Hom }}}\mathcal{K}(w)=\mathcal{K}(\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}w)=\mathcal{K}(w)
, which implies that
\operatorname{Stab}_{\mathcal{K}(w)}\geq\operatorname{Stab}_{w}
, and thus that the final result does not depend on the particular choice of the ambiguous
\Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.0mu
.

Since the lift
\Lambda
recovers invariant kernel fields from their restriction to tangent bundle orbit representatives, it can be viewed as the
inverse

This viewpoint implies that the lift establishes an

\Lambda:{K}_{\textup{quot}}^{\mathcal{I}}\to{K}_{\textup{invar}}^{\mathcal{I}}
between the image of the restriction
{K}_{\textup{quot}}^{\mathcal{I}}
, which we still need to characterize, and

:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{K}_{\textup{quot}}^{\mathcal{I}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{K}_{\textup{invar}}^{\mathcal{I}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Lambda}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Lambda^{-1}=(\,\cdot\,)|_{r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}(\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muT\mkern-1.5muM)}}

In order to characterize the space
{K}_{\textup{quot}}^{\mathcal{I}}
which makes
\Lambda
to an isomorphism, it is sufficient to list the properties of restricted fields
\mathcal{Q}:=\mathcal{K}|_{r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}\mkern-1.5mu(\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muT\mkern-1.5muM)}\in{K}_{\textup{quot}}^{\mathcal{I}}
for
\mathcal{K}\in{K}_{\textup{invar}}^{\mathcal{I}}
:

First of all, since
\Lambda^{-1}
is given by the restriction of the domain to

is required to be of the form

.

Secondly, the property of kernel fields to be bundle
M
-morphisms translates under the restriction
\Lambda^{-1}
to the requirement on
\mathcal{Q}
to satisfy
\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ \!Hom}}}\circ\mathcal{Q}(w)=\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}(w)
for any

Thirdly,
\mathcal{Q}
is required to satisfy the
(vector) stabilizer constraint

\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,$Hom }}}\mathcal{Q}(w)=\mathcal{Q}(w)
for any representative vector
w\mkern-2.0mu\in\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}(\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muT\mkern-1.5muM)
and any
\xi\mkern-1.0mu\in\mkern-1.0mu\operatorname{Stab}_{w}
.
This requirement is a residual from the invariance constraint in Eq. (
317
), surviving the restriction.

It can be deduced by considering the full constraint
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,${Hom} }}}\mathcal{Q}\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}(w)=\mathcal{Q}(w)
for any
w\in r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}(\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muT\mkern-1.5muM)
and any isometry
\phi\in\mathcal{I}
which additionally satisfies that
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}(w)\in r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}(\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muT\mkern-1.5muM)
, i.e. that the pushforward
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}(w)
stays within the restricted domain of
\mathcal{Q}
.
Note that
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}(w)\in\mathcal{I}.w
and that
r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}(\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muT\mkern-1.5muM)
intersects each orbit exactly once.
This implies that
\mathcal{I}.w\cap r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}(\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muT\mkern-1.5muM)=\{w\}
such that
\phi\in\mathcal{I}
is required to satisfy
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}(w)=w
, that is,
\phi\in\operatorname{Stab}_{w}
.
The claimed (vector) stabilizer constraint follows from these considerations.

For an intuition we refer back to Fig.
45
where the black representative vector
w=r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}(v)
is stabilized only by the trivial isometry
\xi=\{e\}
, implying that the corresponding value of
\mathcal{Q}
is unconstrained.
Vectors

which point exactly north- or southwards, i.e. which lie on the dashed reflection axis, are stabilized by reflections in
\operatorname{Stab}_{w^{\prime}}\cong{R}
, implying a constraint on the corresponding kernel values.

The exact constraint depends on the action

on

, which depends on
\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{{Hom}}}}
and thus on

and
\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}
.
The visualized kernel in Fig. (

being the sign-flip (odd parity) representation of the reflection group, which enforces antisymmetric kernels.
The antisymmetry requires

to be constrained to

for

on the reflection axis; cf. Table

As a last requirement,

Proof
:

In order to prove that
\Lambda:{K}_{\textup{quot}}^{\mathcal{I}}\to{K}_{\textup{invar}}^{\mathcal{I}}
is an isomorphism, we need to show that
1)
\Lambda^{-1}
is indeed an inverse of
\Lambda
, that
2) the defining properties of
{K}_{\textup{invar}}^{\mathcal{I}}
and
{K}_{\textup{quot}}^{\mathcal{I}}
are satisfied after lifting and restricting and that
3) the constructions do not depend on arbitrary choices.
In order to not overload this section, we outsource the full proof to Appendix
E.1
.
The individual steps of the proof are listed below:

1 a)

\Lambda\circ\Lambda^{-1}=\mathrm{id}_{{K}_{\textup{invar}}^{\mathcal{I}}}
,
that is,
\Lambda^{-1}
is a right inverse of
\Lambda

1 b)

\Lambda^{-1}\circ\Lambda=\mathrm{id}_{{K}_{\textup{quot}}^{\mathcal{I}}}
,
that is,
\Lambda^{-1}
is a left inverse of
\Lambda

2 a)

\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ \!Hom}}}\mkern-5.0mu\circ\mkern-2.0mu\Lambda(\mathcal{Q})=\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}
for any
\mathcal{Q}\in{K}_{\textup{quot}}^{\mathcal{I}}
,
that is, the lift
\Lambda(\mathcal{Q})
is a bundle
M
-morphism

2 b)

{\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ \!Hom}}}\mkern-5.0mu\circ\mkern-2.0mu\Lambda^{-1}(\mathcal{K})=\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}}
for any
\mathcal{K}\in{K}_{\textup{invar}}^{\mathcal{I}}

2 c)

\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,${Hom} }}}\Lambda(\mathcal{Q})\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}=\Lambda(\mathcal{Q})\ \ \forall\phi\in\mathcal{I}
,
that is,
\Lambda(\mathcal{Q})
satisfies the full isometry invariance (equivariance) constraint

2 d)

\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,$Hom }}}\big[\Lambda^{-1}(\mathcal{K})\big](w)=\big[\Lambda^{-1}(\mathcal{K})\big](w)\ \ \ \forall\;w\mkern-2.0mu\in\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}(\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muT\mkern-1.5muM),\ \xi\mkern-1.0mu\in\mkern-1.0mu\operatorname{Stab}_{w}
, that is,
\Lambda^{-1}(\mathcal{K})
satisfies the stabilizer constraint

3)

All constructions and proofs are independent from the particular choice of
\Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.0mu

The smoothness of lifted quotient representative kernel fields holds by definition.

\Box

The arbitrariness in the choice of section

allows for different, isomorphic quotient kernel fields, expressed on different bundle quotient representatives.

only, i.e. to

\displaystyle\widehat{\Lambda}^{-1}(\mathcal{K}):\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}^{-1}\big(r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.0muM$}}}(\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM)\big)\to\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ \!Hom}}}^{-1}\big(r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.0muM$}}}(\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM)\big),\ \ \ \widehat{w}\mapsto\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big[$}}}}}\widehat{\Lambda}^{-1}(\mathcal{K})\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big]$}}}}}(\widehat{w})\,:=\,\mathcal{K}\big|_{\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}^{-1}(r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.0muM$}}}(\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM))}(\widehat{w})
