), leads to

\displaystyle\big[\Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(v)^{-1}\,\phi\;\Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}v)\big]_{*,\scalebox{.58}{$\Hom$}}\mathcal{Q}\;r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}(v)\ =\ \mathcal{Q}\;r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}(v)\,.

(683)

Putting these observations together proves the claim:

\displaystyle\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,${Hom} }}}\Lambda(\mathcal{Q})\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}(v)\ =

\displaystyle\ \phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,${Hom} }}}\Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}v)_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\Hom$}}}\mathcal{Q}\;r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}\big(\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}v\big)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,${Hom} }}}\Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}v)_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\Hom$}}}\mathcal{Q}\;r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}(v)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \big[\Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(v)\,\Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(v)^{-1}\big]_{*,\scalebox{.58}{$\Hom$}}\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,${Hom} }}}\,\Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}v)_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\Hom$}}}\mathcal{Q}\;r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}(v)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(v)_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\Hom$}}}\,\big[\Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(v)^{-1}\,\phi\;\Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}v)\big]_{*,\scalebox{.58}{$\Hom$}}\mathcal{Q}\;r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}(v)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(v)_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\Hom$}}}\,\mathcal{Q}\;r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}(v)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \Lambda(\mathcal{Q})

(684)

2 d)

\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,$Hom }}}\big[\Lambda^{-1}(\mathcal{K})\big](w)=\big[\Lambda^{-1}(\mathcal{K})\big](w)\ \ \ \forall\;w\mkern-2.0mu\in\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}(\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muT\mkern-1.5muM),\ \xi\mkern-1.0mu\in\mkern-1.0mu\operatorname{Stab}_{w}
, that is,
\Lambda^{-1}(\mathcal{K})
satisfies the stabilizer constraint :

This statement is easily proven since the invariance (equivariance) properties of
\mathcal{K}
carry over to its restriction
\Lambda^{-1}(\mathcal{K})
.
We obtain for arbitrary
w\in r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}(\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muT\mkern-1.5muM)
and
\xi\in\operatorname{Stab}_{w}
, that:

\displaystyle\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,$Hom }}}\big[\Lambda^{-1}(\mathcal{K})\big](w)\ =

\displaystyle\ \xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,$Hom }}}\mathcal{K}|_{r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}\mkern-1.5mu(\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muT\mkern-1.5muM)}(w)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,$Hom }}}\mathcal{K}(w)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \mathcal{K}\big(\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}w\big)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \mathcal{K}(w)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \mathcal{K}|_{r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}\mkern-1.5mu(\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muT\mkern-1.5muM)}(w)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \big[\Lambda^{-1}(\mathcal{K})\big](w)

(685)

3)
All constructions and proofs are independent from the particular choice of
\Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.0mu
:

The definition

\displaystyle\Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.0mu:TM\to\mathcal{I}\quad\textup{such that}\quad\Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(v)_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}(v)=v

(686)

from Eq. (
349
) is unique up to right multiplication of
\Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.0mu
with
any

\displaystyle\xi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.0mu:TM\to\mathcal{I}\quad\textup{such that}\quad\xi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(v)\in\operatorname{Stab}_{r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}(v)}

(687)

since, obviously,
\Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(v)_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}\,\xi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(v)_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}\,r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}(v)\ =\ \Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(v)_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}\,r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}(v)\ =\,v\,
for any
v\in TM
.
As argued in footnote
78
, this covers all degrees of freedom in the definition of reconstruction isometries.
From the stabilizer constraint in Eq. (
356
) it follows that
\xi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(v)_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\Hom$}}}\mathcal{Q}\,r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}(v)=\mathcal{Q}\,r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}(v)
such that the lift
\Lambda
is seen to be invariant w.r.t. the ambiguity of
\Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.0mu
:

\displaystyle\Lambda(\mathcal{Q})\ =

\displaystyle\ \Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(v)_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\Hom$}}}\mathcal{Q}\,r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}(v)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(v)_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\Hom$}}}\,\xi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(v)_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\Hom$}}}\mathcal{Q}\,r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}(v)

Except from the definition of the lifting isomorphism,
\Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.0mu
is only used (in a slightly different context) in step
2 c)
, where the ambiguity is seen to drop out by similar arguments.

Together, these steps prove that
\Lambda:{K}_{\textup{quot}}^{\mathcal{I}}\to{K}_{\textup{invar}}^{\mathcal{I}}
is an isomorphism.

\Box

E.2
Proof of Theorem
8.14
– Equivalence of equivariant kernel field transforms and convolutions on homogeneous spaces

To keep a better overview, we split the proof in two parts, proving the claims made in the first and second statement of Theorem
8.14
, respectively.

Part 1) – Constructing
H
,
HM
and Isom
HM
:

Let
r\in M
be any representative point and, without loss of generality, let
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}
be any isometric gauge at
r
.
We set

\displaystyle H\ :=\ \psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\,\operatorname{Stab}_{r}\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}\,,

(689)

which is just a particular representation of
\operatorname{Stab}_{r}
relative to the chosen coordinatization.
Since the gauge maps are isomorphisms, we get an isomorphism between the two groups:

\displaystyle\alpha:\operatorname{Stab}_{r}\to H,\ \ \ \xi\to\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\;\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\,\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}=:h_{\xi}^{\widetilde{A}\widetilde{A}}(r)

(690)

Since
\operatorname{Stab}_{r}\leq\mathcal{I}\leq\Isom_{G\mkern-1.4muM}
, Theorem
8.3
assures that
h_{\xi}^{\widetilde{A}\widetilde{A}}(r)
is for any
\xi\in\operatorname{Stab}_{p}
an element of
G
and thus that
H\leq G
.
We furthermore have that
H\leq\operatorname{O}(d)
, which is seen by the following calculation, which holds for any
{v},{w}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}
:

\displaystyle\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{339817}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\Big\langle$}}}}h_{\xi}^{\widetilde{A}\widetilde{A}}(r)\cdot{v}\,,\,\ h_{\xi}^{\widetilde{A}\widetilde{A}}(r)\cdot{w}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{339817}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\Big\rangle$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{339817}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\Big\rangle$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{339817}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big\rangle$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{339817}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big\rangle$}}}}}\ \overset{(1)}{=}

\displaystyle\ \ \mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{339817}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\Big\langle$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{339817}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\Big\langle$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{339817}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big\langle$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{339817}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big\langle$}}}}}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big($}}}}}\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\;\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\,\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}\cdot{v}\,,\,\ \mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big($}}}}}\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\;\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\,\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}\cdot{w}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{339817}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\Big\rangle$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{339817}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\Big\rangle$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{339817}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big\rangle$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{339817}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big\rangle$}}}}}

\displaystyle\ \overset{(2)}{=}

\displaystyle\ \ \mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{339817}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\Big\langle$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{339817}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\Big\langle$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{339817}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big\langle$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{339817}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big\langle$}}}}}\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\;\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}\,\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}\,{v}\,,\,\ \psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\;\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}\,\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}\,{w}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{339817}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\Big\rangle$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{339817}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\Big\rangle$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{339817}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big\rangle$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{339817}{655360}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big\rangle$}}}}}

\displaystyle\ \overset{(3)}{=}

\displaystyle\ \ \eta_{r}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big($}}}}}\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}\,\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}\,{v}\,,\,\ \xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}\,\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}\,{w}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}

\displaystyle\ \overset{(4)}{=}

\displaystyle\ \ \eta_{r}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big($}}}}}\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}\,{v}\,,\,\ \big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}\,{w}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}

\displaystyle\ \overset{(5)}{=}

\displaystyle\ \ \langle{v}\,,{w}\rangle

(691)

Step
(1)
made use of Eq. (
690
).
In step
(2)
we identified the expression of
h_{\xi}^{\widetilde{A}\widetilde{A}}(r)
via
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}
with its expression via
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}
, which is justified by the commutativity of the diagrams in Eqs. (
301
) and (
287
).
As we assumed
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}
w.l.o.g. to be isometric, we can identify the inner product
\langle\,\cdot,\cdot\,\rangle
on
\mathbb{R}^{d}
in step
(3)
with the Riemannian metric
\eta_{r}
.
Step
(4)
uses that
\xi\in\operatorname{Stab}_{r}\leq\mathcal{I}
is an isometry, which preserves the metric by definition; see Eq. (
264
).
Lastly, we pull the metric in step
(5)
via the isometric gauge back to the inner product on
\mathbb{R}^{d}
.
The equality of the initial and final expression shows that
h_{\xi}^{\widetilde{A}\widetilde{A}}(r)
preserves the inner product on
\mathbb{R}^{d}
– this is exactly the requirement that
defines
the orthogonal group.
We therefore have that
H\leq\operatorname{O}(d)
, and, together with
H\leq G
, that

\displaystyle H\,\leq\,G\cap\operatorname{O}(d)\,.

(692)

This proves the first statement of part 1) of Theorem
8.14
.
We move on to the second statement of part 1), the construction of
H\mkern-2.5muM
and
\Isom_{H\mkern-2.5muM}
.

Given that
\operatorname{Stab}_{r}
is a subgroup of
\mathcal{I}
, we have the canonical quotient map

\displaystyle{q}:\mathcal{I}\to\mathcal{I}/\operatorname{Stab}_{r},\ \ \ \phi\to\phi.\operatorname{Stab}_{r}

(693)

which sends group elements
\phi\in\mathcal{I}
to the left coset
\phi.\operatorname{Stab}_{r}:=\{\phi\,\xi\,|\,\xi\in\operatorname{Stab}_{r}\}
of
\operatorname{Stab}_{r}
.
It is well known that this quotient map makes
\mathcal{I}
to a principal
\operatorname{Stab}_{r}
-bundle over the base space
\mathcal{I}/\operatorname{Stab}_{r}
, with the right action given by the right multiplication
\blacktriangleleft\,:\mathcal{I}\times\operatorname{Stab}_{r}\to\mathcal{I},\ (\phi,\xi)\mapsto\phi\,\xi
with stabilizer elements
[
74
,
163
]
.
Furthermore,
\mathcal{I}/\operatorname{Stab}_{r}
is isomorphic to the homogeneous space
M
.
The isomorphism is given by

\displaystyle\beta:\mathcal{I}/\operatorname{Stab}_{r}\to M,\ \ \ \phi.\operatorname{Stab}_{r}\mapsto\phi(r)\,,

(694)

which is obviously independent of the choice of coset representative since different representatives differ by group elements that stabilize
r
.
Note that we could equally well view
{q}:\mathcal{I}\to\mathcal{I}/\operatorname{Stab}_{r}
as a principal
H
-bundle since the typical fiber is only defined up to isomorphism.

With these preparations we define the
H
-structure
H\mkern-2.5muM
as an embedding of the principal
H
-bundle
\mathcal{I}
into
G\mkern-1.4muM
(and therefore into
F\mkern-1.5muM
).
We define the embedding map as

\displaystyle{E}:\mathcal{I}\to G\mkern-1.4muM,\ \ \ \phi\mapsto\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\,\sigma^{\widetilde{A}}(r)\,,

(695)

which depends once again on our choice of gauge since
\sigma^{\widetilde{A}}(r)=\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}(e)
.
It can be thought of as tracing out an embedded copy of
\mathcal{I}
in
G\mkern-1.4muM
by pushing around the frame
\sigma^{\widetilde{A}}(r)\in G_{\mkern-1.3mur}\mkern-1.3muM
.
That this gives indeed a valid embedding is guaranteed since the action of
\mathcal{I}
on frames is fixed point free.
The embedding
{E}
is a bundle map over
\beta
, that is,
\beta\circ{q}=\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!G\!M$}}}\circ{E}
.
To show this, it is sufficient to apply both sides on an arbitrary element
\phi\in\mathcal{I}
, which gives the same result:

\beta\circ{q}(\phi)=\beta\big(\phi.\operatorname{Stab}_{r}\big)=\phi(r)
and

\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!G\!M$}}}\circ{E}(\phi)=\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!G\!M$}}}\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\,\sigma^{\widetilde{A}}(r)=\phi\;\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!G\!M$}}}\,\sigma^{\widetilde{A}}(r)=\phi(r)
.
The embedding map is furthermore right equivariant:
For any
\xi\in\operatorname{Stab}_{r}
and any
\phi\in\mathcal{I}
one has

\displaystyle{E}(\phi\,\xi)\ =

\displaystyle\ \ \phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\,\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\sigma^{\widetilde{A}}(r)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \ \phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\,\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}(e)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \ \phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\,\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\,\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}(e)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \ \phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\,\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}\big(h_{\xi}^{\widetilde{A}\widetilde{A}}(r)\big)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \ \phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\,\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}(e)\lhd h_{\xi}^{\widetilde{A}\widetilde{A}}(r)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \ {E}(\phi)\lhd h_{\xi}^{\widetilde{A}\widetilde{A}}(r)\,,

(696)

where we used the right
G
(and thus
H
) equivariance of
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}
(and thus
\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$G\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}
) in the penultimate step.
Together, these properties show that
{E}
is a principal bundle map that makes the following diagram commutative:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{I}\times\operatorname{Stab}_{r}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G\mkern-1.4muM\times H}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{I}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G\mkern-1.4muM}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{I}/\operatorname{Stab}_{r}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces M}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{E}\times\alpha}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\blacktriangleleft\,}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\,\lhd}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{E}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{q}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!G\!M$}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\beta}

(697)

The claimed
H
-structure is then defined as the image

\displaystyle H\mkern-2.5muM\ :=\ {E}(\mathcal{I})\ =\ \big\{\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\,\sigma^{\widetilde{A}}(r)\,\big|\,\phi\in\mathcal{I}\big\}

(698)

of
{E}
together with the restricted right action and projection map of
G\mkern-1.4muM
.
Since embeddings are necessarily injective, we have in particular that
\mathcal{I}
and
H\mkern-2.5muM
are isomorphic as principal bundles.

As a last point we argue that
\mathcal{I}
and
\Isom_{H\mkern-2.5muM}=\{\theta\in\Isom(\mkern-1.5muM\mkern-0.5mu)\,|\,\theta_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}H\mkern-2.5muM=H\mkern-2.5muM\}
coincide.
The equality
\theta_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}H\mkern-2.5muM=H\mkern-2.5muM
holds for a given
\theta\in\Isom(\mkern-1.5muM\mkern-0.5mu)
if
\theta_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}H\mkern-2.5muM
is at the same time a subset and a superset of
H\mkern-2.5muM
.
The first case,
\theta_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}H\mkern-2.5muM\subseteq H\mkern-2.5muM
, requires that for any element
\theta_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\sigma^{\widetilde{A}}(r)\in\theta_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}H\mkern-2.5muM
, there exists some
\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}^{\prime}\sigma^{\widetilde{A}}(r)\in H\mkern-2.5muM
such that
\theta_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\,\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\sigma^{\widetilde{A}}(r)=\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}^{\prime}\sigma^{\widetilde{A}}(r)
.
Since the action of isometries on the frame bundle is free, this requires
\theta_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}=\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}^{\prime}\phi_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}^{-1}
, which in turn implies
\theta=\phi^{\prime}\phi^{-1}
.
As one can easily check, the second case results in the same requirement.
Both
\phi^{\prime}
and
\phi
are elements of
\mathcal{I}
such that
\theta
is required to be an element of
\mathcal{I}
.
This proves the claim

\displaystyle\Isom_{H\mkern-2.5muM}=\mathcal{I}\,.

(699)

Part 2) – Equivalence of
\bm{\mathcal{I}}
-equivariant kernel field transforms and
HM
-convolutions:

To prove the second statement of the theorem, we construct an
\mathcal{I}
-equivariant kernel field transform on
M
and show that it is equivalent to a
H\mkern-2.5muM
-convolution.
Theorem
8.8
proved that
\mathcal{I}
-equivariant kernel field transforms require
\mathcal{I}
-invariant kernel fields, which can, according to Theorem
8.13
, be equivalently encoded in terms of a field of representative kernels
\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}:\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}^{-1}(r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.0muM$}}}(\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM))\to\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ \!Hom}}}^{-1}(r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.0muM$}}}(\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM))
.
For the case of a homogeneous space
M
, the quotient space
\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM
consists of a single element, which we represent by
r=r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-3.0muM$}}}(\mathcal{I}\backslash\mkern-1.5muM)\in M
.
The full invariant kernel field is therefore described by a single kernel
\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}|_{r}=\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}:T_{\mkern-2.0mur}\mkern-1.0muM\to\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in},r},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out},r})
.
This kernel is required to satisfy the stabilizer constraint

\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,$Hom }}}\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}\;\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}=\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}\quad\forall\ \xi\in\operatorname{Stab}_{r}

and is shared over
M
via the lifting isomorphism

\widehat{\Lambda}(\widehat{\mathcal{Q}})(v)=\Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(v)_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\Hom$}}}\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}\ r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}(v)=\Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(v)_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\Hom$}}}\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}\ \Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(v)_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}(v)
.
As shown below, the single
\operatorname{Stab}_{r}
-constrained representative kernel corresponds exactly to an
H
-steerable template kernel, while the weight sharing via the lifting isomorphism
\widehat{\Lambda}
from Theorem
8.13
corresponds exactly to the convolutional weight sharing in Def.
7.4
.

To make the equivalence of the kernel constraints explicit, we express the kernel
\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}
via Eq. (
247
) relative to the same gauge
\widetilde{A}
as considered before as

K:=\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\,\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}\,\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}
.
The frame volume factor
\sqrt{|\eta_{r}^{\widetilde{A}}|}
drops hereby out since we assumed the gauge w.l.o.g. to be isometric.
The stabilizer constraint relative to this gauge then leads to

\displaystyle K\

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\ \ \psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\,

\displaystyle\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}\ \big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\ \ \psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\,\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,$Hom }}}\,

\displaystyle\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}\,\ \xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}\,\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\ \ \psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\,\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,$Hom }}}\,\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}})^{-1}\,

\displaystyle K\ \psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\,\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}\,\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\ \ \rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{{Hom}}}}\big(h_{\xi}^{\widetilde{A}\widetilde{A}}(r)\big)\,

\displaystyle K\ \big(h_{\xi}^{\widetilde{A}\widetilde{A}}(r)\big)^{-1}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\ \ \frac{1}{\big|\mkern-2.0mu\det h_{\xi}^{\widetilde{A}\widetilde{A}}(r)\big|}\;\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{{Hom}}}}\big(h_{\xi}^{\widetilde{A}\widetilde{A}}(r)\big)\,

\displaystyle K\ \big(h_{\xi}^{\widetilde{A}\widetilde{A}}(r)\big)^{-1}

(700)

for any
\xi
in
\operatorname{Stab}_{r}
.
Note that we can include the determinant factor in the last step since
h_{\xi}^{\widetilde{A}\widetilde{A}}(r)\in\operatorname{O}(d)
, as shown above.
The isomorphism between
\operatorname{Stab}_{r}
and
H
in Eq. (
690
) thus allows us to rewrite the stabilizer constraint as the
H
-steerability constraint

\displaystyle K\ =\ \frac{1}{|\mkern-2.0mu\det h\mkern 1.0mu|}\;\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{{Hom}}}}(h)\circ K\circ h^{-1}\qquad\forall\ h\in H\,.

(701)

on template kernels
K
of a
H\mkern-2.5muM
-convolution.
165
165

165

Since
h\in H\leq G\cap\operatorname{O}(d)
, the determinant factor always drops out and could therefore be omitted.

What remains to be shown is the equivalence of the two ways of sharing weights.
The weight sharing via
\widehat{\Lambda}
, expressed via gauge
\widetilde{A}
in terms of
K
, reads

\displaystyle\widehat{\Lambda}(\widehat{\mathcal{Q}})(v)\

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\ \Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(v)_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\Hom$}}}\;

\displaystyle\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}\,\ r_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-1.5muT\!M$}}}\,Q_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}(v)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\ \Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(v)_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\Hom$}}}\;

\displaystyle\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}\,\ \Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(v)_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}(v)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\ \Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(v)_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\Hom$}}}\,\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}\,\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\;

\displaystyle\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}\,\ \big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\big)^{-1}\,\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\;\Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(v)_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}(v)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\ \Big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\,\Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(v)_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\Hom$}}}^{-1}\Big)^{-1}\,

\displaystyle K\,\Big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\,\Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(v)_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}\Big)(v)\,.

The last line already looks quite similar to the definition of
H\mkern-2.5muM
-convolutional kernel fields in Def.
7.4
.
To prove their equivalence, we need to show
1) that the isometry induced gauges

\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\,\Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(v)_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}
and
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}\,\Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(v)_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\Hom$}}}^{-1}
at
\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}(v)

are
H
-compatible with the original gauges
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}
and
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{Hom,}\scalebox{.7}{$r$}}^{\widetilde{A}}
and
2) that the induced gauges correspond to reference frames of unit volume (to explain the missing frame volume factor in Eq. (
E.2
)).
For the first point, note that the codomain of the reconstruction isometry
\Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.0mu:T\mkern-1.5muM\to\mathcal{I}
coincides by Eq. (
699
) with
\Isom_{H\mkern-2.5muM}
.
Theorem
8.3
therefore asserts that these induced gauges are compatible with any
H
-atlas of
H\mkern-2.5muM
.
The second point follows immediately since
H\leq\operatorname{O}(d)
(or since
\Phi_{\mkern-1.0mur_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.45}{$\mkern-2.0muT\!M$}}}}\mkern-3.5mu(v)
is an isometry and
\widetilde{A}
is isometric).
The weight sharing of
\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}
via the lifting isomorphism in Eq.
E.2
is therefore seen to coincide with the
H\mkern-2.5muM
-convolutional weight sharing of the
H
-steerable kernel
K
in Def.
7.4
.
Together with the result that the stabilizer kernel constraint results in the
H
-steerability constraint, this implies that the lifted kernel field is equivalent to a
H\mkern-2.5muM
-convolutional kernel field, which proves part 2) of the theorem.

A different choice of gauge
\widetilde{A}
might for
G<\operatorname{O}(d)
result in a conjugate subgroup
\overline{H}
to
H
and an embedding
\overline{H}\mkern-2.0muM
of
\mathcal{I}
that differs from
H\mkern-2.5muM
.
As one can easily check, the
\overline{H}
-steerability constraint allows to describe the same kernel relative to
\overline{H}\mkern-2.0muM
like the
H
-steerability constraint in relation to
H\mkern-2.5muM
, since the transformation falls out.

Appendix F
Spherical steerable convolutions as
GM
-convolutions – proofs

This Section presents the proofs of Theorems
11.1
and
11.2
from Section
11.2
in the following two subsections.
Together, these theorems assert that the
\operatorname{Stab}_{n}
-steerable spherical convolution kernels by
Cohen et al. 2019a
are equivalent to certain
\operatorname{Stab}_{n}\cong G
-steerable kernels, and that the
\mathcal{I}
-equivariant spherical convolutions with these kernels are equivalent to our corresponding

-convolutions.

F.1
Proof of Theorem
11.1
– Kernel space isomorphism

Theorem

establishes an isomorphism

\displaystyle\Omega:\ {K}^{G,B_{\mathbb{R}^{2}}\mkern-1.0mu(0,\pi)}_{\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\mkern-1.0mu,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}}\xrightarrow{\,\sim\,}\,{K}^{\operatorname{Stab}_{n}}_{\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\mkern-1.0mu,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}}

(703)

between the space
{K}^{G,B_{\mathbb{R}^{2}}\mkern-1.0mu(0,\pi)}_{\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\mkern-1.0mu,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}}

) and (

).
Given arbitrary gauges

at the north pole

, around which the kernel is centered, and gauges

at any other point
