, this isomorphism is given by

\displaystyle\Omega(K)\!

\displaystyle:

\displaystyle\,\ S^{2}\backslash\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{0.75}[1.0]{$-$}\mkern 1.0mun\,

\displaystyle\to

\displaystyle\,\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}\times{c_{\textup{in}}}},\quad p\,

\displaystyle\mapsto\,\big[\Omega(K)\big](p)\

\displaystyle:=

\displaystyle\ K\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$n$}}^{N}\log_{n}p\big)\,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{n\leftarrow p}^{NP}\big)\,\sqrt{\big|\eta_{p}^{\partial\mkern-2.0mu/\mkern-2.0mu\partial{v}}\big|}^{\,-1}\,.

(704)

Abbreviating
p:=\exp_{n}\!\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$n$}}^{N}\big)^{\!-1}{v}
, its inverse is given by

\displaystyle\Omega^{-1}(\kappa)\!

\displaystyle:

\displaystyle\,\ B_{\mathbb{R}^{2}}\mkern-1.0mu(0,\pi)

\displaystyle\to

\displaystyle\mathbb{R}^{{c_{\textup{out}}}\times{c_{\textup{in}}}},\quad{v}\,

\displaystyle\mapsto\,\big[\Omega^{-1}(\kappa)\big]({v})\

\displaystyle:=

\displaystyle\ \kappa\big(\!\exp_{n}\!\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$n$}}^{N}\big)^{\!-1}{v}\big)\,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{n\leftarrow p}^{NP}\big)^{\!-1}\sqrt{\big|\eta_{p}^{\partial\mkern-2.0mu/\mkern-2.0mu\partial{v}}\big|}\!,

(705)

Proof
:

That
\Omega^{-1}
is a well defined inverse of
\Omega
is easily shown by inserting their expressions and verifying that

\displaystyle\Omega\circ\Omega^{-1}=\mathrm{id}_{{K}^{\operatorname{Stab}_{n}}_{\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\mkern-1.0mu,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}}}\qquad\textup{and}\qquad\Omega^{-1}\circ\Omega=\mathrm{id}_{{K}^{G,B_{\mathbb{R}^{2}}\mkern-1.0mu(0,\pi)}_{\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\mkern-1.0mu,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}}}

(706)

hold.
To see this, note that gauges
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$n$}}^{N}
, the transporters
\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{n\leftarrow p}^{NP}\big)
and the (non-zero) volume factor
\sqrt{\big|\eta_{p}^{\partial\mkern-2.0mu/\mkern-2.0mu\partial{v}}\big|}
are always invertible and the latter two commute since the volume scaling factor is a scalar.
The exponential map
\exp_{n}:B_{\mathbb{R}^{2}}\mkern-1.0mu(0,\pi)\to S^{2}\backslash\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{0.75}[1.0]{$-$}\mkern 1.0mun
on
B_{\mathbb{R}^{2}}\mkern-1.0mu(0,\pi)
is inverted by
\log_{n}:S^{2}\backslash\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{0.75}[1.0]{$-$}\mkern 1.0mun\to B_{\mathbb{R}^{2}}\mkern-1.0mu(0,\pi)
.

The kernel constraints of the two kernel spaces furthermore imply each other.
Given any
G
-steerable kernel
K\in{K}^{G,B_{\mathbb{R}^{2}}\mkern-1.0mu(0,\pi)}_{\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\mkern-1.0mu,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}}
, the kernel
\Omega(K)\in{K}^{\operatorname{Stab}_{n}}_{\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\mkern-1.0mu,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}}
satisfies the
\operatorname{Stab}_{n}
-steerability constraint from Eq. (
460
).
This is for any
p\in S^{2}\backslash\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{0.75}[1.0]{$-$}\mkern 1.0mun
, any
\xi\in\operatorname{Stab}_{n}
and any gauge
X
at
\xi(p)
shown by:

\displaystyle\big[\Omega(K)\big]\big(\xi(p)\big)\,

\displaystyle\overset{(1)}{=}\,K\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$n$}}^{N}\log_{n}\xi(p)\big)\cdot\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{n\leftarrow\xi(p)}^{NX}\big)\ \sqrt{\big|\eta_{\xi(p)}^{\partial\mkern-2.0mu/\mkern-2.0mu\partial{v}}\big|}^{\,-1}

\displaystyle\overset{(2)}{=}\,K\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$n$}}^{N}\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}\log_{n}p\big)\cdot\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{n\leftarrow\xi(p)}^{NX}\big)\ \sqrt{\big|\eta_{\xi(p)}^{\partial\mkern-2.0mu/\mkern-2.0mu\partial{v}}\big|}^{\,-1}

\displaystyle\overset{(3)}{=}\,K\big(g_{\xi}^{NN}(n)\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$n$}}^{N}\log_{n}p\big)\cdot\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{n\leftarrow\xi(p)}^{NX}\big)\ \sqrt{\big|\eta_{\xi(p)}^{\partial\mkern-2.0mu/\mkern-2.0mu\partial{v}}\big|}^{\,-1}

\displaystyle\overset{(4)}{=}\,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}\big(g_{\xi}^{NN}(n)\big)\cdot K\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$n$}}^{N}\log_{n}p\big)\cdot\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{\xi}^{NN}(n)\big)^{-1}\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{n\leftarrow\xi(p)}^{NX}\big)\ \sqrt{\big|\eta_{\xi(p)}^{\partial\mkern-2.0mu/\mkern-2.0mu\partial{v}}\big|}^{\,-1}

\displaystyle\overset{(5)}{=}\,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}\big(g_{\xi}^{NN}(n)\big)\cdot K\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$n$}}^{N}\log_{n}p\big)\cdot\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{\xi}^{NN}(n)\big)^{-1}\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{n\leftarrow\xi(p)}^{NX}\big)\ \sqrt{\big|\eta_{p}^{\partial\mkern-2.0mu/\mkern-2.0mu\partial{v}}\big|}^{\,-1}

\displaystyle\overset{(6)}{=}\,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}\big(g_{\xi}^{NN}(n)\big)\cdot K\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$n$}}^{N}\log_{n}p\big)\cdot\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{n\leftarrow p}^{NP}\big)\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{\xi}^{XP}(p)\big)^{-1}\ \sqrt{\big|\eta_{p}^{\partial\mkern-2.0mu/\mkern-2.0mu\partial{v}}\big|}^{\,-1}

\displaystyle\overset{(7)}{=}\,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}\big(g_{\xi}^{NN}(n)\big)\cdot\big[\Omega(K)\big](p)\cdot\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{\xi}^{XP}(p)\big)^{-1}

(707)

The first step just expanded
\Omega(K)
, while the second step used
\log_{n}\xi(p)=\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}\log_{\xi^{-1}(n)}p
, which follows from Eq. (
305
), together with
\xi^{-1}(n)=n
since
\xi\in\operatorname{Stab}_{n}
.
In the third step, we used the definition of isometry induced gauge transformations in Eq. (
286
).
Step four used the
G
-steerability constraint from Eq. (
461
).
The firth step replaced the volume element

\sqrt{\big|\eta_{\xi(p)}^{\partial\mkern-2.0mu/\mkern-2.0mu\partial{v}}\big|}

with that at

\sqrt{\big|\eta_{p}^{\partial\mkern-2.0mu/\mkern-2.0mu\partial{v}}\big|}
,
which is possible since the whole Riemannian geometry of the sphere, including the metric and exponential map and therefore the volume factors of the geodesic normal coordinates, is invariant under the action of
\operatorname{Stab}_{n}
.
Before identifying
\Omega(K)
in the last step, step six used the identity

\displaystyle\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{\xi}^{NN}(n)\big)^{-1}\,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{n\leftarrow\xi(p)}^{NX}\big)\ =

\displaystyle\ \mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big[$}}}}}\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},n}}^{N}\,\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}$ }}}^{-1}\,\big(\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},n}}^{N}\big)^{-1}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big]$}}}}}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big[$}}}}}\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},n}}^{N}\,\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}$}\mkern 0.0mu,n\leftarrow\xi(p)}}\,\big(\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},\xi(p)}}^{X}\big)^{-1}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big]$}}}}}

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},n}}^{N}\;\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}$ }}}^{-1}\,\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}$}\mkern 0.0mu,n\leftarrow\xi(p)}}\,\big(\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},\xi(p)}}^{X}\big)^{-1}

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},n}}^{N}\;\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}$}\mkern 0.0mu,n\leftarrow p}}\,\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}$ }}}^{-1}\ \big(\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},\xi(p)}}^{X}\big)^{-1}

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big[$}}}}}\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},n}}^{N}\,\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}$}\mkern 0.0mu,n\leftarrow p}}\,\big(\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},p}}^{P}\big)^{-1}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big]$}}}}}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big[$}}}}}\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},p}}^{P}\,\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}$ }}}^{-1}\,\big(\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},\xi(p)}}^{X}\big)^{-1}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big]$}}}}}

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{n\leftarrow p}^{NP}\big)\ \rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{\xi}^{XP}(p)\big)^{-1}\,,

(708)

which relies crucially on the commutativity of transporters and isometry pushforwards from Eq. (
307
).

For the opposite direction, assume a
\operatorname{Stab}_{n}
-steerable kernel
\kappa\in{K}^{\operatorname{Stab}_{n}}_{\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\mkern-1.0mu,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}}
to be given.
The corresponding kernel
\Omega^{-1}(\kappa)
satisfies then the
G
-steerability constraint from Eq. (
461
).
To show this, let
{v}\in B_{\mathbb{R}^{2}}\mkern-1.0mu(0,\pi)
, let
g\in G
and let
\xi\in\operatorname{Stab}_{n}
be the unique stabilizer element such that
g_{\xi}^{NN}(n)=\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$n$}}^{N}\,\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$n$}}^{N}\big)^{-1}=g
.
For brevity, we abbreviate
p:=\exp_{n}\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$n$}}^{N}\big)^{-1}{v}
and thus
\xi(p)=\exp_{n}\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$n$}}^{N}\big)^{-1}g{v}
, which is as justified by steps 1-3 below.
We then find:

\displaystyle\big[\Omega^{-1}(\kappa)\big](g{v})\,

\displaystyle\overset{(1)}{=}\,\kappa\big(\!\exp_{n}\!\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$n$}}^{N}\big)^{-1}(g{v})\big)\cdot\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{n\leftarrow\xi(p)}^{NX}\big)^{-1}\ \sqrt{\big|\eta_{\xi(p)}^{\partial\mkern-2.0mu/\mkern-2.0mu\partial{v}}\big|}

\displaystyle\overset{(2)}{=}\,\kappa\big(\!\exp_{n}\!\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$n$}}^{N}\big)^{-1}{v}\big)\cdot\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{n\leftarrow\xi(p)}^{NX}\big)^{-1}\ \sqrt{\big|\eta_{\xi(p)}^{\partial\mkern-2.0mu/\mkern-2.0mu\partial{v}}\big|}

\displaystyle\overset{(3)}{=}\,\kappa\big(\xi\exp_{n}\!\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$n$}}^{N}\big)^{-1}{v}\big)\cdot\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{n\leftarrow\xi(p)}^{NX}\big)^{-1}\ \sqrt{\big|\eta_{\xi(p)}^{\partial\mkern-2.0mu/\mkern-2.0mu\partial{v}}\big|}

\displaystyle\overset{(4)}{=}\,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}\big(g_{\xi}^{NN}(n)\big)\cdot\kappa\big(\exp_{n}\!\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$n$}}^{N}\big)^{-1}{v}\big)\cdot\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{\xi}^{XP}(p)\big)^{-1}\,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{n\leftarrow\xi(p)}^{NX}\big)^{-1}\ \sqrt{\big|\eta_{\xi(p)}^{\partial\mkern-2.0mu/\mkern-2.0mu\partial{v}}\big|}

\displaystyle\overset{(5)}{=}\,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}\big(g_{\xi}^{NN}(n)\big)\cdot\kappa\big(\exp_{n}\!\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$n$}}^{N}\big)^{-1}{v}\big)\cdot\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{\xi}^{XP}(p)\big)^{-1}\,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{n\leftarrow\xi(p)}^{NX}\big)^{-1}\ \sqrt{\big|\eta_{p}^{\partial\mkern-2.0mu/\mkern-2.0mu\partial{v}}\big|}

\displaystyle\overset{(6)}{=}\,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}\big(g_{\xi}^{NN}(n)\big)\cdot\kappa\big(\exp_{n}\!\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$n$}}^{N}\big)^{-1}{v}\big)\cdot\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{n\leftarrow p}^{NP}\big)^{-1}\,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{\xi}^{NN}(n)\big)^{-1}\ \sqrt{\big|\eta_{p}^{\partial\mkern-2.0mu/\mkern-2.0mu\partial{v}}\big|}

\displaystyle\overset{(7)}{=}\,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}\big(g_{\xi}^{NN}(n)\big)\cdot\big[\Omega^{-1}(\kappa)\big]({v})\cdot\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{\xi}^{NN}(n)\big)^{-1}

\displaystyle\overset{(8)}{=}\,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}(g)\cdot\big[\Omega^{-1}(\kappa)\big]({v})\cdot\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}(g)^{-1}

(709)

The first three steps expanded
\Omega^{-1}(\kappa)
, used the definition of
\xi
in terms of
g
and the commutativity of exponential maps with isometry pushforwards, Eq. (
305
).
In the fourth step, the
\operatorname{Stab}_{n}
-steerability constraint of
\kappa
from Eq. (
460
) is used.
Step five replaced again the Riemannian volume element at
\xi(p)
with that at
p
since they are equal.
The sixth step used the relation

\displaystyle\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{\xi}^{XP}(p)\big)^{-1}\,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{n\leftarrow\xi(p)}^{NX}\big)^{-1}\ =

\displaystyle\ \rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{n\leftarrow\xi(p)}^{NX}\,g_{\xi}^{XP}(p)\big)^{-1}

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \Big(\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big[$}}}}}\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},n}}^{N}\,\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}$}\mkern 0.0mu,n\leftarrow\xi(p)}}\,\big(\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},\xi(p)}}^{X}\big)^{-1}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big]$}}}}}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big[$}}}}}\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},\xi(p)}}^{X}\,\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}$ }}}\,\big(\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},p}}^{P}\big)^{-1}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big]$}}}}}\Big)^{-1}

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \Big(\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},n}}^{N}\,\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}$}\mkern 0.0mu,n\leftarrow\xi(p)}}\,\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}$ }}}\,\big(\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},p}}^{P}\big)^{-1}\Big)^{-1}

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \Big(\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},n}}^{N}\,\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}$ }}}\,\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}$}\mkern 0.0mu,n\leftarrow p}}\,\big(\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},p}}^{P}\big)^{-1}\Big)^{-1}

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \Big(\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},n}}^{N}\,\xi_{\overset{}{\mkern-1.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}$ }}}\,\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$n$}}^{N}\big)^{-1}\,\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$n$}}^{N}\,\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}$}\mkern 0.0mu,n\leftarrow p}}\,\big(\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{in}},p}}^{P}\big)^{-1}\Big)^{-1}

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{n\leftarrow p}^{NP}\big)^{-1}\,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{\xi}^{NN}(n)\big)^{-1}\,,

(710)

which relies again on the commutativity of transporters and isometry pushforwards from Eq. (
307
).
The last two steps identify
\Omega^{-1}(\kappa)
and, by definition of
\xi
, that
g_{\xi}^{NN}(n)=g
.

Together, these arguments that
\Omega
is indeed an isomorphism between the kernel spaces.

\Box

F.2
Proof of Theorem
11.2
– Equivalence of steerable spherical and
GM
-convolutions

Theorem
11.2
claims that
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions with a
G
-steerable kernel
K\in{K}^{G,B_{\mathbb{R}^{2}}(0,\pi)}_{\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\mkern-1.0mu,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}}
are equivalent to the spherical convolution with the
\operatorname{Stab}_{n}
-steerable kernel
\Omega(K)\in{K}^{\operatorname{Stab}_{n}}_{\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\mkern-1.0mu,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}}
.
The spherical convolution with a
\operatorname{Stab}_{n}
-steerable kernel
\kappa\in{K}^{\operatorname{Stab}_{n}}_{\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\mkern-1.0mu,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{out}}}}}
from
Cohen et al. 2018b
,
Cohen et al. 2019a
was hereby in Eq. (
466
) pointwise defined as

\displaystyle\big[\kappa\star_{\mkern-2.0muS^{2}}\!f\big]^{P}(p)\ =\int\limits_{S^{2}\backslash\mkern-2.0mu-p}\mkern-8.0mu\kappa\big(\phi_{p}^{-1}q)\,\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{\phi_{p}^{-1}}^{XQ}(q)\big)\,f^{Q}(q)\ dq\,,

(711)

where
P
,
Q
and
X
denote arbitrary gauges at
p
,
q
and
\phi_{p}^{-1}(q)
, respectively.
The isometry
\phi_{p}\in\mathcal{I}
is uniquely specified by demanding that
(\phi_{p})_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}\sigma^{N}(n)=\sigma^{P}(p)
.
Note that this implies in particular that

\displaystyle\phi_{p}(n)\ =\ p

(712)

and, using the definition of sections of
G\mkern-1.4muM
(frame fields) in terms of inverse gauges from Eq. (
191
), that

\displaystyle\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$n$}}^{N}\circ(\phi_{p})_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muG\mkern-2.0muM$}}}^{-1}\ =\ \psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{P}\,,

(713)

both of which we will use below.
With these preparations, we turn to the proof of Theorem
11.2
, i.e. the equivalence

\displaystyle\Omega(K)\star_{\mkern-2.0muS^{2}}\!f\ =\ K\star_{\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.64}{$G\mkern-1.4muM$}}f

(714)

of the convolutions.

Proof
:

Since
\Omega(\kappa)
is defined on
S^{2}\backslash\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{0.75}[1.0]{$-$}\mkern 1.0mun
, the transformed kernel
\Omega(\kappa)\circ\phi_{p}^{-1}
is defined on
S^{2}\backslash\mkern-2.0mu-p
.
Inserting
\Omega(\kappa)
in the pointwise definition of the spherical convolution in Eq. (
466
) leads therefore to

\displaystyle\big[\Omega(K)\star_{\mkern-2.0muS^{2}}\!f\big]^{P}(p)\

\displaystyle=\int\limits_{S^{2}\backslash\mkern-2.0mu-p}\mkern-8.0mu\big[\Omega(\kappa)\big]\big(\phi_{p}^{-1}q)\;\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{\phi_{p}^{-1}}^{XQ}(q)\big)\;f^{Q}(q)\ dq

(715)

\displaystyle=\int\limits_{S^{2}\backslash\mkern-2.0mu-p}\mkern-8.0muK\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$n$}}^{N}\log_{n}\phi_{p}^{-1}q)\;\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{n\leftarrow\phi_{p}^{-1}(q)}^{NX}\big)\;\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{\phi_{p}^{-1}}^{XQ}(q)\big)\;f^{Q}(q)\;\sqrt{\big|\eta_{\phi_{p}^{-1}(q)}^{\partial\mkern-2.0mu/\mkern-2.0mu\partial{v}}\big|}^{\,-1}dq\,,

where the second step follows by expanding
\Omega(K)
as defined in Eq. (
464
).
To simplify this expression, note that

\displaystyle\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$n$}}^{N}\,\log_{n}\,\phi_{p}^{-1}(q)\ =\ \psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$n$}}^{N}\,(\phi_{p})_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0muT\mkern-3.0muM$}}}^{-1}\,\log_{\phi_{p}(n)}(q)\ =\ \psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{P}\,\log_{p}(q)\,,

(716)

which follows from Eq. (
305
) in the first step and Eqs. (
712
) and (
713
) in the second step.
Note furthermore, that

\displaystyle\ \rho\big(g_{n\leftarrow\phi_{p}^{-1}(q)}^{NX}\big)\;\rho\big(g_{\phi_{p}^{-1}}^{XQ}(q)\big)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big[$}}}}}\psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$},n}}^{N}\,\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{A},n\leftarrow\phi_{p}^{-1}(q)}\,\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi_{p}^{-1}(q)$}}^{X}\big)^{-1}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big]$}}}}}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big[$}}}}}\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi_{p}^{-1}(q)$}}^{X}\,(\phi_{p})_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}$}}}^{-1}\,\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$q$}}^{Q}\big)^{-1}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big]$}}}}}\qquad

\displaystyle\big(\text{Eqs.~\eqref{eq:transporter_gauge_A} and~\eqref{cd:pushforward_A_coord} }\big)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$},n}}^{N}\,\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{A},n\leftarrow\phi_{p}^{-1}(q)}\,(\phi_{p})_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}$}}}^{-1}\,\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$q$}}^{Q}\big)^{-1}\qquad

\displaystyle\big(\text{canceled inverse gauges }\big)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$},n}}^{N}\,(\phi_{p})_{\overset{}{\mkern-2.0mu*\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.55}{$,\mkern-2.0mu\mathcal{A}$}}}^{-1}\,\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{A},\phi_{p}(n)\leftarrow q}\,\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$q$}}^{Q}\big)^{-1}\qquad

\displaystyle\big(\text{Eq.~\eqref{eq:transport_isom_commutation} }\big)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{P}\,\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{A},p\leftarrow q}\,\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$q$}}^{Q}\big)^{-1}\qquad

\displaystyle\big(\text{Eq.~\eqref{eq:phipn_gauges} }\big)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \rho\big(g_{p\leftarrow q}^{PQ}\big)\,.\qquad

\displaystyle\big(\text{Eq.~\eqref{eq:transporter_gauge_A} }\big)

Inserting these two identities, we obtain

\displaystyle\big[\Omega(K)\star_{\mkern-2.0muS^{2}}\!f\big]^{P}(p)\

\displaystyle=\int\limits_{S^{2}\backslash\mkern-2.0mu-p}\mkern-8.0muK\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{P}\log_{p}q)\;\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\big(g_{p\leftarrow q}^{PQ}\big)\;f^{Q}(q)\;\sqrt{\big|\eta_{\phi_{p}^{-1}(q)}^{\partial\mkern-2.0mu/\mkern-2.0mu\partial{v}}\big|}^{\,-1}dq\,,

To proceed, we express the integral in geodesic normal coordinates

{v}:S^{2}\backslash\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{0.75}[1.0]{$-$}\mkern 1.0mup\to B_{\mathbb{R}^{2}}(0,\pi),\ \ q\mapsto{v}(q):=\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{P}\log_{p}q

of
S^{2}\backslash\mkern-2.0mu-p
, which are centered at point
p
.
This cancels the Riemannian volume factor

\sqrt{\big|\eta_{\phi_{p}^{-1}(q)}^{\partial\mkern-2.0mu/\mkern-2.0mu\partial{v}}\big|}

(and thus justifies its appearance in the definition of
\Omega
),
such that the spherical convolution becomes

\displaystyle\big[\Omega(K)\star_{\mkern-2.0muS^{2}}\!f\big]^{P}(p)\ =

\displaystyle\int\limits_{B_{\mathbb{R}^{2}}\mkern-1.0mu(0,\pi)}\mkern-8.0muK({v})\;\rho_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{\;\!\!{in}}}}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big($}}}}}g_{p\leftarrow\exp_{p}(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{P})^{-1}{v}}^{PQ}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}\;f^{Q}\big(\exp_{p}(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{P})^{-1}{v}\big)\ d{v}\,,

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\int\limits_{B_{\mathbb{R}^{2}}\mkern-1.0mu(0,\pi)}\mkern-8.0muK({v})\;\big[\operatorname{Exp}^{*}_{p}\mkern-2.0muf\big]^{P}({v})\ d{v}\,,

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\ \big[K\star_{\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.64}{$G\mkern-1.4muM$}}\!f\big]^{P}(p)\,.

(717)

Since all arguments are independent form the chosen point
p
and the chosen gauges, this implies

\displaystyle\Omega(K)\star_{\mkern-2.0muS^{2}}\!f\ =\ K\star_{\mkern-1.0mu\scalebox{.64}{$G\mkern-1.4muM$}}f\,,

(718)

in a coordinate free setting, which proves the theorem.

\Box

Appendix G
Existence and smoothness of kernel field transforms

In Def.
7.6
we proposed
kernel field transforms

{T}_{\overset{}{\mkern 0.0mu\mathcal{K}}}
as smooth integral transforms

\displaystyle{T}_{\overset{}{\mkern 0.0mu\mathcal{K}}}:\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}})\to\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})

(719)

which are parameterized by some kernel field
\mathcal{K}
(Def.
7.2
) and are pointwise given by

\displaystyle\big[{T}_{\overset{}{\mkern 0.0mu\mathcal{K}}}(f)\big](p)\ \ :=\ \int\limits_{T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM}\!\!\mathcal{K}(v)\,\operatorname{Exp}^{*}_{p}\mkern-2.0muf(v)\ dv\ \ =\ \int\limits_{T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM}\!\!\mathcal{K}(v)\ \mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\overset{}{\scalebox{.75}{$\!\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}$},\scalebox{.7}{$p\!\leftarrow\!\exp_{p}\!v$}}}\,f(\exp_{p}\!v)\ dv\,.

(720)

Kernel field transforms include
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions from Def.
7.8
as a special cases for
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutional kernel fields.

Here we briefly discuss the well-definedness of kernel field transforms.
It is clear that the integrand of Eq. (
720
) lies for any
p\in M
and
v\in T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
in
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out},p}
.
What remains to be shown is the
existence
of the integral and the
smoothness
of the resulting feature field.
In the following we will first give some general remarks on how to approach these questions.
We will then prove Theorem
7.7
, i.e. the well-definedness of kernel field transforms for the specific case of fields of kernels which are compactly supported on a ball of fixed radius around the origin.

Existence:

The existence and smoothness of kernel field transforms requires a suitable choice of kernel field
\mathcal{K}
.
Similar to the case of conventional convolutions on
M=\mathbb{R}
, the requirements on
\mathcal{K}
in order for the kernel field transform to exist depend on the specific properties of the input feature field
f\in\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}})
.
166
166

166

See the discussion at
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convolution#Domain_of_definition
.

In general,
\mathcal{K}
needs to decay sufficiently rapidly in order to make the integrand in Eq. (
720
) integrable.

A special case of great practical importance is that of kernels
\mathcal{K}_{p}:T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM\to\Hom(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in},p},\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out},p})
which are at any
p\in M

compactly supported
.
In this case the integral is always guaranteed to exist.
To see this, note that (input) feature fields and kernel fields are defined to be smooth.
The smoothness of the metric further implies that the
Riemannian volume density, the exponential map and the parallel transport are smooth
[
73
]
.
In combination, the whole integrand in Eq. (
720
) is seen to be a smooth and thus continuous function from
TM
to
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}}
.
If
\mathcal{K}_{p}
is in addition compactly supported, the integrand becomes continuous and compactly supported on
T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
, which, by a generalization of the extreme value theorem, implies that its image is compact (and in a local trivialization
\mathbb{R}^{c}
of
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out},p}
bounded)
[
188
]
.
This guarantees the existence of the integral
[
68
,
213
]
.

Depending on the application, the requirement on the support of
\mathcal{K}
might be relaxed.
For instance, images on
M=\mathbb{R}^{d}
are usually compactly supported themselves, such that no additional properties of
\mathcal{K}
except for its smoothness are required.

Smoothness:

We turn to discuss the smoothness of kernel field transforms, that is, their property to map smooth input fields
f_{\textup{\;\!\!in}}\in\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}})
to smooth output fields
f_{\textup{\>\!\!out}}:={T}_{\overset{}{\mkern 0.0mu\mathcal{K}}}(f_{\textup{\;\!\!in}})\in\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}})
.
By definition, a map
f_{\textup{\>\!\!out}}:M\to\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}}

between manifolds

M
and
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}}
is said to be smooth if its coordinate representations are smooth.
In equations,
f_{\textup{\>\!\!out}}
is smooth if for any
p\in M
there exist smooth charts
(U,\phi)
about
p
in
M
and
(\widetilde{U},\widetilde{\phi})
about
f_{\textup{\>\!\!out}}(p)
in
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{out}}
with
f_{\textup{\>\!\!out}}(U)\subseteq\widetilde{U}
such that
\widetilde{\phi}\circ f_{\textup{\>\!\!out}}\circ\phi^{-1}:\phi(U)\to\widetilde{\phi}(\widetilde{U})
is smooth as a map between (subsets of) Euclidean spaces.
Given
(U,\phi)
, a convenient choice for
(\widetilde{U},\widetilde{\phi})
would be

\widetilde{\phi}:=\big(\phi\times\mathrm{id}\big)\circ\Psi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.65}{$\!\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{out}}}}\!:\ \pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6 }{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{out}}}}^{-1}(U)\mapsto\phi(U)\times\mathbb{R}^{c}\,\subseteq\,\mathbb{R}^{d}\times\mathbb{R}^{c}\,,

however, the following discussion is independent from this choice.
167
167

167

Note that
\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6 }{$\!\!\mathcal{A}$}_{\textup{out}}}}^{-1}(U)
is guaranteed to be trivializable given that
(\phi,U)
is a chart of
M
.
This is clear since the coordinate bases
\big[\frac{\partial}{\partial\phi_{\mu}}\big]_{\mu=1}^{d}
of
(\phi,U)
yields a trivialization of
\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!T\!M$}}}^{-1}(U)
(see Appendix
A
) and since the local trivializations of
FM
and
\mathcal{A}
were in Section
6.4
induced from those of
TM
.

A map between (subsets of) Euclidean spaces is smooth if it is smooth in each component of its image, here in each of the
d+c
dimensions of
\phi(U)\times\mathbb{R}^{c}
.
We are therefore interested in the smoothness of the maps

\displaystyle F_{i}:\phi(U)\to\mathbb{R},\ \ x\mapsto\Big[\,\widetilde{\phi}\circ f_{\textup{\>\!\!out}}\circ\phi^{-1}\Big]_{i}

(721)

for any
i=1,\dots,d+c
.
By writing out
f_{\textup{\>\!\!out}}
and expressing the integral over
T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
by an integral over
\mathbb{R}^{d}
as discussed in Appendix
A.4
, the
F_{i}
are seen to be of the form

\displaystyle F_{i}(x)=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}I_{i}({v},x)\,\ d{v}\,.

(722)

The coordinate expressions of the integrands
I_{i}
are hereby for any
i=1,\dots,d+c
given by

\displaystyle I_{i}\!:\mathbb{R}^{d}\mkern-2.0mu\times\mkern-2.0mu\phi(U)

\displaystyle\to\mathbb{R},

(723)

\displaystyle({v},x)

\displaystyle\mapsto\bigg[\widetilde{\phi}\circ\mathcal{K}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big($}}}}}\mkern-1.0mu\psi_{\scalebox{.65}{$T\!M\mkern-1.0mu,\mkern 2.0mu$}\scalebox{.75}{$\phi^{\mkern-1.0mu\shortminus 1}\mkern-1.0mu(x)$}}^{-1}\mkern-2.0mu({v})\mkern-1.0mu\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}\circ\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\scalebox{.8}{$\!\mathcal{A}_{\textup{in}}$},\scalebox{.83}{$\,\phi^{\mkern-1.0mu\shortminus 1}(x)\!\leftarrow\!\exp\circ\mkern 1.0mu\psi_{\scalebox{.7}{$T\!M\mkern-1.0mu,\mkern 1.0mu$}\scalebox{.9}{$\phi^{\mkern-1.0mu\shortminus 1}(x)$}}\!({v})$}}\mkern-1.0mu\circ f_{\textup{\;\!\!in}}\circ\exp\circ\,\psi_{\scalebox{.65}{$T\!M\mkern-1.0mu,$}\scalebox{.7}{$\phi^{\mkern-1.0mu\shortminus 1}(x)$}}^{-1}\mkern-2.0mu({v})\bigg]_{i}\,,

where we assumed, for convenience and without loss of generality, that

\psi_{\scalebox{.65}{$T\!M\mkern-1.0mu,\mkern 2.0mu$}\scalebox{.75}{$\phi^{\mkern-1.0mu\shortminus 1}\mkern-1.0mu(x)$}}

is an
isometric
gauge of
T_{\phi^{\mkern-1.0mu\shortminus 1}\mkern-1.0mu(x)}M
, such that the volume scaling factor
\sqrt{|\!\det\eta_{p}|}=1
drops out.
Note that the integrands
I_{i}
are composed of smooth maps and are therefore smooth as well.

From the previous discussion it is clear that the smoothness of
f_{\textup{\>\!\!out}}
holds if all
F_{i}
are smooth, i.e. infinitely often partially differentiable.
To prove the smoothness of the
F_{i}
, it is sufficient to show that the partial differentiations and the integration in Eq. (
722
) commute – which is not always the case.
If they do commute, partial derivatives of arbitrary orders
(n_{1},\dots,n_{d})\in\mathbb{N}^{d}
are given by

\displaystyle\Big[\partial_{x_{1}}^{n_{1}}\dots\partial_{x_{d}}^{n_{d}}\>F_{i}\Big](x)\ =\ \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}\Big[\partial_{x_{1}}^{n_{1}}\dots\partial_{x_{d}}^{n_{d}}\>I_{i}\Big]({v},x)\,\ d{v}

(724)

where
1) the partial derivatives
\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big[$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big[$}}}}}\partial_{x_{1}}^{n_{1}}\dots\partial_{x_{d}}^{n_{d}}\>I_{i}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big]$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{291272}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big]$}}}}}
of the integrand exist (due to the smoothness of
I_{i}
their existence is guaranteed) and
2) their integral exists.
Whether or not the differentiations commute with the integral can be investigated by making use of the following lemma
from
[
68
]
,
168
168

168

Similar versions of this lemma in English language can be found in
[
115
]
or at

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leibniz_integral_rule#Measure_theory_statement
.
In contrast to those versions, the version from
[
68
]
allows for
T
being any non-degenerate interval, including closed intervals, which saves us some additional steps below.

which is a consequence of the dominated convergence theorem.

Theorem G.1
(Differentiation lemma
[
68
]
).

Let
{V}
be a measure space, let
T\subset\mathbb{R}
be a non-degenerate interval and let
I:{V}\times T\to\mathbb{R}
be a map with the following properties:

(i)

For any fixed
t\in T
the map
{v}\mapsto I({v},t)
is Lebesgue integrable on
{V}

(ii)

For any fixed
{v}\in{V}
the map
t\mapsto I({v},t)
is differentiable in
T

(iii)

There exists a Lebesgue integrable function
{B}:{V}\to\mathbb{R}
such that

\big|\frac{\partial}{\partial t}I({v},t)\big|\leq{B}({v})

for any
({v},t)\in{V}\times T

Then the function
F:T\to\mathbb{R},\ t\mapsto\int_{V}I({v},t)\,d{v}
is differentiable
with derivative

\displaystyle\frac{\partial}{\partial t}F(t)\ =\ \int_{V}\frac{\partial}{\partial t}I({v},t)\;d{v}\,.

The applicability of this lemma (repeatedly for every single partial differentiation) depends on the properties of the integrand, which in turn depends on the specific properties of the kernel field
\mathcal{K}
and the input feature field
f_{\textup{\;\!\!in}}
.
For the case of a kernel field which is compactly supported on balls of fixed radius around the origin of each tangent space, the lemma applies.
Based on this, we give a proof of Theorem
7.7
in the remainder of this appendix.

G.1
Proof of Theorem
7.7
(Sufficiency of compact kernel support on tangent balls)

Denote by

B_{T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM}^{\mkern 1.5mu\textup{closed}}(0,R):=\big\{v\in T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM\,\big|\,\lVert v\rVert\leq R\big\}

the closed ball of radius
R>0
around the origin of
T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM
and by

B_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}^{\mkern 1.5mu\textup{closed}}(0,R):=\big\{v\in\mathbb{R}^{d}\,\big|\,\lVert v\rVert\leq R\big\}

the corresponding ball around the origin of
\mathbb{R}^{d}
.
Note that any isometric gauge satisfies
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}\big(B_{T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM}^{\mkern 1.5mu\textup{closed}}(0,R)\big)=B_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}^{\mkern 1.5mu\textup{closed}}(0,R)
.
Let
\widetilde{\mathcal{K}}
be a kernel field whose support falls within balls of the same radius
R
in each tangent space, i.e. which satisfies

\displaystyle\supp\!\big(\widetilde{\mathcal{K}}_{p}\big)\subseteq B_{T_{\mkern-1.5mup}\mkern-0.5muM}^{\mkern 1.5mu\textup{closed}}(0,R)\quad\forall p\in M

(725)

and thus, for any isometric gauge
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}
:

\displaystyle\supp\!\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big($}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big($}}}}}\widetilde{\mathcal{K}}_{p}\circ\big(\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$T\!M,$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}\big)^{-1}\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\displaystyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\textstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{360448}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{4.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Big)$}}}}}\subseteq B_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}^{\mkern 1.5mu\textup{closed}}(0,R)\quad\forall p\in M

(726)

According to Theorem
7.7
this property is sufficient to guarantee that the corresponding kernel field transform
{T}_{\mathcal{K}_{\mkern-1.0muR}}
is well defined.
A proof of this statement is given in the following.

Proof
:

As already stated in the beginning of this appendix, the existence of the integral is guaranteed given that the kernel supports are compact:
The compactness of the kernels carries over to the integrands of the kernel field transform.
Their smoothness further implies their continuity and integrals of compactly supported continuous functions always exists.

To prove the smoothness of the resulting output feature field
f_{\textup{\>\!\!out}}
, we proceed with the discussion earlier in this section.
We aim to apply the differentiation lemma
G.1
to swap partial derivatives
\frac{\partial}{\partial x_{\mu}}
for any
\mu=1,\dots,d
in Eq. (
724
) at any
x_{0}\in\phi(U)
with the integration over
\mathbb{R}^{d}
.
For this purpose, we introduce the auxiliary functions

\displaystyle I_{i,x_{0},\mu}:\mathbb{R}^{d}\times[-\varepsilon,\varepsilon]\to\mathbb{R},\ \ ({v},t)\mapsto I({v},x_{0}+t\epsilon_{\mu})

(727)

and

\displaystyle F_{i,x_{0},\mu}:[-\varepsilon,\varepsilon]\to\mathbb{R},\ \ t\mapsto F(x_{0}+t\epsilon_{\mu})=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}I_{i,x_{0},\mu}({v},t)\ d{v}\,,

(728)

where
\epsilon_{\mu}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}
is the unit vector in
\mu
-direction and

\varepsilon>0
is chosen such that
\big\{x_{0}+t\epsilon_{\mu}\,\big|\,t\in[-\varepsilon,\varepsilon]\big\}\subset\phi(U)
, which is always possible since
\phi(U)
is open.
Then
I_{i,x_{0},\mu}
is with the identifications
{V}=\mathbb{R}^{d}
and
T=[-\varepsilon,\varepsilon]
of the form required by lemma
G.1
.
It satisfies property
(i)
by the assumption that the kernel field transform exists as discussed earlier.
Property
(ii)
holds due to the smoothness of the full integrand in Eq. (
723
).
For property
(iii)
, observe that both
I_{i,x_{0},\mu}
and its derivative are smooth such that the absolute value
\big|\frac{\partial}{\partial t}I_{i,x_{0},\mu}\big|
is continuous.
Since it is in addition compactly supported on
B_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}^{\mkern 1.5mu\textup{closed}}(0,R)\times[-\varepsilon,\varepsilon]
, it is by (a generalization of) the extreme value theorem bounded by some number
b\geq 0
.
We therefore set
{B}({v})=b\cdot\mathbb{I}_{B_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}^{\mkern 1.5mu\textup{closed}}(0,R)\times[-\varepsilon,\varepsilon]}
where
\mathbb{I}
is the indicator function.
This choice satisfies

\big|\frac{\partial}{\partial t}I({v},t)\big|\leq{B}({v})

for any
({v},t)\in{V}\times T

and is integrable such that property
(iii)
is fulfilled as well.
We can therefore swap the order of differentiation and integration for arbitrary choices of
x_{0}
and
\mu
, which we use to pull arbitrary partial derivatives into the integral:

\displaystyle\bigg[\frac{\partial}{\partial x_{\mu}}F_{i}\bigg](x_{0})\,=\,\bigg[\frac{\partial}{\partial t}F_{i,x_{0},\mu}\bigg](0)\,=\,\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}\frac{\partial}{\partial t}I_{i,x_{0},\mu}({v},t)\Big|_{t=0}\ d{v}\,=\,\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}\frac{\partial}{\partial x_{\mu}}I_{i}({v},x)\Big|_{x=x_{0}}\ d{v}

(729)

Due to the smoothness and compact support of the integrand
I_{i}
, its partial derivatives
\frac{\partial}{\partial x_{\mu}}I
are smooth and compactly supported as well.
They do therefore satisfy properties
(i)
,
(ii)
and
(iii)
as well (with a potentially adapted bound
b
).
It is thus possible to repeat the partial differentiation of
F_{i}
infinitely often, which proves its smoothness.
Since the derivations were independent from the particular choices for the point
p\in M
, charts
(U,\phi)
and
(\widetilde{U},\widetilde{\phi})
, points
x_{0}\in\phi(U)
and indices
i
and
\mu
, this result proves the smoothness of the whole output feature field
f_{\textup{\>\!\!out}}={T}_{\overset{}{\mkern 0.0mu\mathcal{K}}}(f_{\textup{\;\!\!in}})
.

~\hfill\Box

Appendix H
Regular feature fields as scalar functions on
G
-structure

Real-valued functions
\digamma:G\mkern-1.4muM\to\mathbb{R}
on the
G
-structure are equivalent to regular feature fields
f:M\to\mathcal{A}_{\textup{reg}}
on the manifold, that is, that there is an isomorphism

\displaystyle C^{\infty}(G\mkern-1.4muM)\ \cong\ \Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{reg}})\,.

(730)

This appendix presents a proof of this claim for the case of finite structure groups
G
.
We start with the usual definition of (real) regular representations of finite structure groups, which act on the (free) vector spaces
\mathbb{R}^{|G|}
.
One defines a basis
\big\{\epsilon_{g}\in\mathbb{R}^{|G|}\,\big|\,g\in G\big\}
of
\mathbb{R}^{|G|}
, which is labeled by the group elements
g\in G
.
The (left) regular representation’s action on
\mathbb{R}^{|G|}
is then defined in terms of its action on these basis vectors, which is given by left translation.
Specifically, for any
h,g\in G
, the regular representation acts as follows:

\displaystyle\rho_{\textup{reg}}(h)\,\epsilon_{g}\ :=\ \epsilon_{hg}\,.

(731)

Note that the action on
coefficients
of a vector is inverse

\displaystyle\rho_{\textup{reg}}(h)\,\sum_{g\in G}{f}_{g}\,\epsilon_{g}\ =\ \sum_{g\in G}{f}_{g}\,\epsilon_{hg}\ =\ \sum_{{\widetilde{g}}\in G}{f}_{h^{-1}\widetilde{g}}\ \epsilon_{\widetilde{g}}\,,

(732)

which is useful to know, however, we won’t need this property in the following.
As the regular representation permutes the basis vectors of
\mathbb{R}^{|G|}
, it is a
permutation representation
.
Some visualizations for the cyclic group
G=\operatorname{C}_{4}
are found in Appendix B of
[
234
]
.
Regular feature fields are defined as smooth sections of the associated
G
-bundle

\displaystyle\mathcal{A}_{\textup{reg}}\ =\ \big(G\mkern-1.4muM\times\mathbb{R}^{|G|})/\!\sim_{\rho_{\textup{reg}}}\,.

(733)

The isomorphism
C^{\infty}(G\mkern-1.4muM)\cong\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{reg}})
substantiates our claim in Section
12
that the
Parallel Frame CNNs
by
Yang et al. 2020b
are specific
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions between regular feature fields.
It furthermore establishes the link between
group convolutions
(see Section
D.1
) and
regular
G\mkern-1.4muM
-convolutions
that was claimed in Section
9.4
and
[
234
]
.

With these preparations and remarks we are ready to formulate the theorem:

Theorem H.1
(Regular feature fields as scalar functions on
G
-structure).

Let
G\leq\operatorname{GL}(d)
be a finite structure group, let
G\mkern-1.4muM
be a
G
-structure over
M
and let
\mathcal{A}_{\textup{reg}}
be the bundle that is associated by the action of the regular representation
\rho_{\textup{reg}}
of
G
.
Regular feature fields are then identical to smooth, real-valued functions on the
G
-structure, that is, there is an isomorphism

\displaystyle\Lambda:C^{\infty}(G\mkern-1.4muM)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{reg}})\,.

(734)

This isomorphism is defined by

\displaystyle\big[\Lambda\digamma\big](p)\

\displaystyle=\ \Big[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\,,\,\sum\nolimits_{g}\digamma\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\lhd g\big)\,\epsilon_{g}\Big]\,,

(735)

where
[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\in G_{\mkern-1.3mup}\mkern-1.2muM
is an arbitrarily chosen representative frame at
p
.
Its inverse is given by

\displaystyle\big[\Lambda^{-1}f\big]\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\big)\

\displaystyle=\ \Big\langle\epsilon_{e}\,,\,\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}}f(p)\Big\rangle\,,

(736)

where we abbreviated
p=\pi_{\overset{}{\scalebox{.6}{ $\!G\!M$}}}(E)
and denote by
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}}
that (unique) gauge that corresponds to the frame
{[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}}
, i.e. which satisfies
\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}}\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\big)=e
.

Proof
:

To prove this statement, we need to show that
1) the isomorphism preserves the smoothness of the maps,
2) that the choice of representative frame
[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\in G_{\mkern-1.3mup}\mkern-1.2muM
in the definition of
\Lambda
is indeed arbitrary and
3) that
\Lambda^{-1}
is indeed a left and right inverse of
\Lambda
.

1) smoothness :

That the isomorphism preserves the smoothness of the equivalent field representations is clear since all involved morphisms (right action, gauge map, inner product) are smooth.

2) independence of the definition of
\Lambda
, Eq. (
735
), from the choice of representative frame
{[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\in G_{\mkern-1.3mup}\mkern-1.2muM}
:

Suppose that we used
any
other frame
[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\lhd h
for an arbitrary
h\in G
.
This arbitrary gauge transformation drops then out by making use of the equivalence relation
\sim_{\rho_{\textup{reg}}}
that is underlying the associated bundle construction, Eq. (
734
):

\displaystyle\big[\Lambda\digamma\big](p)\ =

\displaystyle\ \Big[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\lhd h\,,\,\sum\nolimits_{g}\digamma\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\lhd hg)\,\epsilon_{g}\Big]\qquad

\displaystyle\big(\text{def. of $\Lambda$, Eq.~\eqref{eq:regular_field_scalar_GM_iso_lambda} }\big)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \Big[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\,,\,\rho_{\textup{reg}}(h)\sum\nolimits_{g}\digamma\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\lhd hg)\,\epsilon_{g}\Big]\qquad

\displaystyle\big(\text{equivalence relation $\sim_{\rho_{\textup{reg}}}$, Eq.~\eqref{eq:equiv_relation_A} }\big)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \Big[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\,,\,\sum\nolimits_{g}\digamma\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\lhd hg)\,\epsilon_{hg}\Big]\qquad

\displaystyle\big(\text{$\rho_{\textup{reg}}$ action on basis $\epsilon_{g}$, Eq.~\eqref{eq:finite_regular_rep_action} }\big)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \Big[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\,,\,\sum\nolimits_{\widetilde{g}}\digamma\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\lhd\widetilde{g})\,\epsilon_{\widetilde{g}}\Big]\qquad

\displaystyle\big(\text{substitution $\widetilde{g}=hg$ }\big)

(737)

3)
\Lambda^{\!-1}
in Eq. (
736
) is a well defined inverse of
\Lambda
in Eq. (
735
) :

3 a)

\Lambda^{-1}\!\circ\!\Lambda=\mathrm{id}_{C^{\infty}(G\mkern-1.4muM)}
,
that is,
\Lambda^{-1}
is a left inverse of
\Lambda
:

For any
\digamma\in C^{\infty}(G\mkern-1.4muM)
and any
[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}
this is shown as follows:

\displaystyle\ \big[\Lambda^{-1}\!\circ\!\Lambda\,\digamma\big]\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\big)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \Big\langle\epsilon_{e}\,,\,\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}}[\Lambda\digamma](p)\Big\rangle

\displaystyle\big(\text{def. of $\Lambda^{-1}$, Eq.~\eqref{eq:regular_field_scalar_GM_iso_lambda_inv} }\big)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \Big\langle\epsilon_{e}\,,\,\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}}\big[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\,,\,\sum\nolimits_{g}\digamma\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\lhd g\big)\,\epsilon_{g}\big]\Big\rangle

\displaystyle\big(\text{def. of $\Lambda$, Eq.~\eqref{eq:regular_field_scalar_GM_iso_lambda} }\big)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \Big\langle\epsilon_{e}\,,\,\sum\nolimits_{g}\digamma\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\lhd g\big)\,\epsilon_{g}\Big\rangle

\displaystyle\big(\text{def. of $\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}$, Eq.~\eqref{eq:trivialization_A_p} }\big)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \sum\nolimits_{g}\digamma\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\lhd g\big)\,\langle\epsilon_{e},\epsilon_{g}\rangle

\displaystyle\big(\text{pull inner product into sum\,}\big)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \digamma\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\big)

\displaystyle\big(\text{Kronecker delta $\delta_{e,g}=\langle\epsilon_{e},\epsilon_{g}\rangle$}\big)

3 b)

\Lambda\!\circ\!\Lambda^{-1}=\mathrm{id}_{\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{reg}})}
,
that is,
\Lambda^{-1}
is a right inverse of
\Lambda
:

Let
f\in\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{reg}})
and
p\in M
, then:

\displaystyle\ \big[\Lambda\!\circ\!\Lambda^{-1}f\big](p)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \Big[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\,,\,\sum\nolimits_{g}\big[\Lambda^{-1}f]\big([e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\lhd g\big)\,\epsilon_{g}\Big]

\displaystyle\big(\text{def. of $\Lambda$, Eq.~\eqref{eq:regular_field_scalar_GM_iso_lambda} }\big)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \Big[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\,,\,\sum\nolimits_{g}\Big\langle\epsilon_{e}\,,\,\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\lhd g}f(p)\Big\rangle\,\epsilon_{g}\Big]

\displaystyle\big(\text{def. of $\Lambda^{-1}$, Eq.~\eqref{eq:regular_field_scalar_GM_iso_lambda_inv} }\big)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \Big[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\,,\,\sum\nolimits_{g}\Big\langle\epsilon_{e}\,,\,\rho_{\textup{reg}}(g)^{-1}\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}}f(p)\Big\rangle\,\epsilon_{g}\Big]

\displaystyle\big(\text{gauge transformation, Eq.~\eqref{eq:transition_fct_A}}\big)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \Big[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\,,\,\sum\nolimits_{g}\Big\langle\rho_{\textup{reg}}(g)\epsilon_{e}\,,\,\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}}f(p)\Big\rangle\,\epsilon_{g}\Big]

\displaystyle\big(\text{unitarity of $\rho_{\textup{reg}}$}\big)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \Big[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\,,\,\sum\nolimits_{g}\Big\langle\epsilon_{g}\,,\,\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}}f(p)\Big\rangle\,\epsilon_{g}\Big]

\displaystyle\big(\text{$\rho_{\textup{reg}}$ action on basis $\epsilon_{e}$, Eq.~\eqref{eq:finite_regular_rep_action}}\big)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ \Big[[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}\,,\,\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}^{[e_{i}]_{i=1}^{d}}f(p)\Big]

\displaystyle\big(\text{remove expansion in basis $\epsilon_{g}$}\big)

\displaystyle\ =

\displaystyle\ f(p)

\displaystyle\big(\text{def. of $\psi_{\scalebox{.6}{$\!\mathcal{A},$}\scalebox{.7}{$p$}}$, Eq.~\eqref{eq:trivialization_A_p}}\big)

(739)

This concludes our prove of the equivalence of
C^{\infty}(G\mkern-1.4muM)
and
\Gamma(\mathcal{A}_{\textup{reg}})
.
